Arjuna's meetings with Krsna, however, were never the same as before. Now there was a new dimension to their relationship, revealed in how they looked at and spoke to each other.

Arjuna continued to love and serve the Lord of Dvaraka as a confidential friend, always conscious that in Vraja, along with Radha's other friends, Arjuniya was serving Govinda as a paramour.

Krsna had not only given Arjuna insight into the ways of the milkmaids of Vrndavana, but had also disclosed to him his concurrent eternal identity as a cowherd girl.

In two forms, in two places, these two personalities eternally serve the Lord. But they unite, along with Lalita-devi, in the body of Ramananda Raya when Krsna appears as Caitanya Mahaprabhu.

During the Lord’s last days in Puri, Ramananda Raya and Svarupa Damodara recited suitable verses from Srimad-Bhagavatam and other books to assuage Lord Caitanya's feelings of separation from Krsna.

In the role of Sri Radha, Caitanya Mahaprabhu shows how to turn the embers of love for Sri Krsna into a great conflagration by pouring upon them the highly combustible fuel of service in separation.

Lord Caitanya would sit in the Gambhira, just as Radha does at the Yoga-pitha, waiting for Krsna. He would say, “My friends! Let Me disclose My heart, and you can judge Me correct or not.

“Love for Krsna, devoid of cheating propensities, is not possible within this material world. If there were such a love, there could be no separation, for in such separation one cannot live."

Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu would continue, “I feel ashamed to disclose the activities of My heart; nonetheless, finished with all formalities I will hide nothing from you. Please listen!”

Lord Caitanya said, na prema-gandho ’sti darapi me harau krandami saubhagya-bharam prakasitum / vamsi-vilasy-anana-lokanam vina bib-harmi yat prana-patangakan vrtha:

“My dear friends! I have not the slightest tinge of love for Krsna within My heart. When you see Me crying in separation, I am just making a false show of good fortune to mislead you.

“Indeed, not seeing the beautiful face of Krsna playing His flute, I continue to live My life like an insect, caring for My body without purpose. Know, therefore, that love for Krsna is far away from Me.”

Thus Arjuna’s and Arjuniya’s lessons on krsna-prema continue into eternity, revealing ever new facets of the philosophers’ stone of spontaneous loving devotion extracted from the rich soil of Vraja.

Krsna had bound Arjuna by a vow never to disclose his entrance into the realm of gopi-bhava, but somehow Uddhava came to know of Arjuna’s perfection and the esoteric steps that lead to that paragon.

Thus when Uddhava, the faithful follower of the Vraja-vasis, retired to the abode of Nara-Narayana, he took inspiration from his friend Arjuna and attained Vraja and the intimate pastimes of Govinda.

Dear devotees! Sometimes we hear that pure love for Krsna cannot be found in this world, but then we see the example of devotees like Arjuna and hear the teachings of acaryas like Srila Prabhupada.

These great souls encourage us to relentlessly strive for krsna-prema and to remain determined in our efforts, bolstered by the empowered, unfailing blessings of guru, Gauranga, and the Vaisnavas.

We may feel so far from that goal when we see even great devotees struggling to attain it. But by hearing about it and crying for it, one day — like a sudden downpour — love for Krsna will descend upon us.

And once we become fortunate enough to obtain just one drop of love for Krsna, we will feel like we have fallen into a bottomless ocean of happiness that can drown not just this world, but the entire universe.

**\* \* \* \***

When we speak of Radha-kunda in Bhauma Vrndavana, we mean not only of the lake itself but also Syama- kunda and the surrounding town of Radha-kunda with its other kundas, temples, and holy places.

In New Vraja-dhama, the two ponds in the temple courtyard, the temple itself, the terraces surrounding it, and the area encompassing the inner petals of the Yoga-pitha are together called Radha-kunda.

Behind Nima-grama devotees meditate upon the Yoga-pitha and offer their obeisances before proceeding west towards Ramesvara Mahadeva who guards this rear entrance to Radha-kunda.

Every form of Lord Siva present in New Vraja-dhama can be worshipped through Gopisvara Mahadeva, who sometimes lives in his own temple, and sometimes with Yogamaya in Vrnda’s grove.

I offered my respects to the dhama and to Ramesvara Mahadeva, and paused for a moment to pray for admission to Radha-kunda — Radha’s and Krsna’s intimate residence and exclusive playground.

Anyone who takes the trouble to visit New Vraja-dhama may enter the temple, but it takes more than the strain of travel or an entrance fee to access Radha-kunda as the sadhakas do.

Resident devotees have easy physical access to Radha-Syamasundara’s temple, but such ease is no substitute for the pure Vaisnava conduct and Krsna consciousness essential to see Radha-kunda in truth.

True worshippers of Radha and Krsna are sober devotees who can tolerate the urge to speak, the mind’s demands, the actions of anger, and the urges of the tongue, belly, and genitals.

Such sincere souls guard their devotion by strictly avoiding gluttony, greed, over ambition, frivolity, ceremonialism, whimsy, bad company, and pride, austerities rarely performed in the dark Age of Kali.

Serious Vaisnavas display genuine enthusiasm, act with confidence, and patiently await the result. They are fixed in the regulative principles and strictly follow the example set by previous acaryas.

No matter how many good qualities we may engender, however, without developing loving friendships with devotees, we will stay far from the favour of the divine couple and Their entourage.

Sincere Vaisnavas thus cultivate love for one another by offering gifts, accepting gifts, revealing their minds in confidence, enquiring confidentially, and accepting and offering prasada.

These kind-hearted souls respect all devotees — be they neophyte, practising, or advanced in devotional service — albeit in ways commensurate with each devotee’s level of spiritual development.

Progressive devotees mentally honour beginners who chant the holy name of Lord Krsna, but offer humble obeisances to Vaisnavas who have undergone initiation and who worship the Deity.

Moreover, serious devotees seek out and faithfully serve pure devotees who are advanced in undeviated devotional service and whose pure-hearted natures are wholly devoid of the tendency to criticise others.

Vaisnavas take great care to avoid seeing such advanced devotees from a materialistic point of view, never identifying them with their bodies, be those bodies low-born, deformed, diseased, or infirm.

Situated in their original Krsna conscious position, pure devotees no longer identify with their bodies, which, like the Ganges, cannot be polluted despite seeming defects, having been spiritualised by service.

Such ideal Vaisnava character is present only in devotees who are sheltered by Lord Krsna’s divine name, the priceless gift Caitanya Mahaprabhu gave to the world through Srila Prabhupada’s mercy.

The tongue of one afflicted by the jaundice of ignorance cannot taste anything transcendentally sweet, but by carefully chanting these names every day, their natural sweet taste returns.

Attentive chanting destroys at the root the lust afflicting the heart, and the chanter comes to relish the transcendent sweetness of Lord Krsna’s name, character, and pastimes.

The essence of all advice, therefore, is to utilise all our time in nicely chanting Krsna’s divine names and in remembering His transcendental form, qualities, and eternal pastimes.

In this way, mature devotees reside in New Vraja-dhama and serve under the guidance of their superiors. Eventually, when advanced to the perfectional stage, they may follow in the wake of the Vraja-vasis.

Briefly, I have outlined the path by which we can engage our minds and senses in Krsna consciousness and qualify ourselves to enter the topmost spiritual sphere — Radha-kunda.

Of all the holy sites we are visiting in the holy dhama, Radha-kunda stands supreme, for there only does the elixir of transcendental love churned by Radha’s and Krsna’s amorous pastimes overflow.

It is said that Mathura is spiritually superior to Vaikuntha, for there Krsna took birth. And superior to Mathura is the forest of Vrndavana because Krsna’s rasa-lila pastimes took place in those sacred groves.

Sastra further says that Govardhana Hill is superior to the forest of Vrndavana because Krsna raised the Hill with His own divine hand and had loving pastimes there with His cows, friends, and gopis.

But above Govardhana Hill, above Vrndavana forest and Mathura, above Vaikuntha or any other holy realm, superexcellent Radha- kunda, resting at the foot of Giriraja, stands supreme.

Where, then, is that intelligent person, who after visiting or residing in the home of Lord Krsna, is unwilling to serve celestial Radha- kunda and its heart and soul, Radha and Syama?

Practising devotees who have firm faith in the transcendental reality of Krsna’s pastimes at Radha-kunda are superior to fruitive workers, spiritual philosophers, and even liberated souls.

Practising and perfected devotees alike, knowing the residents of Vraja to be more confidential than the Lord’s other devotees, always try to stay absorbed in thoughts of the Vraja-vasis’ services.

And Vaisnavas who are attracted by the gopis’ love for the Lord, who know the gopis to be exalted above all other devotees due to their total dependence upon Krsna, worship the foremost gopi, Sri Radha.

Radha’s lake is as dear to Krsna as She is; hence, such fortunate Vaisnavas reside on the banks, groves, and gardens of Radha-kunda, which steadily become the objects of their constant meditation.

Either with a purified mind or in a spiritual body surcharged with ecstatic devotional love, devotees render service to Radha and Krsna as They perform Their eternal eightfold daily pastimes.

Now that Radha-kunda and the divine couple have graciously appeared in New Vraja-dhama, what sincere devotee will neglect to serve Them according to his or her level of spiritual advancement?

Indeed, sastra tells us that if we take advantage of the opportunity to undertake devotional service on the banks of Radha-kunda, we become the most fortunate souls in the universe.

Great devotees like Narada rarely attain the transcendental vision of Radha-kunda. How difficult it must be, then, for ordinary devotees practising regulated devotion to attain.

But by bathing in Radha-kunda, either in body or mind, greatly fortunate devotees will gradually awaken within their hearts a love similar to that of the maidservants of Radha.

But even if we cannot bathe in Radha-kunda every day, our daily absorption in the morning and evening program in Radha-Syama’s temple is like submerging ourselves in that lake of nectar.

A bath either by pure sadhana on the banks of Radha-kunda or by dipping into her waters assures success for devotees interested in advancing their devotion in the wake of the gopis or manjaris.

Bhaktivinoda Thakura says that Vaisnavas eager to return back to Godhead should live at Radha-kunda, take shelter of the manjaris, and under their guidance engage in the service of Sri Radha.

Having abandoned all material conceptions and taken shelter of Srimati Radharani and Her friends, devotees thus constantly engaged in this lifetime, after giving up the body, return to Godhead.

In Goloka Vrndavana, with the perfected spiritual bodies of gopis, such devotees will serve Sri Radha in the same way as they contemplated during this lifetime on the banks of Radha-kunda.

O devotees who seek after the essence of life! Reside on the banks of Radha-kunda, remain always absorbed in Syama’s loving service, bathe there regularly, and take shelter of Radha and the gopis.

**\* \* \* \***

Radha-kunda is the pleasure garden of Radha and Krsna in Goloka, manifest here on earth during the time of Krsna's descent, along with other holy places like Govardhana Hill and Manasa-ganga.

Radha-kunda’s appearance on earth is linked to Krsna’s slaying the bull-demon Arista, which took place on the seventh night of the waning moon in the month of Karttika.

Once, Uddhava informed Paurnamasi that Kamsa had asked two of his servants, Arista and Kesi, to spy on the young boy who was killing the demons Kamsa had been regularly sending to Vrndavana.

As Kesi was spying on Krsna, the demon spotted Sri Radha. Upon returning to Mathura, Kesi described Radha’s beauty in great detail to King Kamsa, who at once decided to invade Gokula and abduct Her.

Aristasura advised Kamsa to send his intimate friend Sarikhacuda to kidnap Srimati Radharani, but like the other demons, that foolish Yaksa was quickly dispatched to the abode of Yamaraja.

Lusty Kamsa now placed his hopes in the giant bull Aristasura, who true to his name (calamity) brought misfortune wherever he went. He was feared by humans and demigods alike.

On one occasion, fearsome Aristasura frightened Lord Siva merely by playfully shaking his head. Afraid for the welfare of his own bull Nandi, Siva concealed his mount in a cave of Mandara Mountain.

Wherever the terrible Arista went, the three worlds hid in fear. When Aristasura stood up, all creatures fell down, and when he moved about, the winds refused to blow in the sky.It was late evening, midway through the period of dusk, when Arista appeared on the outskirts of Nandagrama, bellowing harshly and making the earth tremble as he struck the ground with his hooves.

Not far away, Krsna was trying to put out the flames of Visakha’s anger, which threatened a well-planned rasa dance with the gopis, who by then had become intimidated by Visakha’s unrelenting huff.

But the loud roar of Arista so frightened Visakha-devi that she forgot her anger and hid behind Krsna, along with the other gopis, who made Krsna venture out to investigate the noise.

Krsna arrived in the pastures outside Nandagrama to find an enormous black bull with a mountainous hump. The whirling of its long raised tail was stirring the clouds overhead into a storm.

That ugly beast was tearing up embankments with its horns, pulling out fences, and gouging deep furrows in the earth, while every now and then passing stool and urine here and there.

Vraja’s cows, calves, and bulls ran into their barns in fear, and the gopas and gopis were trembling at the mere sight of the demon, whose thunderous roar caused pregnant cows and women to miscarriage.

The brave gopas who had tried to face the demon ran away as soon as they saw Arista charging at them, his thunderbolt horns lowered, his nostrils shooting fire, his hooves cracking the earth.

In response to the chaos disturbing His village, Krsna called out to the Vraja-vasis and cows, “Don’t be afraid!” After comforting them, He turned to the sinful creature and cried:

“You fool! Wicked rascal! What do you think you’re doing frightening the cowherd community and their animals when I am here just to punish corrupt, sinful miscreants like you!”

Killing a cow or a bull is a most heinous act, but Krsna stood His ground and tightened the sash around His waist. He was prepared to kill any demon whose death would be only a boon to the universe.

Krsna challenged the demon by loudly slapping His arms with His palms, and then showed further contempt for His opponent by casually slinging an arm over Subala’s shoulder.

This provoked Arista, who pawed the ground and glared menacingly with his horns pointed dead ahead, his tail upright. He then rushed at full speed towards Krsna like a thunderbolt hurled by Indra.

Krsna seized Arista by the horns, stopping his charge, pushed him back eighteen steps, and made the demon fall back on his haunches, just as the great Kuvalayapida would a rival elephant.

Arista rose to his feet, breathing hard and sweating. With mindless rage the demon again charged. This time Krsna caught Him by the horns and then knocked him to the ground with a ferocious kick.

Krsna began to beat Arista like a piece of wet cloth. He yanked out the bull’s left horn and struck him with it again and again until the demon, unable to move, vomited blood and passed stool.

Krsna would not kill Aristasura because the demon had the form of a bull; instead, unseen by the Vraja-vasis, Yamaraja appeared and killed the demon, who was at once freed from his sinful condition.

Krsna then playfully disposed of Arista by tossing his lifeless body out of Vrndavana as if it were a toy ball, freeing the universe from a great calamity and making Nandagrama auspicious and happy again.

**\* \* \* \***

After Krsna had disposed of Arista, in great triumph He and Balarama returned to Nandagrama where the citizens greeted the brothers with pageantry and joyous expressions of love.

But because the Vraja-vasis were intent on celebrating Krsna's most recent victory until late into the night, He was unable to rejoin the gopis for their scheduled nocturnal rasa dance festival.

On the following evening, however, Krsna met the gopis at the far end of Govardhana Hill in a clearing where Arista and Krsna had fought before their final showdown closer to Nandisvara.

Although the gopis greeted their beloved with showers of flowers and jubilant cheers, at Krsna’s request that they resume their activities of the previous evening, Radha recoiled, declaring emphatically, “No!"

Krsna thought Radha was just being coy, as She is prone to be, but when He reached out to touch Her, She responded, not playfully, but with belligerence, “O sinful bull-killer! Do not touch Me!”

“Foolish woman!” Krsna exclaimed. “I did not kill a bull, but a terrible demon in the guise of a bull. How can You equate the heroic act of vanquishing a demon with the sinful deed of killing a bull?”

Thinking He had diffused Radha’s argument, Krsna again reached for Her arm. But She slapped His hand away and pierced Him with a glance that made it clear He would not win so easily this time.

“What You say may be true,” She countered, “but even though Arista was a demon, he was in the body of a bull. So You will have to atone for Your sins, just as Indra did after killing the brahmana Vrtrasura.”

Krsna restlessly tapped the ground with His right foot. He didn’t expect this sort of gratitude for saving the gopis, but He knew better than to press His luck when Radha was like this. So He asked: “O Radha! Please tell Me. What should I do to atone for this act?” Visibly pleased with His new attitude, She said, “In order to purify Yourself, You must bathe in every last holy place in the three worlds.”

"That’s outrageous!” thought Krsna. But with a smile He replied, “Why should I spend My time wandering the universe when I can call all the holy places and take My bath in them here?”

At this Radha glanced at Her friends with amusement. They were all staring sceptically at Krsna as He raised His right forefinger like a wizard about to conjure an object from the air. “Just watch!” He said.

Krsna struck His heel into the ground to make a knee-deep depression and ordered, “Come here!” One by one, streams of water bubbled out of the ground, filling up the hole and forming a pond.

These springs were the holy waters of the universe, including even the Bhogavati River from the lower Patala region. Krsna, looking pleased with Himself, said, “Friends! Behold all the holy waters.”

But as far as the gopis could tell, they saw only ordinary trickles, so they laughed with disdain. Chuckling, Radhika challenged, “If these waters are so holy then where are their presiding deities?”

Krsna shook His head imperiously, as if to say, “Now I will show you!” then clapped His hands and commanded, “Appear!” Suddenly the area was crowded with divine beings, palms joined reverentially.

These deities with golden crowns and divine ornaments introduced themselves one by one, bowing low before Radha. One said, “I am the salt ocean.” Another said, “I am the ocean of milk.”

All the sacred waters were there, including the rivers Sona, Sindhu, Tamraparni, Sarasvati, Godavari, Yamuna, and Reva, the confluence of rivers at Prayaga, and the holy lake of Puskara.

The gopis were amazed to see the deities of famous holy places they had only heard about, and others completely unknown to them, introduce themselves and say, “Here are my waters!”

After smashing the doubts of Radha and Her friends, Krsna observed the proper rituals and bathed in His lake, as the deities of the holy places stood by chanting sacred hymns such as the purusa-sukta.

Purified by the sacred hath, Krsna came out of the water and dressed Himself in fresh clothes. Donning a garland of lotuses, He came before the gopis in a painfully arrogant mood and said:

“I have created a sacred lake containing all the holy waters. I have bathed there and become free from any taint of sin. Have any of you performed such a pious deed or taken such a holy dip!”’

Such bold-faced provocation could not go unanswered. Radha addressed Her friends in a voice laced with sarcasm, carefully pronouncing each syllable so that Hari would hear every word clearly.

“Friends, I must have an even more beautiful lake than this one. Please arrange to construct it at once!” Pointing to where Arista’s hooves had left a hole in the ground, She said, “Over there!”

The gopis at once began digging the soft earth with their hands, and when that proved too slow, they used their bangles instead. Within an hour they had excavated a sizeable, extremely attractive kunda.

Astonished by the charm of the lake the gopis had created, Krsna thought to tease His beloved and so He suggested, “O lotus-eyed girl! You may, if You like, fill Your kunda with water from My lake."

But Radha would have none of that, and so She protested. Holding up both hands in disdain, She said, “Impossible! By bathing in that lake You have polluted its water with the dreadful sin of killing a bull.

“Instead, My friends and I will fill My lake with water from Manasa- ganga. Thus, for having constructed such a sacred place of pilgrimage, My fame will surely spread throughout the universe.”

The gopis’ leaders, like Lalita, quickly mobilised the girls. Within a short time, using milk pots to carry water from Manasa-ganga, they had filled the pool and were proudly calling it Radha-kunda.

Suddenly, Krsna made a mysterious gesture. A divine personality rose from Syama’s lake, startling the gopis. This divine being, an envoy of all the sanctified places, approached Radha with tears in his eyes.

Palms joined in entreaty, the deity bowed before Vrsabhanu-nandini in praise: “O Goddess! Neither Brahma, the knower of all scriptures, nor Siva, nor Laksmi can fully conceive of Your glories.

“Only the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna, the best of all men, can understand them. He therefore renders You menial service, like wiping drops of perspiration from Your limbs when You suffer fatigue.

“Lord Krsna paints Your feet with red lacquer and then adorns them with anklets, rejoicing in the supreme good fortune of being the servant of Your delicate pink lotus feet.

“The Supreme Lord has ordered us, the holy places, to enter into this beautiful lake He created with one kick of His heel. But we have a desire that only Your merciful glance can fulfil.”

Pleased by these humble words, Radha smiled slightly and looked for cues, first from Krsna and then from Her friends. Seeing them favourably inclined, She asked, “Tell Me, then, what is your desire?”

With fervent emotion the heavenly being said, “We request that You kindly make our lives successful by granting us permission to enter and reside in Your beautiful lake. That is our desire.”

Sri Radha glanced at Her beloved from the corners of Her eyes and replied with a smile, “Yes, please come!” These words immersed Her friends, and indeed all creatures, in an ocean of happiness.

Blessed by Sri Radha, the holy waters forcibly broke through the western bank of Krsna’s lake with a crash, creating a canal through which the waters of Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda mixed.

The two lakes were as splendid as the eyes of a peacock. As the divine couple looked on, lotuses of all colours appeared on the surface of Their kundas, and groves of every description sprang up on their banks.

Krsna turned to Radha and declared, “Most beloved! Because Your kunda is as dear to Me as You are, I will bathe in it daily. May Radha- kunda garner more fame in this world than My own Syama-kunda.”

Now it was Radha’s turn. She completely abandoned Her contrary mood and openly revealed Her true feelings: “O Syama! You may kill a hundred bull-demons, but every day I will bathe in Your kunda.

“From now on, any person who has intense devotion for Your lake, Syama-kunda, or who bathes there or lives on its banks, will certainly become very dear to Me and thus come to Me.”

After Radha and Krsna had pronounced Their vows and given Their blessings, the entire area surrounding the two lakes echoed with the voices of cheering gopis and the sounds of rejoicing forest animals.

Giriraja had also been watching these events from a hiding place nearby, and he tightly embraced the two sacred lakes, thrilled that he would be witness to the daily pastimes of the divine couple.

By the time the excavation and filling of Radha-kunda was complete and the obstacles to Krsna’s long-awaited plan for a rasa dance were removed, the hour of midnight had arrived.

But it was well worth the wait! Aristasura’s arrival in Vraja and Krsna’s fierce battle with the bull-demon turned out to be mere preludes to the appearance of the universe’s most hallowed place.

In this unfortunate age of quarrel and hypocrisy we are condemned to lives of misery and strife, but these two holy lakes are oases of divine opportunity that promise bliss no sane woman or man would deny.

Persons who devotedly serve Syama-kunda, which is millions of times greater than the Ganges, and which was born from the touch of Krsna’s lotus foot, become dearer to Syama than even Lord Siva.

And in the same way, persons who worship the cintamani jewel known as Radha-kunda attain the full mercy of Lord Krsna and become the most dear and most glorious of Syama’s devotees.

As Krsna foretold, Radha-kunda became more famous than His own Syama-kunda; indeed the whole area is known by names connected with Radha, names such as Radha-kunda, Sri-kunda, and Srivana.

In fact, Radha’s lake has become so well known that pilgrims who plan to visit and bathe in both lakes hardly mention the name of Syama-kunda. They simply say, “We are going to Radha-kunda.”

Everyone understands that wherever Radharani goes, Krsna is always nearby. In a similar way, everyone understands that any mention of Radha-kunda automatically includes Syama-kunda.

In the month of Karttika, after midnight on the eighth day of the dark moon (Krsnastami), also known as Bahulastami, Krsna enjoyed a splendid rasa dance on the banks of these two lakes.

And this night was special, because the normal features of the rasa dance — successive dancing, strolling, and bathing—also unveiled the transcendental features of Radha-kunda and the area surrounding it.

In other words, from that night onwards, until Krsna left for Dvaraka, the Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda of the spiritual world became visible in their full opulence and sweetness on earth.

After Krsna left Vraja the lakes assumed their original appearance as two simple ponds until Vajra restored some of their glory. The lakes then became known as Kancana-kunda and Vajra-kunda respectively.

Vajra named the village in the area Arit-grama. Some authorities say that Vajra-kunda was named after Vajra, others that it was named after the thunderbolt (vajra) Indra threw to help excavate the lake.

Like other sacred places in Vraja, the death of Pariksit Maharaja brought gradual decline to this area. The lakes became covered by natural overgrowth and lost to the vision of all but self-realised souls.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu Himself rediscovered Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda, which by that time had deteriorated into two unrecognisable puddles in a common agricultural field.

And finally, by Lord Caitanya’s order, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami again excavated and then further expanded Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda into the forms they take today in sacred Bhauma Vrndavana.

Scriptures say that faithful, single-minded devotees who bathe in Radha-kunda on Bahulastami are blessed with prema-bhakti like that of the friends or maidservants of Srimati Radharani.

In addition to the perception exclusive to great transcendentalists, they will also he granted a vision not only of the entirety of Vraja-mandala but of the whole cosmic creation as well.

Generally pilgrims are forbidden to bathe at holy places in the dead of night, but Radha-kunda is the only place on earth at which people are blessed to take the midnight sacred bath called ardha-ratri-snana.

Before bathing in Radha-kunda, whether it be day or night, devotees first offer prayers such as this from Varaha Purana,

*sarva-papa-haras tirtham namaste hari-muktidah*  
*namah kaivalya-nathaya radha-krsna-bhidhayine*

**“O Sri Radha-kunda! O Sri Krsna-kunda! You destroy all sins within the heart and then fill it with one-pointed love. From the very core of my being I offer my humble obeisances to you again and again."**

**\* \* \* \***

In glorifying Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda, great devotees have in their ecstasy described, in various ways and in metaphorical terms, the cause of these two divine lakes’ appearance on earth.

At one time the ocean of Radha’s and Krsna’s celestial splendour overflowed its shores. Two drops of that nectar mercifully fell to earth so that conditioned souls could directly taste Their sweetness.

These two drops assumed the forms of two beautiful lakes, which are the roots from which the creeper of pure devotional service sprouts and the treasure trove of amorous love’s jewels eternally expands.

It is also said that Syama-kunda and Radha-kunda are the seeds from which bud the jewel-vines of Radha’s and Krsna’s pastimes, which then spread throughout the luxuriant garden known as Vrndavana.

Since the natural course of those divine pastimes dictates that the divine couple must part after meeting, They assumed the forms of two lakes in order to constantly relish the union of their splashing waves.

It is also said that once, at the sight of Syama, Radha melted and assumed the liquid form of Her lake. When Syama saw His beloved’s condition He also melted to become the liquid form of His own lake.

These two lakes, then, bear not only the names of the divine couple hut also Their qualities and love, and so the fortunate souls who bathe in them know they are bathing in the liquid forms of divine love.

Because Radha and Krsna both have faith that the other is present in His or Her lake, when Radha sees Syama-kunda, She directly sees Him, and when Syama sees Radha-kunda, He directly sees Her.

The wise request pilgrims to approach these two lakes as directly the forms of the divine couple. Bathers should therefore offer the same respect they would offer to Deities of Radha and Krsna.

Always remember that Radha-kunda is as dear to Krsna as is the glowing tiara amongst the young girls of Gokula, and Syama-kunda is as dear to Radha as is the unbridled young prince of Vraja.

Just as Govardhana Hill, though eternal, seems to appear at one time in Goloka to enhance the human-like pastimes of Radha and Krsna, eternal Syama-kunda and Radha-kunda seem to appear there as well.

One day, in the spiritual realm of Goloka Vrndavana, Radha and Krsna, attended by gopis, were seated together in a flowering grove, fully absorbed in the wonder of each other’s beauty and qualities.

By the divine couple’s mutual attraction, Their love for each other became like a blazing inferno in which the flames on one side of the fire stoked the flames on the other, and vice versa.

This time, however, the mood of the supreme beloved, Radha, so dominated Krsna that His empathy for Her gradually intensified until He fully identified with Her, becoming completely lost to Himself.

Just as a brown chameleon assumes the green colour of the leaf it sits upon, blackish Krsna assumed Srimati Radharani’s golden complexion and delicate bodily features in contact with Her.

Krsna — who was now fully convinced He was Radha — became so distressed at not being able to see the son of Maharaja Nanda that the tears from His intense weeping formed a small pond nearby.

Finally, unable to contain Himself, Krsna rose to His feet, called out His own name again and again, and ran into the forest in search of Himself, leaving Radha and Her girlfriends behind.

Krsna’s intense emotional outburst affected Radha in kind. Having seen a heartbroken Radha run off into the forest, the original Radha assumed Krsna's inner identity and outward bodily features.

In the mood of Krsna, She thought, “My beloved has left Me!” She called out the name Radha again and again and cried so profusely that Her tears formed a second pond next to the first.

The wonderstruck and desolate gopis, try as they might, could not pacify Radha as She madly flailed Her arms and called out in a voice like a peacock, “O Radha! Where are You? Where are You?”

Finally some gopis ventured out in search of Krsna. After some time they found Him wandering about aimlessly, questioning forest animals like deer and parrots as to the whereabouts of Himself.

With great difficulty the gopis managed to pacify Krsna and explain to Him what had happened; they told Him how His departure had cast Radharani into the flames of intense suffering.

Krsna then went along with the gopis to where Radha was still writhing about in separation from Herself. Krsna pacified Her by His presence and told Her of Their present predicament.

Krsna felt guilty for having been the source of suffering for Radha. He said, “O My queen! I have caused You great sorrow by running away. I am Your menial servant who deserves to be punished.

“But My foolish acts gave Me a taste of the unbearable poison of separation as well. If You agree, We can both drink the remedy of loving pastimes by resuming Our original forms.”

Radha bent Her neck slightly and then shyly stared at the ground, giving Her consent to Krsna’s suggestion. He cheerfully responded, “Just look at the two lakes formed by the flood of Our tears!”

Then Krsna took Radha’s hand and led Her to the water’s edge. He dipped into the lake formed by His own tears, and then, to the sound of the gopis’ applause, emerged in His original form of Syamasundara.

Srimati Radharani, who still looked like Krsna, then bathed in the lake created by Her tears and at once resumed Her original gopi form, dazzling Krsna with Her radiant beauty.

Krsna proclaimed, “In the future the residents of Vrndavana will call the magical lake made from Your tears Radha-kunda, and the lake next to it made from Mine, Syama-kunda.”

With Radha and Syama back in Their original forms and identities, Their loving exchanges as supreme lover and beloved could resume with even greater ecstasy on the banks of Their newly formed lakes.

And after this appearance pastime in Goloka, Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda resumed their eternal forms as the divine couple’s charming, confidential, midday transcendental playground.

These two lakes overflow with divine mellows. The lakes of Radha’s eight most important friends surround Radha-kunda, and the lakes of eight select friends of Krsna, like Subala, surround Syama-kunda.

Forest maidens expert in constructing and decorating things from flowers maintain these sixteen delectable groves—which correspond to the same gopis and gopas — surrounding the two main lakes.

Radha-kunda is square-shaped, Syama-kunda octagonal. Spanning the confluence between them is a beautiful suspension bridge that serves as the Yoga-pitha for the entire Radha-kunda area.

In these lakes and groves Radha and Krsna dance, joke, ride on swings, play hide-and-seek, Holi, or dice, throw ball, enjoy water sports, hear the poetry of parrots, and eat fruit from the trees.

On all sides of the lakes are bathing ghatas fashioned from jewels, beyond which lie luxuriant gardens replete with all sorts of furnishings like seats, swings, couches, and elegant places for dining.

Devotees who hear about or recall descriptions of these lakes as they think about Radha’s and Krsna’s midday pastimes know that words cannot duplicate their glory. They must be realised to be truly valued.

Nonetheless, let us now hear the marvels of these lakes, the crown jewels of Vraja, as great souls have described them and meditated upon them — the divine couple’s pleasure playground.

**\* \* \* \***

Radha-kunda is completely surrounded by ornate jewelled steps leading into its water. The designated bathing areas at its sides and corners feature platforms and pavilions made of gold.

Laden with flowers and evenly spaced around the banks of the lake stand trees in pairs. Their main overhead branches intertwine to form girders from which hang wonderfully shaped and decorated swings.

Trees and vines weighed down by profuse leaves, fruits, and flowers surround Radha-kunda on all sides. Jewelled platforms of varying shapes and sizes hug the bases of those trees.

Radha and Krsna are partial to these altar-like platforms, and They often sit on them to enjoy a joke or to watch birds try to drink from the ripples on the jewelled seats, mistaking them for waves.

Gardens of madhavi vines encompassed by groves of kesara and asoka trees adorn the four corners of Radha-kunda, beyond which lie shadegiving banana trees and beyond them, fragrant flower gardens.

Vrnda-devi assigns forest goddesses and maidservants to maintain Radha-kunda and to provide, amongst other things, the fruits and flowers needed for service to Radha and Krsna.

These groves, flower gardens, and sub-forests are always well stocked with countless amenities of comfort, such as sweet-smelling incense for day and softly burning lamps for the night.

In addition to forests that go through the normal cycle of six seasons, there are seasonal forests surrounding Radha-kunda, each of which retain, year round, the climate of only one season.

The yards, pathways, and cottages are always sprinkled with fragrant water, and the groves, gates, swings, platforms, courtyards, and canopies are always lush with countless varieties of aromatic flowers.

The groves themselves are always replete with beds and cots whose mattresses and pillows are stuffed with a mixture of freshly plucked lotus petals, soft leaves, and stemless flowers.

Upon tables and countertops lie goblets of water and honey-wine, containers of betel leaves and spices, and varieties of sweets, fruits, and nuts, as well as savouries prepared from the finest ingredients.

The lake resembles a rainbow due to clusters of lotus flowers scattered on its mirror-like surface: in one place blue indivaras, in another white kahlaras, and in yet another red utpalas.

The pollen and honey of these flowers dissolve into the water, and as the sandalwood-scented breezes churn the waves, the already nectarean waters of Radha-kunda become still more aromatic.

A wide variety of birds enrich the atmosphere with their songs, inspiring one another in a variety of ways. Parrots, for example, recite poetry about Krsna in response to the cooing of swans.

At the sight of Krsna or a black cloud, the peacocks dance wildly. At this the doves and pigeons coo softly, inciting the cowherd girls to indulge in romantic fantasies with Syama.

The sun is intense at midday, but because of the shade provided by the lush foliage around Radha-kunda, the paths, groves, lakeside, and even the water at the lake’s centre stay invigoratingly fresh.

The groves of Radha’s eight dearmost girlfriends (asta-sakhis) grace the eight directions. These intimate friends personally oversee the affairs of their groves, decorating them with their own hands.

Because these groves display the pinnacle of the internal energy's artistic and architectural mastery, their inconceivable features and forms are impossible to describe or to comprehend fully.

The following portrait of Lalita’s grove — situated on the northern ghata of Radha-kunda, and the most famous of the sakhis’ kunjas — hints at the beauty, purpose, and structure of all the sakhis’ groves.

The exquisite Lalitanandada-kunja can be compared only to itself and to Lalita-devi’s unrivalled beauty, extraordinary qualities, and fathomless love for Radha and Krsna.

No doubt Lalita’s grove manifested itself from her perfected loving service to the divine couple. It can also be said, then, that Lalita-devi’s handsome grove bears a likeness to her magnificent heart.

The form of Lalita-sundari’s grove resembles a thousand-petalled lotus, the centre of which is an effulgent gold platform that expands and contracts, as does the entire lotus itself, to suit Krsna’s fancy.

Moreover, in this grove, which is well maintained by Lalita’s follower, Kalavali, the seasons also manifest their unique characteristics in keeping with the flow of Krsna’s amorous moods and activities.

At the centre of its innermost whorl is a stunningly attractive temple, which is actually a form of the goddess of beauty Indira, and which is known as Ananga-rangambuja, the lotus of amorous play.

Untold varieties of trees adorn the centre of this lotus with their five-coloured leaves, flowers, and branches. Those trees also decorate the matching multicoloured ornate platforms that surround them.

The filaments of the lotus — the stalks of its stamens — are banana trees whose trunks are made of gold set with jewels, and the stamens’ anthers are composed of the trees’ leaves, each one a different jewel.

The innermost whorl of the lotus consists of eight petals that form the eight principal sub-groves of Lalita-devi’s kunja. These are the residences and service areas of her eight main gopi assistants.

Just as Lalitanandada-kunja has eight sub-groves, each sub-grove also has its own eight subordinate groves where the attendants of Lalita-devi’s assistants enthusiastically serve and reside.

By design, each gopi's grove is the centre of another eight sub-groves of subordinate gopis, for as many groves as there are followers of Lalita-sakhi, or any of the other seven intimate friends of Sri Radha.

The innermost petals are gold, followed by petals of lapis lazuli, sapphire, crystal, and ruby each decorated with images of animals, humans, and demigods, designed to arouse amorous affection.

Asoka vines, completely covered by white, red, green, yellow, and blue flowers, embellish these eight groves, all with their own distinctive aromas that blend into one invigorating bouquet.

The northeast sub-petal, shaped like yet another eight-petalled lotus, swarms with humming bees and singing cuckoos. Said to give the spring season its joy, it is called Vasanta-sukhada-kunja.

Resembling a blue lotus, Asitambuja-kunja decorates the eastern wing of Lalita’s grove. It abounds in tamala trees with overhanging branches embraced by gold vines in bloom.

Asitambuja-kunja is ornately decorated with blue gems and surrounded by another set of sub-groves also shaped, tinted, and ornamented, resembling blue lotuses with golden receptacles.

In the southeastern part of Lalita’s grove Krsna and the gopis enjoy swinging on a lotus-shaped swing whose movements resemble Cupid’s lithesome bearing, thus it is called Madanandolana.

Two expansive bakula trees converge here to form a shade-giving canopy over the swing, which is suspended waist-high on four sturdy silken ropes that hang from the trees’ central branches.

The entire swing appears like an ornamented lotus, a central receptacle serving as the base of Radha’s and Krsna’s lotus-shaped seat, which features comfortable backrests, footrests, and cushions.

In eight directions, smaller lotus seats for the eight sakhis surround the main receptacle, all facing towards Radha and Krsna and similarly equipped with backrests, footrests, and cushions for sitting.

Above the divine couple’s seat is a canopy made of shimmering cloth laced with strings of pearls and garlands of miniature flowers that gracefully sway to and fro with the movements of the swing.

Vrnda and other girls push while some of them sing the divine couple’s glories. Radha and Krsna appear to face all of Their friends simultaneously as everyone enjoys the thrill of the festival.

Touching the southern bank of Radha-kunda is Arunambuja-kunja, the red lotus petal of Lalita’s grove, studded with glowing red rubies and brimming with aromatic, blossoming red-clove vines.

Perhaps the most stunning wonder of Lalitanandada-kunja is the lotus temple that rests on its southwestern petal, comprised of sixteen main chambers spread out, like lotus leaves, around a circular hall.

Each of these sixteen main chambers is divided into sixteen smaller rooms, located beside and above each other on either two or three floors, with windows or balconies on the outer wall of each room.

The rooms are accessed either by doors or by staircases. Although some rooms have no walls, all have gold floors supported by crystal pillars, and all are enhanced with ornate coral balconies.

In a few places the structure has no roof overhead, but for the most part the rooms are covered by intricately carved and decorared domes and spires that give shelter from both sun and rain.

The highest point of the lotus-palace, Sri Padmamandira, is a three- storey-high turret from which Radha and Krsna happily view the magnificent forest on one side, and Their two lakes on the other.

Each of the hundreds of rooms has its own unique decor, and each serves a singular purpose in the divine couple’s pastimes, making this jewelled palace a wonderland of multifaceted bliss.

Lalita-devi’s personal touch is visible everywhere, especially in the paintings that hang on each wall depicting her Lord’s many triumphs like the rasa dance, kunja pastimes, and the killing of Putana.

To the west of the glorious Padmamandira is the gold-lotus grove, Hemambuja, coated in yellow gold, set with gold tiles of many shades, and abounding with golden campaka trees in full bloom.

To the northwest is a grove of eternally blossoming madhavi creepers. It is known as Madhavanandada-kunja because its appearance and fragrance give great pleasure to Madhava.

Here Lalita carefully stores and then offers gifts of love to Radha and Krsna. Anyone who enters this eight-petalled, lotus-shaped kunja feels exhilarated, as though flying upon the back of a crane.

Finally, to the north is the all-white Sitambuja-kunja, a grove of naga-kesara and punnaga trees interspersed with every last variety of jasmine vine, heavily laden with their tiny white blossoms.

The whorl of this lotus is fashioned from gold-studded moonstones, and the filaments are composed of artistically set pearls. The other groves surrounding this lotus are also shaped like white lotus flowers.

This description gives hardly a hint of the astounding elegance, opulence, and sweetness of Lalitanandada-kunja, which only its transcendental beneficiaries, Radha and Krsna, can truly appreciate.

But gopis exclusively devoted to Radha and Krsna and Their dear Lalita-devi, who are completely dependent upon Them in all ways, can by the grace of these guardians know the secrets of this grove.

**\* \* \* \***

The multicoloured grove next to Lalita’s belongs to Visakha- devi. Because it is said to give Cupid bliss, it is famous as Madananandada-kunja as well as Visakhanandada-kunja.

At the centre of this grove is a jewel-laden, sixteen-petalled lotus temple whose structure is difficult for even exalted demigods to comprehend, not to speak of mere human beings.

Replete with beds, clothes, canopies, and curios, this kunja is surrounded by four gates made from flowering vines and guarded by bumblebees intoxicated by the prema that drips from the flowers.

Sri Visakha-devi resides here in great ecstasy, and her follower Manjumukhi, an expert artist, always ensures that the kunja’s unlimited facility is at the disposal of Radha and Krsna.

Four platforms shaded by a forest of campaka trees surround the central temple, and the combined fragrance of red, green, yellow, and blue campaka blossoms blocks out all other aromas.

The trees’ boughs teem with blue, yellow, and green chattering parrots. Shade-giving madhavi vines embrace those trees, which have colourful canopies strung between them from trunk to trunk.

If seen from above, the trees’ branches conceal the central temple and everything in its vicinity, appearing like a perfectly formed sixteen-petalled grove made entirely from leaves and flowers.

On the eastern shore of Radha-kunda is the embodiment of diversity and wonder, Citranandada-kunja, the grove of Citra-devi. Swarming with birds and bees, it is even more colourful than Visakha’s kunja.

Within the grove, like valuable gems set in a brooch, are trees, vines, jewels, platforms, courtyards, pavilions, and swings, all in hues displaying the full range of the visible spectrum.

In Radha-kunda’s southeastern corner is Indulekha’s grove, Purnendu-kunja, so named for its resemblance to the full moon and for possessing a whiteness far surpassing Lalita’s sub-grove Sitambuja.

Its couches and their sheets are white, its platforms and pavilions are made of crystal and moonstone, its lotuses are either pundarika or kairava, and its vines and trees all have white leaves and flowers.

Since the bees, pikas, and parrots are all white, they can be identified by their sounds alone. And the ground’s diamond-dust reflects moon and sun alike, whitening anything not already white by nature.

If, on a full moon night, someone accidentally wanders into this grove while the gopis entertaining Krsna are dressed in white, as they are on such nights, that guest will see nothing but glaring white light.

Opposite Lalita’s grove, on the south side of Radha-kunda, is the golden Campakalatanandada-kunja. Here all is either naturally golden, or becomes so due to the reflection from the gold-coloured ground.

Campakalata’s astonishing grove is dense with golden vines and trees. The yards, bees, swings, flowers, platforms, and pavilions are all similarly set in an array of golden hues.

When golden-complexioned Radha comes here dressed and ornamented in yellow, even Krsna does not see Her. If He does, He cannot distinguish Her from Her golden-complexioned companions.

Sometimes Krsna covers His dark limbs, hair, and face with His yellow shawl and enters unnoticed into Campakalata’s grove to hear the sweet words Radha and the gopis are speaking about Him.

If Jatila, sent to Radha-kunda by envious Padma, enters this golden grove when the divine couple sit side by side, then the old lady sees Krsna sitting alone, dutifully reciting His diksa-mantra.

This golden grove houses Radha-kunda’s famous kitchen, as well as the dining area of Radha and Krsna, a nicely set golden platform attended by Campakalata and the guru of all other cooks, Vrnda-devi.

Sometimes the exhilaration of loving exchanges spoils the divine couple’s appetites, but when They sit on this dining platform, its influence is such that They at once become hungry.

Due to restlessly hankering for Radha, Krsna’s appetite is often weak when He eats at Nandagrama, but in Campakalata’s grove He eats heartily because here His every last desire is fulfilled.

Nestled in the southwestern corner of Radha-kunda is a mysterious black grove that delivers (prada) unlimited happiness (sukha) to its stewardess, Rangadevi, thus it is called Rangadevi-sukhaprada-kunja.

Everything in this grove is blackish, such as the tamala trees entwined by black vines. Radhika’s attraction to Her lover increases whenever She comes here, because whatever She sees reminds Her of Syama.

The ground, platforms, and pavilions are covered with sapphires set so close together that they impart a blackish hue to whomever or whatever enters the kunja, thus Krsna is camouflaged here.

Once Jatila heard a rumour that Radha and Krsna were together at Radha-kunda. She went there as quickly as she could and happened upon Them as They sat together conversing here in Nila-kunja.

But because Krsna completely merged with the grove’s blackish interior, Jatila saw only innocent, demure Radha. After praising her daughter-in-law’s chastity, Jatila cursed the rumour-mongers and left.

The crimson grove of Tungavidya, behind the western bathing ghata of Radha’s divine lake, abounds in reddish vines, trees, yards, swings, leaves, and flowers. Its platforms and pavilions are set with rubies.

Tungavidyanandada-kunja, also known as Aruna-kunja, is the delight of Radha’s dear girlfriend. Its ruddy brilliance ignites fires of intense passionate love within the hearts of the divine couple.

Next to Aruna-kunja, in the northwestern corner of Radha-kunda, is the emerald grove of Sudevi named Sudevi-sukhada-kunja, where the vines, trees, birds, and even the bees are green.

The pavilions and platforms here are all studded with emeralds. Within a cottage on one such platform, Radha, surrounded by Her friends, and Krsna, surrounded by His, play games of dice.

Madhumangala is Krsna’s advisor, and Lalita is Radha’s. Krsna throws golden dice, Radharani black ones, as both contestants wager Their friends, pets, ornaments, and finally Themselves.

At the centre of Radha-kunda, connected to the northern ghatu by a bridge, is the secret island grove of Ananga-manjari, which excites unbounded bliss within Krsna by its unmatched display of beauty.

Covered in emeralds, rubies, and moonstones, Ananga-manjari’s grove resembles a sixteen-petalled lotus floating upon the water, and so is aptly named Salila-kamala-kunja.

Along the island’s waterline, the forms of swans and lilies, intricately carved and set with valuable gems, bob up and down with the waves, appearing like real swans playing amongst lovely clusters of lilies.

At the centre of the grove is a golden cottage inlaid with moonstones. Here Radha blissfully makes arrangements for Her younger sister, the embodiment of youthful perfection, to be alone with Krsna.

The eight primary groves on the banks of Radha’s lake resemble a vaijayanti garland around the neck of Radha-kunda, and the island grove of Radha’s sister, a bejewelled toy lotus in Radha-kunda’s hand.

The extraordinary features of Radha’s lake remind moonlike Krsna of His beloved, and so His heart overflows with joy to see them. He thinks, “Radha’s lake is as dear to Me as Sri Radha Herself.”

When Krsna finds Himself alone at Radha-kunda, suffering from the pain of being separated from His beloved, in His eagerness to again meet Radha He sees Her form in the different facets of Her lake.

The flamingoes playing on the water remind Him of Her swaying breasts, the white foam along the lakeside Her dangling pearl necklaces, and the movements of the waves Her changing moods.

The gentle lapping of the waves reminds Him of Her gentle love, the golden lotus flowers Her lotus face, and the bees swarming around the flowers the curly locks circling Her forehead.

The restless wagtail birds make Krsna think of the restless movements of Srimati Radharani’s lotus eyes, and the swans’ sweet warbling inspires Him to meditate on Her jingling ankle bells.

Krsna notices the clusters of red lotus flowers resisting the water as it enters from Syama-kunda. This reminds Him of Radha’s reddish lotus hands as they pretend to try to stop Him from embracing Her.

And when Krsna sees the wind drop some lotuses from His own lake onto the bee-covered lotuses in Hers, He recalls Her angry, crooked looks as He forcibly tries to kiss Her lotus face.

“Just listen!” thinks startled Krsna. “The buzzing bees flying over the waters and throughout these groves sound just like My Radhika’s faltering cries as She feigns anger with Me.”

As He looks to Giriraja for solace, Krsna cheers Himself: “At least I am not the only one here shedding tears. Aren’t these two lakes the tear-filled eyes of the lowered head of the Govardhana peacock?”

As Krsna thus remembers Radha (radha-smaranam) by absorption in the transcendental features of Her lake, He feels great bliss, even though He still feels extremely restless without Her.

Devotees who meditate upon the delightful features of Radha-kunda are actually meditating upon Sri Radha. May their contemplations one day mature into direct vision of Radha and Krsna.

**\* \* \* \***

By Krsna’s will the holy places associated with Radha are more famous and thus more glorified than those associated with Him, yet Syama-kunda is as dear to Krsna and His beloved as is Radha-kunda.

Brimming with playful charm, the waters, stairways, platforms, pavilions, and other remarkable features of Syama-kunda are in every way as sublime and attractive as the features of Radha-kunda.

Learned Vaisnavas, therefore, do not discriminate between the two lakes, judging one somehow superior and the other inferior, just as they do not see any ontological difference between Radha and Krsna.

However, the wise also recognise that Radha and Krsna, as the supreme worshipper and the supreme object of worship respectively, are two inseparable aspects of the one Supreme Absolute Truth.

Vaisnavas who prefer Radha-kunda over Syama-kunda, then, are merely expressing their natural mood of fondness for the supreme devotee, Srimati Radharani, and Her supreme place of worship.

To conclude, Radha-kunda is the highest place of worship for Srimati Radharani and Her followers, who all see Syama-kunda as the wor- shipable residence of their most worshipable object, Sri Krsna.

At Syama-kunda eight principal gopas — under the patronage of the eight sakhis, in a mood complementary to that of the gopis — each maintain their own grove in service to Krsna and His beloved Radha.

But only the most intimate boyfriends of Krsna (priya-narma-sakhas) are allowed to know of and participate in Krsna’s amorous pastimes— and even then in a limited way, not as fully as the gopis do.

Radha-kunda is perfectly square and Syama-kunda is perfectly octagonal, sitting just southeast of Radha-kunda. The groves of the eight principal gopas grace the eight sides of that octagonal kunda.

On the northwestern side of Syama-kunda is Subala’s grove, called Subalanandada-kunja. Sri Radha accepts this grove as Her own, and so it is the foremost of all other groves surrounding Syama's lake.

It was at the foot of Subala’s grove that Radha first bathed in Syama-kunda. Ever since then She and Her girlfriends come here at noon every day to bathe in the ghata called Manasa-pavana.

Because Krsna also bathes in His lake, Radha deems its waters to be like honey flowing from His lotus feet. And when She dips under the water, She feels as if She is in the strong embrace of Her paramour.

In this tranquil grove Radha and Krsna sometimes recline upon a soft bed of flowers while Subala fans Them and offers refreshments, astonishing even the gopis with his mood of intimate service.

At the northern side of Syama-kunda, inlaid with moonstones and pearls and always resounding in mirth, is comic Madhumangala’s grove, Madhutnangalanandada-kunja, whose patron is Lalita-devi.

Provoked by Madhu, that risible brahmana jester, Radha and Krsna entertain Their companions and intensify Their amorous feelings for each other by exchanging jokes and speaking in riddles.

The foliage, animals, and structures in this grove all reflect the personified mellows of comedy, so much so that as soon as one enters, one’s heart is at once touched and delighted by its jocular mood.

Overseen by Visakha, Ujjvala’s grove is next, paved with rubies. And on the eastern side, looked after by Citra-devi, is the gopa Arjuna’s grove, in which everything is blue or inlaid with sapphires.

To the southeast, supervised by Indulekha, is the gopa Gandharva’s grove, Gandharvanandada-kunja, which displays a dazzling array of colours and forms. Krsna and the gopis enjoy swing pastimes there.

On the southern side of Syama-kunda is a grove of illusion (maya), Haritmanimaya-kunja, in which the bees, birds, animals, vines, trees, and cottages appear to be made of pure emerald (harit-mani).

In this, Vidagdha’s pleasure grove, overseen by Campakalata, the divine couple play dice (chaupar) and then disappear from sight as Their sapphire and golden complexions blend into an emerald green.

Above the southwestern ghata is Kokila’s grove, with Rangadevi as its benefactress. Next to that is the eighth and final grove. It is a very colourful grove in the care of Sananda and overseen by Tungavidya.

In this way, taking inspiration from the groves surrounding Radha-kunda, the groves of Krsna’s dearest friends artistically decorate Syama-kunda like a garland of multicoloured lotuses.

The gopas manifested themselves as groves, desiring that their love might be the throne upon which Sri Radha and Sri Krsna sit, the temple that gives Them shelter, or the birds that serenade Them.

But despite their best intentions, the gopas’ groves are not enough to compel Krsna to reveal His amorous activities with Radha; the sakhas had to seek the patronage of the sakhis to fulfil their hearts’ desires.

Because the amorous pastimes of Radha and Krsna are extremely exclusive and confidential, they cannot be understood through the mellows of servitude, fraternity, or parental love.

Only the gopis have the right to revel in these transcendental pastimes of amorous love, and only the gopis can embellish them. Indeed, without the gopis, these pastimes could not take place at all.

Because there was no other way to enter the pastimes and service of Radha and Krsna, each gopa took shelter of a cowherd girl by adopting her ecstasy and following in her footsteps.

If even the divine couple cannot fully enjoy the mellows of Their own pastimes in the absence of the gopis, is it any wonder that the Vraja-vasis must also take shelter of the gopis to enter those pastimes!

Radha’s and Krsna’s pastimes are self-effulgent, unlimited, and all-powerful— ecstatic love personified. Even so, the spiritual mellows of those pastimes remain incomplete without the gopis.

The Supreme Lord is never complete without His spiritual potencies, so unless we take shelter of the gopis we cannot hope to enter into the company of Radha and Krsna or Their loving pastimes.

The waterway that joins the two lakes leaves Syama-kunda between the groves of Sananda and Subala and enters Radha-kunda under a golden bridge between the groves of Citra and Indulekha.

That bridge widens into a beautiful lotus at its centre where a golden pavilion covers it, and the entire structure rests upon latticework arches supported by columns carved from lapis lazuli.

Because the centre of this bridge is above the place where the waters of the two lakes meet, it is called the Yoga-pitha of Radha-kunda. It is as full of wonder, sweetness, and mystery as is Govinda-sthali.

When Radha and Krsna stand upon this bridge They can see peacocks jubilantly dancing on the shores, swans singing in the water, and swarms of bumblebees humming in the air.

As the divine couple gaze into the water of Their lakes, They see Themselves, and as They gaze at the meeting place (sangama) between the kundas, They are reassured of Their eternal union.

Next to the roads running parallel to the eastern side of Syama-kunda and the western side of Radha-kunda are two public ghatas where men and animals can rest, bathe, and quench their thirst.

Only the gopis and gopas who reside within the aforementioned groves can see all the transcendental marvels of these two lakes. Other Vraja-vasis see only as much as their relationships permit.

Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda are the exclusive playgrounds of paramour love. That love dances in every grove and upon every ghata, and makes the divine couple dance along.

Transcendental paramour love creates and maintains these divine lakes and also makes them visible to those devotees steeped in the perfected moods of ujjvala-rasa, but not to anyone else.

Because the loving mood of Krsna’s servants, friends, and parents is more or less devoid of ujjvala-rasa, they cannot see Radha-kunda and Syama-kunda as the cowherd girls do.

They see these two lakes as beautiful parks full of singing birds and flowering groves, but without any of the accoutrements of Cupid, like the flower-beds, extensive wardrobes, or private palaces and quarters.

And because the other Vraja-vasis’ mellows of devotion do not correspond with the mellow of Radha-kunda, they prefer residences and pastime places that nourish their own moods of love for Krsna.

For that reason, other than the gopis and priya-narma-sakhas, the Vraja-vasis rarely come to Radha-kunda. And when they do, they stay but briefly, prompted from within by Yogamaya to quickly move on.

And if such Vraja-vasis happen by Radha-kunda during Radha and Krsna's intimate pastimes, Yogamaya discourages them from stopping at all, directing them to continue on to their destinations.

In this world, advanced transcendentalists also see the eternal abode of Radha-kunda from their vantage points of perfection, provided they are inclined to these pastimes of transcendental amorous love.

Practising devotees so inclined may conceive of spiritual Radha- kunda, hut their success will he in proportion to the purity of their hearts and their capacities to practise remembrance (smaranam).

When non-devotees hear about or visit Radha-kunda, they generally consider it a material place; still, they may gain affinity for Krsna's abode by its spiritual influence and the mercy of a self-realised soul.

But pure-hearted Vaisnavas can feel the potency of transcendental Radha-kunda according to the level of their spiritual advancement, and a few very rare souls can see its eternal form.

O friend! Just meditate upon Radha and Krsna decorated with different ecstatic symptoms as They enjoy each other’s company during the midday hours in the charming setting of Radha-kunda.

Under the influence of both natural and transitory ecstasies, Their loving affairs are unpredictable. At any time, for example, Their eyes may show symptoms of obstinacy or eagerness.

Pleased by the jokes of Lalita and the sakhis, They are enthusiastic to enjoy activities like swinging, roaming in the forest, playing in the water, hiding Krsna’s flute, drinking honey, and worshipping the sun.

If your heart is so inclined, just meditate in this way upon lovely Radha and playful Krsna as They engage in pastimes of love amongst Their friends within the transcendental realm of Radha-kunda.

**\* \* \* \***

Prabodhananda Sarasvati Thakura writes, yatha yatha gaura padaravinde vindeta bhaktim karta-punya-rasih / tatha tathotsarpati hrdy akasmad radha-padambhoja-sudhambu rasih:

“By executing regulated devotional service and faithfully serving Lord Caitanya under the guidance of a spiritual master, we become fortunare enough to attain the inconceivable mercy of the Lord.

“As much as we direct our full attention to the service of Lord Caitanya, to that extent we will taste the nectarean service of the lotus feet of Srimati Radharani in Vrndavana.”

Indeed the more we serve Caitanya Mahaprabhu and His mission, the more qualified we become for eternal service as assistants of Srimati Radharani at Her divine lake, Radha-kunda.

But only those Vaisnavas who have surpassed the stage of ecstatic devotion and who have had their spiritual identities revealed to them are fully qualified for direct service to Radharani.

Those fortunate souls, by hearing the pastimes of the divine couple or seeing Radha-kunda on earth, may develop an intense desire to serve Radha by following in the footsteps of the Vraja gopis.

Such eager devotees pray: “O exquisite one! When Your lake, splendid with sweet water and blossoming lotus flowers, appeared before me, I at once began to yearn for Your service.”

“O Rupa-manjari! Will I one day see you assist Sri Radha as She decorates Her submissive lover, Krsna, with delicate flower ornaments in a secluded grove by the shore of Her lake?”

“O enchanting Radha! When will I see Krsna, whose form floods me with bliss, joyfully decorate You with forest flowers on the shore of Your lake, which teems with blossoming buds and humming bees?”

“By the shore of Your lake in a grove filled with humming bees, will You, the exemplar of all musical artistry, teach me to play the kacchapi-vina, which is the envy of Your rivals?”

“O enchanting lake! In the solitary groves gracing your shores my mistress eternally enjoys amorous sports with Her lover. You are most dear to Them. Kindly show me the girl who is my life and soul.”

A spiritually realised, perfected practitioner leaves behind all gross bodily identification, eschews worldly attachment, and directly beholds Vraja, the exquisite realm of eternally conscious bliss.

Such a greatly fortunate soul takes birth in the capital of King Vrsabhanu, accepts the appearance and disposition of a simple cowherd girl, a follower of Radha, and later marries in nearby Yavata.

She acquires the spiritual body of a gopi with a name, bodily lustre, and specific dress that perfectly complement her singular desire to express her own unique, individual love tor Krsna.

Then one day, as she carries water from the river Yamuna loudly singing Krsna’s names, some eternally liberated maidservants of Radha will approach her and speak to her sweetly:

“Our dear friend! From now on you will be counted amongst the companions of Lalita-devi. Forget your household chores for now. Come along with us and worship Radha and Krsna.”

At this the new gopi will at once wholeheartedly take shelter of these manjari associates of Sri Radha, who will mercifully take her hand and lead her into the presence of Lalita-sakhi.

Elegant Lalita-devi will graciously accept this new gopi as one of her personal maidservants and offer this new assistant a place of residence in her own majestic grove north of Radha-kunda.

By the order of beautiful Lalita-devi, Rupa-manjari will adopt this cowherd girl as an apprentice and lovingly teach her new disciple the ways of divine service by her words and example.

At the feet of Sri Visakha, Rupa-manjari’s new apprentice will then learn to play music full of transcendental mellows and to sing songs describing the wonders of Sri Krsna’s pastimes.

The other maidservants, such as Rati-manjari and Kasturi-manjari, will also affectionately welcome her into their fold, and the girls will all feel untold bliss to be together at the feet of Sri Radha.

Serving the desire-tree groves and cintamani banks of Radha-kunda, the new gopi will live in her own stunningly effulgent kunja, always hankering for the opportunity to serve Radha and Krsna.

Then one day, as she chants Krsna’s names, the song of His flute will enter her ears, leaving her spellbound by the sound of its call — “Radha! Radha!” — and bewildered as to what to do next.

Another day, while this gopi is absorbed in remembering the lotus feet of Sri Radha, Rupa-manjari will approach her and say, “O friend! Why are you just sitting here? Come outside and see who is coming!

“Radha and Krsna are approaching from different directions. Soon They will meet nearby to enjoy the bliss of each other’s company. Today you will be one of the maidservants at Their lotus feet."

To see Radha and Krsna perform Their midday pastimes at Radha- kunda is the essence of all perfection, and to do some small service for Them at that particular time is the crown jewel of divine treasures.

Then Rupa-manjari will say, ‘ Friend! Quickly! Make arrangements just as I have taught you!” That young gopi will obey her mentor’s command, then both will go to where Radha and Krsna are waiting.

She will carry the items of service on a pristine golden plate, standing shyly behind Rupa-manjari as Radha and Krsna smile and enquire, “From where have you brought this new maidservant?”

Rupa-manjari will explain that Their new maidservant was sent by her guru and say, “Because she is very meek and humble, I have kept her with me and enlisted her in Your service. I hope You are pleased.”

Rupa-manjari will then engage her disciple in the service of Radha and Krsna, thus fulfilling the young girl's long-standing desires as a sadhaka and a perfected soul.

When Sri Radhika, surrounded by Her friends, gives Her new maidservant a signal, the girl will pick up a jewelled comb to carefully and very expertly groom Radha’s gorgeous curly locks.

That gopi will then apply musk and sandalwood paste on the limbs of both Radha and Krsna, hang garlands around Their necks, and shyly gaze at Their faces while she decorates Their foreheads with tilaka.

She will then fix gold anklets on Their lotus feet, wash those feet with clear water from a golden pot, and carefully dry them with the abundant hair of her opened braid.

“The eternal perfection of their personal mellow of love as expressed in their service is the treasure of the gopis of Vraja. These individual moods and service are transcendentally fickle and supremely chaste.

“In contrast, neither the meditation of yogis nor the impersonal speculation of brahmavadis can bring their practitioners even near to the realm of such transcendental mellows as displayed by the gopis.”

Dear devotees! The perfection attained by this young gopi is available to anyone who takes shelter of Lord Caitanya’s teachings as they have come down to us from Rupa Gosvami through Srila Prabhupada.

By following the instructions of the Lord, we become qualified to see Radha and Krsna enacting Their midday pastimes at Radha-kunda, and there offer Them some menial service.

Advanced devotees who aspire for service at Radha-kunda always yearn to be in the group wherein Sri Radha is the leader and sole object of everyone’s desire to serve.

The treasure of such a fortunate soul’s life is the playful son of Nanda Maharaja, Sri Krsna, who is the Lord of Radha, but who is content to be known as Radha’s submissive, menial servant.

These devotees hanker, with the absolute totality of their faith and determination, for confidential service to the divine couple similar to that rendered by Rupa-manjari and her loyal companions.

Whether living at Radha-kunda physically or mentally, such devotees discard all material attachments and intensely pray for the attainment of this topmost spiritual perfection.

*May very fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa, on the shore of which, in a pleasant courtyard Queen Rādhā and Her friends sweetly joke with Lord Kṛṣṇa, the moon of Vraja, be my shelter. (Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī)*

## Chapter 16 - Siva-khor to Svananda-sukhada-kunja

In Bhauma Vrndavana the circumambulation of Govardhana Hill naturally includes parikrama of Radha- kunda and Syama-kunda, the peacock eyes of Giriraja. This is true in New Vraja-dhama as well.

When approaching Radha-kunda on Govardhana parikrama, one passes by the lake Siva-khor and its guardian, Ramesvara Mahadeva. This is the rear entrance to the Radha-kunda area.

The front entrance, however, passes by the protector of Radha-kunda, Kundesvara Mahadeva, to whom pilgrims offer prayers, hoping to be admitted into the divine abode of the Lord.

Thus on Govardhana parikrama, after offering obeisances to Ramesvara, devotees then face Kundesvara Mahadeva and offer their prayers to him, begging his permission to enter Radha-kunda.

Just as no one can approach Vamsivata or the circle of the rasa dance without the blessings of Gopisvara Mahadeva, no one can enter Radha-kunda without the grace of Kundesvara Mahadeva. This raises a question: Even materialistic people come into the area of Radha-kunda. How can it be said that no one enters without the permission of Kundesvara Mahadeva?

To understand the answer to this question one must first realise that Lord Siva is the husband of the material energy, Durga-devi, and that he also represents the master of the false ego, Lord Sankarsana.

On the order of her husband, Durga-devi covers Radha-kunda with a protective veil of matter that prevents those ruled by false ego, who identify only with their material bodies, from seeing the actual kunda.

Thus non-devotee visitors do not walk into Radha-kunda — or into any part of the holy dhama, for that matter. Instead, they tread upon a subtle layer of matter that covers and protects the dhama.

In this way Kundesvara Mahadeva — assisted by his wife, Durga-devi, and his master, Lord Sankarsana — protects Radha-kunda by keeping unqualified people from intruding into Radha’s and Krsna’s pastimes.

But as devotees approach Radha-kunda, Lord Siva ascertains the extent to which they are influenced by bodily identification and directs Durga-devi to give them access accordingly. In other words:

To the degree that one is free from false ego, to that degree the material covering is removed, and to that degree one may detect — but not necessarily see — Srimati Radharani’s divine abode.

Only to those devotees completely free from even the slightest taint of false ego, who fully know themselves to be servants of the servants of Radha and Krsna, does Devi give access to Radha-kunda.

Thus, to free ourselves from that false bodily identification, which Lord Sankarsana—represented by the snakes upon Siva’s body—can remove for us, we worship Siva as a devotee of Lord Sankarsana.

And because Lord Siva, as a pure Vaisnava, is favourably disposed to other Vaisnavas, he readily responds to our earnest prayers for deliverance from all material contamination.

We may wonder: “But if materialists cannot feel the presence of the dhama without Lord Siva’s grace, how is it that even casual visitors at times appear strongly affected by the dhama's atmosphere?”

The answer to this question is that both Kundesvara Mahadeva and Radha-kunda are merciful to those who are not offensive to the dhama, even if those persons are ignorant of the dhama’s true glories.

By having taken the trouble to travel to Vraja, and by appreciating its external beauty and natural opulences, visitors to the dhama have unwittingly accumulated pious credits (ajnata-sukrti).

Furthermore, hearing from and associating with the dhama’s residents elevates such ajnata-sukrti to a semblance of devotion (bhakty-abhasa), at which point Radha-kunda reciprocates.

In this way, almost all the guests who visit Radha-kunda and the holy places there, unless extremely envious or offensive, appear to have some feelings for Krsna stirred within their hearts.

About Lord Siva, Sri Sukadeva says: “Lord Siva is always united with his personal energy, the material nature. Manifesting himself in three features in response to the entreaties of nature’s three modes —

“He thus embodies the threefold principle of material ego in goodness, passion, and ignorance. The sixteen elements have evolved as transformations of that false ego.

“When a devotee of Lord Siva worships his manifestation in any one of these elements, the devotee obtains all sorts of corresponding enjoyable opulences.”

I prayed, “Obeisances to you! Your followers may worship you as the deity of fire in order to master fire, but I worship you as the deity of the false ego, the flames of which have tortured me life after life.

“O master! Please remove the misconception that makes me think of myself as master and controller. Only then, liberated from the clutches of your mara, will I be able to understand my real identity.
