To become gopi heroines in competition with Radha is undesirable to the followers of Lord Caitanya because they know that the best way to make Krsna happy is to unite Him with Radha. Therefore, the manjaris' mood of exclusive devotion to Radha is praised as the highest form of selfless love. Of this love Prabodhananda Sarasvati sings:

*radha-keli-nikunja-vithisu caran radhabhidham uccaran*  
*radhaya anurupam eva paramam dharmam rasenacaran*  
*radhayas caranambhujam paricaran nanopacarir muda*  
*karhi syam sruti-sekharopari carann ascarya-caryam caran*

**“When will I walk on the pathways of Radha’s pastime forests, chant the holy name of Radha, follow the religion of worshipping Radha, and happily serve Radha’s lotus feet in untold ways? And when, walking on the heads of all the Vedas, will I serve Radha in profuse wonderful ways?”**

**Verse 3**

*vrajendra-vasati-sthale vividha-ballavi-sankule*  
*tvam eva rati-manjari pracura-punya-punjodaya*  
*vilasa-bhara-vismrta-pranayi-mekhala-margane*  
*yad adya nija-nathaya vrajasi nathita kandaram*

**“O Rati-manjari! You are the most fortunate gopi in the city of Vraja’s king, because when Sri Radha forgot Her favourite belt in the midst of various pastimes, She requested you to retrieve it from the cave in which She had left it.”**

Commentary: Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami now reveals his spiritual identity as Rati-manjari, but he does so indirectly. He does not say, “I am Rati-manjari." Rather, after addressing Rupa-manjari in verse one, he now records Rupa-manjari’s reply, in which she describes her friend Rati to be one of Srimati Radharani’s favourite attendants. Why? Because Radha selected Rati to render a very confidential service.

Living entities attain their eternal spiritual bodies (siddha-deha) only after having become pure devotees on the platform of ecstatic devotional service (bhava), liberated from all material contamination. Devotees who have reached the stage of steadiness in devotional service (nistha) may be attracted to the activities of Krsna’s eternal companions, but that attraction cannot be fully realised at any stage of devotional service in practice, meaning that one’s spiritual identity is still beyond reach. However, after crossing the threshold of transcendence and arriving at bhava, or progressing further to prema, one is finally able to enter into the pastimes of the Lord, as Dasa Gosvami will describe in the verses to come.

*krsne rati gadha haile ‘prema’-abhidhana*  
*krsna-bhakti-rasera ei 'sthayi-bhava’-nama*

**“When affection for Krsna becomes deeper, one attains love of Godhead in devotional service. Such a position is called sthayi-bhava, permanent enjoyment of the mellows of devotional service to Krsna.”**

It appears from verse three that Radha and Krsna had gone to a cave of Govardhana Hill to be alone. When They returned to the assembly of gopis. Radha noticed that She was missing Her belt. Radharani thus finds Herself in a dilemma. If Her friends see Her without a belt, they will know that She has been intimate with Krsna and will certainly tease Her for it. But if She asks someone to find Her belt, the news will leak out in one way or another, and still She will be the brunt of jokes.

But Radharani notices Rati-manjari nearby. She knows that Rati is trustworthy and confidential. So, without uttering a word, Radha discreetly communicates with gestures and glances to Rati, who is able to retrace the divine couple’s steps to the cave. There she finds the belt, upon which hang sweet-sounding bells that charm Krsna’s mind when Radha walks or dances.

It also appears that a third person is privy to this secret: Rupa-manjari is so attentive to Radha’s needs that she not only noticed the missing belt, but She witnessed Radha’s secret communication with Rati as well. And so as Rati returns from the cave, Rupa meets her in a secluded place and praises her with the words we read in this verse.

Finally, keeping the belt concealed under her veil, Rati-manjari slides up to Sri Radha and fastens it around Her waist without anyone noticing. Rati’s mission was perfectly accomplished. While the other gopis are dancing and Krsna is playing the flute, Sri Radha gives Her servant a grateful sidelong glance that says, “Well done!”

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami accepts and records the words of Rupa-manjari as the blessings of his guru. This pastime is very dear to Dasa Gosvami, as evidenced by the fact that it is mentioned again in verses ninety-four through ninety-six.

**Verse 4**

*prabhur api yadunandano ya esa*  
*priya-yadunandana unnata-prabhavah*  
*svayam atula-krpamrtabhisekam*  
*mama krtavams tam aham gurum prapadye*

**“Let me surrender to my spiritual master, Yadunandana Acarya, who as a dear devotee of Yadunandana-Krsna is very powerful, and who showered me with the nectar of his mercy.”**

Commentary: In his identity as Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami the author now praises his initiating spiritual master. The opening lines of his book at once step into Vraja, but here, just three verses later, Dasa Gosvami offers respect, praise, and gratitude to Yadunandana Acarya. This is standard Vaisnava etiquette; how can one fail to remember one’s spiritual master when everything one has is due to his mercy? In another book, Sri Mukta-carita, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami lists some of the many gifts a devotee receives by the grace of his guru:

*nama-srestham manum api saci-putram atra svarupam*  
*rupam tasyagrajam uru-purim mathurim gosthavatim*  
*radha-kundam giri-varam aho radhika-madhavasam*  
*prapto yasya prathita-krpaya sri-gurum tava nato ’smi*

**“I bow down to the beautiful lotus feet of my spiritual master, by whose causeless mercy I have obtained the supreme holy name, the divine mantra, the service of the son of Saci-mata, the company of Srila Svarupa Damodara, Rupa Gosvami and his older brother Sanatana Gosvami, the supreme abode of Mathura, the blissful abode of Vrndavana, divine Radha-kunda and Govardhana Hill, and the desire within my heart for the loving service of Sri Radhika and Madhava in Vrndavana.”**

And if devotees find that bad habits are obstructing their access to those gifts bestowed by the spiritual master, they should not look outside their spiritual master’s line for “higher teachings” to circumvent those obstacles, or seek miracle cures to purify dirty hearts. Rather, they should remain sheltered beneath the desire tree of the spiritual master, who has offered divine fruit, with faith that the shelter of his shade will also enable them to relish that fruit.

*yasya deve para bhaktir yatha deve tatha gurau*  
*tasyaite kathita hy arthah prakasante mahatmanah*

**“Only unto those great souls who have implicit faith in both the Lord and the spiritual master are all the imports of Vedic knowledge automaticallyrevealed.”**

If devotees long to taste a specific flavour of love, they need only render single-minded service to the lotus feet of the one who instructed them in the conclusions of the scriptures and initiated them into the mantras embodying Krsna. The grace of such a guru or gurus will be the cause of removing those obstacles that cannot be overcome by devotees’ own efforts. Only in that way will Krsna’s supreme mercy be secured.

Raghunatha Dasa was extremely renounced and devoted, but despite repeated efforts he was unable to free himself from the shackles of family life. Finally, at the Panihati festival, Lord Nityananda blessed him that he would obtain the mercy and company of Lord Caitanya. This blessing fructified through Yadunandana Acarya, who proved to be instrumental in enabling Dasa Gosvami to flee to Jagannatha Puri and join Lord Caitanya's entourage.

**Verse 5**

*yo mam-dustara-geha-nirjala-maha-kupad apara-klamat*  
*sadyah sandra-dayambudhih prakrtitah svairi krpa-rajjubhih*  
*uddhrtyatma-saroja-nindi-carana-prantam-prapadya svayam*  
*sri-damodara-sac-cakara tam aham-caitanyacandram-bhaje*

**“I worship Lord Caitanyacandra, the supremely independent ocean of mercy, who with His ropes of mercy suddenly lifted me from the waterless well of household life, which is full of limitless suffering and from which it is very difficult to escape. He gave me the shelter of His lotus feet, which rebuke the lotuses, and He entrusted me to the care of Svarupa Damodara Gosvami.”**

Commentary: As a young man Raghunatha Dasa repeatedly tried to join Lord Caitanya, but he was always sent home with the instruction to absorb himself in thoughts of Krsna while fulfilling his household duties. Then one night, without warning, it appeared that Krsna had arranged circumstances so as to help Raghunatha Dasa not only escape his guards but get Lord Caitanya’s mercy as well. And sure enough, when Dasa Gosvami arrived in Puri the Lord welcomed him, putting him under the care of His personal secretary, Svarupa Damodara. Thus Raghunatha Dasa could stay in close proximity to the Lord and be trained by Him.

The significance of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s having resided in Puri with Lord Caitanya cannot be overstated. Of the Six Gosvamis, Raghunatha Dasa was the only one to live for an extended period of time in the company of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Moreover, not only was he privy to the Lord’s pastimes, but he lived in the company of Svarupa Damodara Gosvami, who was one of the two most confidential companions of Lord Caitanya.

By living in Puri in close proximity to Caitanya Mahaprabhu, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami had first-hand experience of the Lord’s later pastimes. And by meeting with the many great devotees who would visit the Lord from Navadvipa, Raghunatha Dasa also heard of the Lord’s childhood pastimes from those who had personally witnessed them.

From Svarupa Damodara, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami learned the process of rendering spontaneous service to Radha and Krsna within the mind (manasa-seva). In fact, Caitanya Mahaprabhu personally introduced the practice to him with these words:

*amani manada hana krsna-nama sada la’be*  
*vraje radha-krsna-seva manase karibe*

**“Do not expect honour, but offer all respect to others. Always chant the holy name of Lord Krsna, and within your mind render service to Radha and Krsna in Vrndavana.”**

And from Svarupa Damodara, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami also came to know of the ontological identity of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the philosophical points that underpin His teachings, and the reasons for His appearance in this world.

Therefore, when Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami came to Vrndavana, he transmitted this knowledge through his own writings and through the two famous books of his close companion and disciple, Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami, Govinda-lilamrta and Sri Caitanya-caritamrta.

Thus, much of what we know today of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, His mission, and His teachings, is thanks to Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami. Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami explains this in his own words:

**“In those days, Svarupa Damodara and Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami lived with Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, whereas all other commentators lived far away from Him. These two great personalities \[Svarupa Damodara and Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami\] recorded the activities of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu moment by moment. They described these activities briefly as well as elaborately in their notebooks. Svarupa Damodara wrote short notes, whereas Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami wrote elaborate descriptions.”**

**Verse 6**

*vairagya-yug-bhakti-rasam prayatnair*  
*apayayan mam anabhipsum andham*  
*krpambudhir yah para-duhkha-duhkhi*  
*sanatanas tam prabhum asrayami*

**“I was unwilling to drink the nectar of devotional service possessed of renunciation, but Sanatana Gosvami, out of his causeless mercy, made me drink, even though I was otherwise unable to do so. Because Sanatana Gosvami is such an ocean of mercy, he is very much compassionate to fallen souls like me, and thus it is my duty to offer my respectful obeisances unto his lotusfeet.”**

Commentary: Although Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami praises Sanatana Gosvami as his instructing spiritual master, Sanatana referred to the younger Vaisnava as his friend (suhrt). After Caitanya Mahaprabhu had left this world, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami came to Vrndavana in order to commit suicide by jumping from the top of Govardhana Hill. But Lord Caitanya appeared to Rupa and Sanatana in a dream and informed them of Dasa Gosvami’s plan. The two brothers then befriended Raghunatha Dasa and nurtured him, not allowing him to end his own life.

Sanatana Gosvami told Dasa Gosvami that he too had wanted to commit suicide: Sanatana had planned to throw himself beneath the wheels of Lord Jagannatha’s cart, but the Lord had reprimanded him for even thinking of such a foolish thing. “My dear Sanatana,” Lord Caitanya had said, “if I could attain Krsna by committing suicide, I would certainly give up millions of bodies without a moment’s hesitation.” After expressing his sympathy, the elder Vaisnava then instructed Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami to live on the banks of Radha- kunda and await the Lord’s mercy.

Dasa Gosvami followed Sanatana’s order, remaining at Radha- kunda for almost fifty years until he thought that he could not wait a moment longer. In that state of mature perfection, full of intense love and on the threshold of the final stage of ecstatic separation — death — Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami composed the verses of Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali.

From the time he instructed Raghunatha Dasa until the time he passed away, Sanatana Gosvami would regularly visit Raghunatha Dasa, review his writings, counsel him in his spiritual practices, and encourage him to be patient. “Your time will come!” he would say.

In this verse Raghunatha Dasa remembers his well-wisher, Sanatana Gosvami, for having taught him that renunciation, even to the point of renouncing the body, is artificial if it does not bring pleasure to Krsna or if it cannot be engaged in His service. Thinking himself to be very miserable, Raghunatha Dasa calls Sanatana an ocean of mercy for feeling the misery of others. In his own case, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami suffered the misery of separation from Srimati Radharani, and Sanatana Gosvami assisted him in bearing that misery.

The third line of this verse was often quoted by Srila Prabhupada to describe the merciful nature of Vaisnavas.

**“A Vaisnava is described as para-duhkha-duhkhi because although he is never distressed in any condition of life, he is distressed to see others in a distressed condition.”**

**Verse 7**

*aty-utkatena nitaram virahanalena*  
*dandahyamana-hrdaya kila kapi dasi*  
*ha svamini ksanam iha pranayena gadham*  
*akrandhanena vidhura vilapami padyaih*

**“O Princess! A certain maidservant overwhelmed with love, her heart burning in the great fire of separation, laments in the following verses.”**

Commentary: What does it mean to cry for Krsna? In the next ten verses Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami exemplifies this perfection of Krsna consciousness, summarised by Caitanya Mahaprabhu in His Siksastaka:

*yugayitam nimesena caksusa pravrsayitam*  
*simyayitam jagat sarvam govinda-virahena me*

**“O Govinda! Feeling Your separation, I am considering a moment to be like twelve years or more. Tears are flowing from My eyes like torrents of rain, and I am feeling all vacant in the world in Your absence.”**

Here referring to himself as dasi, the author again enters into his eternal identity as a gopi maidservant of Srimati Radharani. He now expresses his misfortune at being separated from his princess and longs for the opportunity to directly serve Her once again.

Love of Godhead is said to be marked by two prominent though dissimilar characteristics: bitterness and sweetness. More precisely, it simultaneously resembles poison and nectar. The poison is the transcendental misery of being separated from Krsna, and the nectar is the bliss of meeting Him.

Even devotees enjoying the bliss of Krsna’s company are keenly aware that they may soon be separated from their Lord, and that knowledge acts like poison. Indeed, even in Krsna’s presence the poison of impending separation may overwhelm devotees and make them think that Krsna has gone.

Conversely, when a devotee actually is separated from Krsna, the suffering is as intolerable as the effect of snake poison on the body — one must die. Yet the intensity of such separation causes deep absorption in Krsna, which in turn kindles a spark of hope that Krsna may soon reappear. And in that hope one also tastes the nectar of transcendental bliss.

If one were to compare the two states — one of meeting, the other of separation — he would find that the latter is even more intensely blissful than the former. Only those who have endured these kinds of loving sentiments for the Lord can truly understand how this is possible.

Krsna Himself explains the greater bliss of separation:

*tathapi sambhoga-sukhad api stutah*  
*sa ko 'py anirvacya-tamo mano-ramah*  
*premoda-rasih parinamato dhruvam*  
*tatra sphuret tad rasikaika-vedyah*  
*tac-choka-duhkhoparamasya pascac*  
*cittam yatah purnataya prasannani*  
*samprapta-sambhoga-maha-sukhena*  
*sampanna-vat tisthati sarvadaiva*

**“But this anguish of separation is praised as greater than the happiness of enjoying with those one loves. Separation is so pleasing to the mind that it cannot be described. It always transforms at last into an abundance of pleasure. Only experts in tasting these moods can understand how this happens. After the pain of despair is relieved, one’s heart feels fully satisfied, delighting constantly as one enjoys the great pleasure of meeting with one’s beloved.”**

Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali is filled with Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s expressions of pain due to separation from his worshipable Deity, Srimati Radharani. By tasting the lamentations of Dasa Gosvami, readers may experience a token drop of the bliss he felt as he composed these verses. Devotees can also learn the art of serving in separation, an art Caitanya Mahaprabhu taught by His example and Srila Prabhupada encouraged his followers to learn.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu specifically dedicated the last twelve years of His earthly pastimes to relishing the emotions of separation the gopis felt after Krsna departed Vrndavana for Mathura. In this regard Srila Prabhupada writes:

**“This ecstatic feeling of separation was specifically advocated by Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu through His actual demonstrations.”**

Neophytes and pseudo-devotees generally measure spiritual advancement in terms of an individual’s ability to see Krsna. But Caitanya Mahaprabhu teaches that devotees need not be overly anxious to see the Lord; rather, they should serve Him in the ecstasy of separation. Such ecstatic feelings are very helpful in attaining love of God.

Madhavendra Puri was the first devotee to write a poem addressed to Krsna expressing such feelings of ecstasy in separation from the

Lord. Lord Caitanya repeatedly tasted that verse, a favourite of Gaudiya Vaisnavas, as a vehicle for entering Radha’s woeful feelings upon Krsna’s departure from Vraja. Madhavendra Puri also chanted the verse at the very end of his life:

*ayi dina-dayardra natha he*  
*mathura-natha kadavalokyase*  
*hrdayam ivad-aloka-kataram*  
*dayita bhramyati kim karomy aham*

**“O My Lord! O most merciful master! O master of Mathura! When shall I see You again? Because of My not seeing You, My agitated heart has become unsteady. O most beloved one, what shall I donow?”**

As devotional service in separation is central to this verse, it is also central to the whole of Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali. For this reason Dasa Gosvami says, “A certain maidservant...laments in the following verses.” Vaisnavas of the Madhva-Gaudiya sampradaya consider this kind of worship in separation — in which devotees think themselves very poor and neglected by the Lord — to be the topmost level of devotional service. Caitanya Mahaprabhu disclosed Srimati Radharani’s feelings of ecstasy through the above verse of Madhavendra Puri, and Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami now discloses the manjaris’ feelings of ecstasy through his own profound composition.

**Verse 8**

*devi duhkha-kula-sagarodare*  
*duyamanam ati-durgatam janam*  
*tvam krpa-prabala-naukayadbhutam*  
*prapaya sva-pada-pankajalayam*

**“O Goddess! Please rescue this unfortunate person drowning in an ocean of pain. Haul me into the strong boat of Your mercy and transport me to the wonderful realm of Your lotus feet.”**

Commentary: It is said that the sum total of misery in the universe cannot equal even a drop of the misery Sri Radha feels when separated from Krsna, and the sum total of happiness in the universe cannot match a drop of the bliss She feels when meeting Him.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu also endured these acute feelings of separation and meeting. Night after night in the Gambhira, Lord Caitanya, submerged in the ocean of ecstatic separation from Krsna, displayed signs of emotional devastation like crying, madness, and raving. At such times, Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya sang appropriate verses composed by the acaryas and thus soothed the Lord’s misery by absorbing His mind in the glorification of Krsna. Lord Caitanya would taste the meanings of those verses and expand on them in turn; in this way He revealed the thoughts and desires of Srimati Radharani. Visions of Krsna would occasionally satiate the Lord’s divine passions, but once again Krsna would disappear, suddenly throwing Lord Caitanya back into a whirlpool of despair.

Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali follows this dynamic pattern of Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s ecstasies. In Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s eternal identity as the maidservant Rari-manjari, he finds himself floundering in an ocean of misery, the waves of which are churned by separation from his beloved, Sri Radha. By voicing his aspirations for serving Radha, he too becomes somewhat pacified until another towering wave of separation crashes down on his head, threatening to drown him. But just at the last moment, like a rescue boat unexpectedly arriving in the middle of the ocean, Srimati Radharani appears and consoles Raghunatha Dasa, only to disappear once again, leaving him heartbroken. The commentaries to Dasa Gosvami’s ecstasies presented here are meant to elaborate upon the meditations of one who aspires to personally cultivate such feelings of separation and meeting, feelings that gradually lead to the very threshold of transcendence.

The expressions of pain voiced in this verse by Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami can come only from the heart of one who has developed real attachment to his worshipable Deity, which goes hand in hand with detachment from all things ephemeral. Beyond this transcendental attachment and detachment, greed to serve Krsna in the manner of the Vraja-vasis must also arise, which in Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali specifically refers to serving Krsna as the manjaris do. All three spiritual assets — attachment, detachment, and greed — are acquired and then cultivated by hearing from devotees already endowed with these devotional ornaments and by offenceless chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra.

In this regard, scriptures emphasise the all-encompassing importance of time spent with pure devotees. The company of saints is so powerful that just a moment in their association is sufficient to plant the seed of attraction to serving Krsna’s eternal entourage, *lava-matra sadhu-sange sarva-siddhi haya*: “By even a moment’s association with a pure devotee, one can attain all success.”

Rupa Gosvami advises devotees who want to develop spontaneous love in the wake of the Vraja-vasis to acquire divine greed, in one way or another:

*krsna-bhakti-rasa-bhavita matih*  
*kriyatam yadi kuto ’pi labhyate*  
*tatra laulyam api mulyam ekalam*  
*janma-koti-sukrtair na labhyate*

**“Pure devotional service in Krsna consciousness cannot be had even by pious activity in hundreds and thousands of lives. It can he attained only by paying one price — that is, intense greed to obtain it. If it is available somewhere, one must purchase it without delay.”**

**Verse 9**

*tvad-alokana-kalahi-damsair eva mrtam janam*  
*tvat-padabja-milal-laksa-bhesajair devi jivaya*

**“O most beautiful one! With the medicine of the red lac from Your lotus feet, please resurrect this person now dead from the venom of the black snake of not seeing You.”**

Commentary: As already noted, the pain of separation is like poison. When a venomous black snake bites someone, poison spreads throughout the victim’s body with the intensity of liquid fire. If the poison reaches the throat and one can taste it, then death is nigh. This is how Rati-manjari feels in separation from Sri Radha; she would die if she could, but the ambrosial taste of prema keeps her alive. Thus she feels both alive and dead simultaneously.

Rati remembers the red lac on Radha’s lotus feet and prays, “I am on the verge of death. At any moment my soul could leave this body. If I could only see Your beautiful lotus feet, the soles of which are smeared with glowing red lacquer, then the poison that is killing me would be neutralised.”

And what if Krsna were to appear instead? Would Rati-manjari be satisfied? No! Srimati Radharani is her only shelter, a shelter even Krsna cannot replace. But if Radharani were also to appear with Krsna, then Rati’s prayers would be answered and her heart would be at peace. Pure devotion is marked by specific loyalty to one of Krsna’s eternal companions. Naturally this includes loyalty to Krsna Himself, but the pure devotee’s transcendental allegiance cannot be exchanged outright for allegiance to Krsna. Caitanya Mahaprabhu is referring to this principle in part when He says, *gopi-bhartuh pada-kamalayor dasa-dasanudasah*: “I am the eternal servant of the servant of the servant of Krsna, the maintainer of the gopis.”

The more intense are one’s feelings of separation from one’s beloved, the deeper is one’s absorption in thoughts of him or her; the deeper the meditation, the closer one will feel to one’s worshipable Deity.

The gopis paint their feet with a red lacquer called laksa or alta. It is a cosmetic that women paint on the soles of the feet, which when dry reflects the colour of the heart’s passion. In addition to a beauty aid, laksa also safeguards the feet from drying out in contact with the warm dust of Vrndavana. Thus it is doubly effective.

*kamam tulikaya karena harina yalaktakair ankita*  
*nana-keli-vidagdha-gopa-ramani-vrndais tatha vandita*  
*ya sanguptataya tathopanisadam hrdy eva vidyotite*  
*sa radha-carana-dvayi mama gatir lasyaika-lilamayi*

**“The splendid, glorious, playful dancing feet of Sri Radha, which Krsna paints with red lacquer, which intelligent, beautiful gopis worship, and which the Upanisads keep concealed within their hearts, are the only goal of my life.”**

**Verse 10**

*devi te carana-padma-dasikam*  
*viprayoga-bhara-dava-pavakaih*  
*dahyamanatara-kaya-ballavim*  
*jivaya ksana-niriksanamrtaih*

**“O effulgent one! With the elixir of a moment’s glance, please restore the life of this gopi maidservant of Your lotus feet, who now burns in the great forest fire of separation from You.”**

Commentary: As hard as he prays, Raghunatha Dasa still cannot see the red lac on Sri Radha’s soles. Therefore the poison of separation consumes his whole being with an intensity comparable only to being trapped in the midst of a raging forest fire, or worse, the inextinguishable vadava fire said to burn within the depths of the ocean.

“Perhaps I am already dead!” Raghunatha Dasa thinks as Rati-manjari . “Surely Sri Radha will miss my services. But if She were to simply send a fleeting glance this way, then my life would be restored, just as Sukracarya brought the dead demons back to life.”

In truth, wherever devotees glorify Krsna or chant His name with the loving intensity displayed by Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, Krsna cannot be far away. The same principle may be applied to Srimati Radharani. The Lord says:

*naham tisthami vaikunthe yoginam hrdayesu va*  
*tatra tisthami narada yatra gayanti mad-bhaktah*

**“My dear Narada, actually I do not reside in My abode, Vaikuntha, nor do I reside within the hearts of the yogis, hut I reside in that place where My pure devotees chant My holy name and discuss My form, pastimes, and qualities.”**

After Krsna disappeared from the rasa dance, the gopis first searched for Him, then enacted His pastimes, and finally they appealed to Him in song. All that time Krsna was hiding behind a tree nearby, watching. As Krsna admits in the verse above, even the sweetness and opulence of Vaikuntha cannot keep Him from witnessing the love-laden drama of the gopis’ sankirtana.

But why don’t Radha and Krsna reveal Themselves immediately — and permanently — to practising or perfected devotees who pine for Their audience? For each of the two categories of devotees in question, the sadhaka and the Siddha, the answer is different.

For practising devotees who worship the Lord by sankirtana and other means with feelings of separation, Radha and Krsna do not reveal Themselves at once because They want to give these aspiring Vaisnavas further impetus to perfect their worship. Deep humility develops in such surrendered devotees as a result of the feelings of neglect they endure, not being able to see their worshipable Deities. They think, “My sadhana is useless. Because of my offences, my Lord remains far distant from me." By constantly thinking in this way, immature devotees gradually become freed from lust and its corollaries, and their attachment matures into pure loving devotion.

However, for devotees like Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami—whose love is already mature — Radha and Krsna do not appear on request for another reason. That reason is to increase the devotees’ attachment even further and to glorify both the intensity of love and the love’s possessor. And when Radha or Krsna do appear, They quickly disappear again in order to deepen Their devotees’ love once more through feelings of separation. A devotee who has thus lost the vision of his beloved is like a pauper who has lost a great fortune: he becomes so anxious that he can think of nothing else.

While speaking the verses of Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami suffers a level of anguish in separation that only a personal companion of the Lord can know. Occasionally he gets to see Srimati Radharani in person, but he quickly loses sight of Her again and falls even deeper into the abyss of remorse. To hear Dasa Gosvami’s words as he passes through such pitiable states cannot help but enrich the heart of the practising devotee with similar feelings.

**Verse 11**

*svapne ’pi kim sumukhi te caranambujata-*  
*rajat-paraga-patavasa-vibhusanena*  
*sobham param autaram ahahottamanam*  
*bibhrad bhavisyau kada mama sartha-nama*

**“O beautiful-faced girl! When, even while dreaming, will I decorate my head with the splendid, perfumed dust of Your lotus feet, and thus justify my head’s being called the highest limb of my body?”**

Commentary: It is very hard to have a vision of Sri Radha. But Dasa Gosvami cannot give up hope, and so he places another alternative before his mistress: “Even if You do not appear before my eyes, if at least You appear to me in a dream, and in that dream place Your lotus feet upon my head, I will have achieved the perfection of life.”

Devotees sometimes dream of Krsna. These visions are often the product of mental impressions released in one’s unconscious state, but on occasion they are instances of the Lord appearing in person. In fact, the scriptures are full of accounts in which the Lord or His eternal associates appear to devotees in dreams. Generally, the more Krsna conscious a devotee is, the greater the likelihood that a dream of the Lord is actually Krsna personally manifesting Himself. As long as the modes of nature dominate a devotee’s consciousness, his so- called spiritual experiences are materially tinged. But when one has reached the transcendental platform his consciousness is pure and unchanging, whether awake or asleep.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami longs to see Radha in his sleep, because if Radha were to appear in that way, as Rati-manjari, he might find an opportunity to smear the dust of Sri Radha’s feet on his head. The dust of Radha’s feet is very potent, being a mixture of different transcendental ingredients.

Like the other gopis and gopas, Srimati Radharani walks barefoot throughout Vraja. Thus Her soles are covered with cintamani dust and flower pollen. Both of these ingredients have their own characteristics, but upon Radha’s feet they are reddened by the lacquer She paints on Her soles as well as spiritually enhanced simply by contact with Her divine form. Sri Radha is love and kindness personified; therefore, that reddish dust can bless whomever it touches with those same qualities. And yet, another ingredient further enhances the fragrant pollen-dust wafting from the lotus of Radha’s feet: the kunkuma that Radha smears upon Her breasts.

How would the kunkuma from Radha’s chest find its way to Her own feet? When the divine couple meet and embrace, Krsna’s broad chest and flower garland are smeared with the kunkuma from Radha’s breasts. After Their amorous pastimes, as Krsna rearranges Radharani’s clothes and ornaments, He becomes enamoured by Her dainty feet and holds them to His heart, moistening them with His tears. In this way Radha’s kunkuma also finds its way to Her soles. Rati-manjari thinks, “If I could just place that dust on my head, the dust itself would be like a crown, giving me dominion over a kingdom greater than any territory ruled by the world’s greatest emperors.”

*svakam sva-kuca-kunkumadibhir atha priyam limpati*

**“Sometimes \[Radha\] anoints \[Krsna\] with the kunkuma and other fragrant powders on Her breasts.”**

**Verse 12**

*amrtabdhi-rasa-prayais tava nupura-sinjitaih*  
*ha kada mama kalyani badhiryam apanesyate*

**“O auspicious girl! When will the sound of Your ankle bells, sprinkling droplets from the ocean of nectar, cure my deafness?”**

Commentary: Krsna’s name, form, and pastimes bring auspiciousness to both the materia! and spiritual worlds, but Radha brings auspiciousness to Krsna. Thus Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami calls Her Kalyani (“auspicious one”).

The author’s eagerness for Radha is insatiable. Nonetheless, he reasons that to see Her in a dream may still be asking for too much, so he suggests an alternative: “Let me just hear the tinkling sound of Your ankle bells.” Of course, that tinkling is no ordinary sound. It is an elixir capable of restoring life to the afflicted, just as a vision of Radha is capable of doing.

As Radha walks along the forest path, Her ankle bells sound like the cooing of swans. Suddenly She sees Krsna in the distance. Not knowing what else to do, She looks down at Her feet and walks forward with slow, faltering steps. Then, cursing the shyness that keeps Her from glancing at Krsna’s moonlike face, Srimati Radharani looks up and runs to Her beloved as Her ankle bells jingle in a way that must be heard to be properly cherished.

The sound of Radha’s ankle bells is usually compared to the cooing of swans or the singing of cranes, but in this verse Dasa Gosvami compares that jingling sound to the sprinkling of droplets from the boundless ocean of prema. Srimati Radharani is Herself that ocean of nectarean love and Her ankle bells shower droplets of Her loving ecstasies over the paths of Vraja in the form of transcendental sound.

Dasa Gosvami thinks, “If my ears were to hear that sound, they would be cured of their deafness.” He considers his senses impotent without being engaged in Radha’s service. Thus, because he cannot see Her, he is blind; because he cannot hear Her voice, he is deaf; and because he cannot speak to Her directly, he is dumb.

Devotional service means to engage one’s senses in the Lord’s service (hrsikena hrsikesa-sevanam bhaktir ucyate). A body with senses not so engaged is as good as dead. Therefore, Raghunatha Dasa reasons that if he could just hear the sound of Radha’s ankle bells, then not only would his deafness be cured, but all of his senses would be spiritually enlivened. Just as any one of a transcendental- ist’s senses can serve the function of any other sense, when any onesense becomes touched by divine grace, every other sense shares in thebenefit.

Finally, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami appeals to Srimati Radharani as Kalyani. “You bring auspiciousness to everyone including Krsna. How then can You abandon me, exiling me to such abject misfortune and suffering? O Kalyani! Please don’t neglect Your worthless maidservant!”

**Verse 13**

*sasakabhrd-abhisare netra-bhrnancalabhyam*  
*disi vidisi bhayenodghurnitabhyam vanani*  
*kuvalaya-dala-kosany eva klptani yabhyam*  
*kim u kila kalaniyo devi tabhyam jano 'yam*

**“O Goddess! When You go out to meet Krsna on a moonlit night, dashing fearfully from one tree to another like a rabbit and turning the whole forest blue with Your restless, bumblebee eyes, will You glance towards me?”**

Commentary: Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s relentless entreaties for some form of personal contact with Srimati Radharani have brought his mind to the point of uninterrupted absorption in Her pastimes with Krsna. This pure sadhana is his only consolation, because through all of his suffering, Dasa Gosvami’s senses remain absorbed in the object of his meditation.

As the Age of Kali unfolds, it will be increasingly difficult to find devotees — who are in this age, by and large, new to Krsna consciousness— with the purity of heart needed to fully absorb their minds in Krsna’s pastimes. Unlike great souls such as Srila Prabhupada, who worshipped Radha and Krsna from childhood, the conditioned souls of this time, despite having obtained human birth, worship mammon instead. Thus, in their materialistic lives, the attempts they make to become happy are akin to drinking poison. Fortunately for them, Krsna descended from Goloka as Caitanya Mahaprabhu to bring them the congregational chanting of Krsna’s names. It is this nama- sankirtana that will alone purify the most covetous heart and grant the key to obtain Goloka’s treasure of divine love.

Therefore, to enter the realm from which Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami offers his prayers, devotees must sincerely worship Gaura- Nitai by chanting and distributing, without offence, the holy names of Radha and Krsna — Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare — and by praying for the mercy of Radha and Krsna as did Narottama Dasa Thakura:

*ha ha prabha nanada-suta, vrsabhanu-suta-yuta,*  
*karuna karoho ei-baro*  
*narottama-dasa kaya, na theliha ranga paya,*  
*toma vine ke ache amara*

**“My dear Lord Krsna, You are the son of King Nanda, and Your consort, Radharani, is the daughter of King Vrsabhanu. So You are standing together here. Now I am surrendering unto You. Please do not kick me away or push me away with Your lotus feet because 1 have no other shelter. I am just taking shelter \[of\] Your lotus feet without having any other means. So please accept me and deliver me."**

As the white lotus of Radha’s and Krsna’s mercy gradually unfolds, its recipients become attracted to the pastimes of the divine couple more and more, until those pastimes become their very life and soul.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami offers us one vivid example of this divine truth. Absorbed in his identity as Rati-manjari, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami prays to he able to go with Sri Radha on that night’s clandestine excursion to meet Krsna.

Because the moon has lit up all of Vraja with its silver rays, Radharani dresses in an all-white sari, smears Her limbs with white sandal paste, and dons pearl and diamond ornaments. She is all white, except for Her restless bluish eyes. She and Her only companion, Rati, tiptoe out of Radha’s home and past the barns, where Her husband is most likely asleep with the cows. The front gate is so heavy that it normally takes two men to open it, but empowered by Her determination, Radha opens it by Herself.

Between Her home and the edge of the forest is mostly open space with only a tree here and a house there. Afraid that passing villagers will see Her, Radha runs from one shelter to another, looks around frightfully the way rabbits do, and then dashes to the next hiding place. All the while, Rati-manjari is right behind Her. Suddenly startled by the voice of a night watchman, the two girls freeze, their hearts racing. Radha looks at Rati with fear in Her eyes, but Rati reassures Her with a sympathetic glance and whispers, “Don’t worry. He’s going the other way.”

Srimad-Bhagavatam says that Krsna is feared by fear personified (yad bibheti svayam bhayam). But Krsna fears Radha’s temper. And now that young cowherd girl who is feared by He who is feared by fear personified looks to Her youthful maidservant for reassurance, fearful that Her flight to Krsna may be foiled. Rati grasps Radha’s hand, looks around the corner from their hiding place, and says, “It’s clear now. Let’s go.”

The two girls finally slip into the forest, where they are free to move without risk. The leafy canopy overhead blocks out all light from moon and stars, making Rati wonder whether they will be able to find their way. But then she notices that wherever Radha looks Her glance lights up the forest, tinting everything blue. Without a word, Radha looks behind Her at Rati with a grateful expression that says, “I couldn’t have done that without you. Thank you so much.” Then Radha turns back around and plunges deeper into the forest, running at the speed of mind, worried that Krsna must be anxious for Her arrival. Rati tries to follow, but Sri Radha disappears down the forest path ahead of her.

In the next moment Rati finds herself sitting by the bank of Radha-kunda as the Gosvami, Raghunatha Dasa. Having lost vision of Radha, bereft of service to Her, feeling as though forcefully expelled from Her pastimes, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami laments and his tears moisten the ground.

**Verse 14**

*yadavadhi mama kancin manjari rupa-purva*  
*vraja-bhuvi bata netra-dvandva-diptim cakara*  
*tadavadhi bata vrndarainya-rajni prakamam*  
*carana-kamala-laksa-sandidrksa mamabhut*

**“O queen of Vrndavana! Ever since a manjari called Rupa filled my eyes with light in the land of Vraja, I have yearned to see the red lac adorning Your lotus feet.”**

Commentary: Separation from Srimati Radharani absorbs the mind of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami more deeply in thoughts of his mistress. In such a spellbound state, it is as if he hears Her asking, “Rati! How did you develop this strong desire to see Me, to see the alta on My soles?” Dasa Gosvami answers, “O my queen! Ever since I came to Vrndavana I’ve had the good fortune to spend time with Your Rupa-manjari. Her teachings and company have transformed me, filled me with an intense desire to serve You, and made me eager to see the red lac on Your feet, of which devotees speak and to which even Krsna offers service.”

Devotees whose practice has brought them to the stage of perfection in amorous love are first introduced by their spiritual masters to Rupa-manjari, the leader of Radha’s maidservants. Sri Rupa then trains these aspirants in the finer details of service to the divine couple. When they are accomplished in every way, she introduces them to Radha and Krsna.

The newly perfected and fully trained maidservant carries Rupa-manjari’s items of service, following her to a grove where Radha and Krsna are waiting. As she stands shyly behind Sri Rupa, the new maidservant attracts the divine couple’s curiosity. When They at last kindly enquire, Rupa-manjari introduces her new maidservant.

That same Rupa-manjari appeared in this world as Rupa Gosvami. According to the order of Lord Caitanya, he wrote many books on the science of devotional mellows: Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu describes the cultivation of pure devotional service, which leads to the awakening of love for Krsna in one of five primary mellows; Ujjvala-nilamani guides devotees in knowledge of the amorous mellow exclusively, including the mellow of Radha’s maidservants, the unique gift Caitanya Mahaprabhu gave to the greater community of Krsna’s devotees; Stavamala, amongst other works, elaborates on Srimati Radharani’s personality and the nature of Her liaison with Krsna, as well as the gopis’ roles in enhancing the mutual love of the divine couple.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has written about what he learned from Rupa Gosvami in this way:

*yad-yatnatah sama-damatma-viveka-yogair*  
*adhyatma-lagnam avikaram abhun mano me*  
*rupasya tat smita-sudham sadayavalokam*  
*asadya madyati hares caritair idanim*

**“Because of Srila Rupa Gosvami’s efforts, my heart is now peaceful, controlled, able to know the nature of spirit, fixed in yoga, and attached to the Supreme Lord. By His smiling, nectarean, compassionate glance my heart has become wild by remembering the transcendental pastimes of LordHari.”**

Thus, whether in this world as Rupa Gosvami or in the spiritual world as Rupa-manjari, Sri Rupa is responsible for nurturing the Krsna consciousness of Lord Caitanya’s followers. It is for that reason we cannot possibly repay our debt to this unlimitedly compassionate soul. Nevertheless, we must try. Thus, in this world we assist Rupa Gosvami in giving pure devotional service to others. To him we pray:

*sri-caitanya-mano-’bhistam sthapitam yena bhutale*  
*svayam rupah kada mahyam dadati sva-padantikam*

**“When will Srila Rupa Gosvami Prabhupada, who has established within this material world the mission to fulfil the desire of Lord Caitanya, give me shelter under his lotus feet?”**

**Verse 15**

*yada tava sarovaram sarasa-bhrnga-sanghollasat-*  
*saroruha-kulojjvalam madhura-vari-sampuritam*  
*sphutat-sarasijaksi he nayana-yugma-saksad-babhau*  
*tadaiva mama lalasajani tavaiva dasye rase*

**“O lotus-eyed girl! When Your lake, filled with sweet water and splendid with many blossoming lotus flowers and buzzing bees, appeared before my eyes, I at once began to yearn for the nectar of direct service to You.”**

Commentary: By the grace of Rupa Gosvami, Raghunatha Dasa was able to live by the bank of Radha-kunda in Bhauma Vrndavana. And by the divine grace of Srimati Radharani, Radha-kunda revealed to Dasa Gosvami its eternal form in Goloka.

After Krsna killed the demon Arista, Srimati Radharani insisted that He purify Himself from the sin of killing a bull by bathing in all the holy places of the universe. But instead of travelling from tirtha to tirtha, Krsna dug His own kunda, called the holy places to come there, and bathed before Sri Radha and Her friends in a mood of arrogant triumph.

At the sight of Krsna’s wonderful achievement, Radha became transcendentally jealous. She and Her girlfriends excavated Sri Radha's own lake then and there, first filling it with water from Manasa-ganga before that liquid nectar was mixed with the holy waters that had come to fill Krsna’s kunda. At midnight Radha and the gopis bathed in Her lake, after which She was again willing to accept Krsna’s company in pastimes of love.

In this way the divine couple manifested eternal Syama-kunda and Radha-kunda, both of which displayed all transcendental opulence for as long as Krsna remained here on earth. But after Krsna’s disappearance the two lakes, like other eternal pastime places, hid their divine attributes. They appeared subject to the laws of material nature, gradually becoming covered and then lost, until CaitanyaMahaprabhu rediscovered them on His visit to Vrndavana. Finally, the two lakes were given to Dasa Gosvami to develop into the forms we see today.

*tirtha ‘lupta jani’ prabhu sarvajna bhagavan*  
*dui dhanya-ksetre alpa-jale kaila snana*

**“The Lord then understood that the holy place called Radha-kunda was no longer visible. However, being the omniscient Supreme Personality of Godhead, He discovered Radha-kunda and Syama- kunda in two paddy fields. There was only a little water, but He took His bath there.”**

Radha-kunda is very fragrant. Its shores are magnificent with blossoming groves named after Radha’s friends and alive with the sweet sounds of bees and birds. This lake is strikingly attractive, but beneath its alluring veneer is a reservoir of spiritual mellows. A desire vine of pure love appears within the hearts of those who bathe or live there, even within the hearts of those who merely see or touch it. In other words, by serving Radha-kunda, the celestial vine of pure love for Krsna sprouts, hearing flowers of service to Sri Radha. By the power of that divine love, devotees may one day see Krsna following His beloved at Radha-kunda, carrying Her bathing clothes as if He were Her attendant.

Those greatly fortunate souls who have been granted residence on the banks of Radha-kunda may one day see Krsna and the gopis laughing and splashing as they enjoy water sports. They may see Radha singing to Krsna on Radha-kunda’s banks as She accompanies Herself with Her lute, or they may see the gopis tease Krsna as He loses a game of dice in one of the groves on the banks of the kunda.

But how rare these visions are! Even Narada Muni cannot see these things. Only those with fully developed pure spontaneous love in the mood of the gopis are fortunate enough to be blessed with these sublime visions. And those not so fortunate should worship the souls who are, as Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami says:

*pura premodrekaih pratipada-navananda-madhuraih*  
*krta-sri-gandharvacyuta-carana-varyarcana-balat*  
*nikamam svaminyah priyatara-saras-tira-bhuvane*  
*vasanti sphita ye ta iha mama jivatava ime*

**“Because of having previously worshipped the beautiful lotus feet of Sri Gandharva-Acyuta with the eternally fresh sweetness of pure transcendental love, some great souls are able to reside on the shore of Queen Radha’s favourite lake \[Radha-kunda\]. These great devotees are my life and soul.”**

**Verse 16**

*padabjayos tava vina vara-dasyam eva*  
*nanyat kadapi samaye kila devi yace*  
*sakhyaya te mama namo ‘stu namo ‘stu nityam*  
*dasyaya ce mama raso 'stu raso ‘stu satyam*

**“Devi! I shall never ask You for anything other than the excellent service of Your lotus feet. Again and again I offer my respectful obeisances to the idea of becoming Your friend, but I only aspire to become Your maidservant.”**

Commentary: After Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has expressed his desire to directly serve Srimati Radharani, the question arises, “In what way does he want to serve Her?”

If Radha were to say, “Rati! Would you like to become one of My girlfriends like Lalita or Visakha?”

“Thank You, but no,” Rati would answer without hesitation, because she only aspires to be Radha’s maidservant.

All things being transcendentally equal, since Radha’s sakhis are sublimely superior to Her maidservants, the manjaris, why would Dasa Gosvami so eagerly accept the inferior role of a maidservant? Because the maidservants’ fortune is greater than that of even Radha’s closest friends!

Narottama Dasa Thakura advises devotees who follow in the footsteps of Rupa Gosvami and Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami to carefully understand the manner in which these acaryas love and serve Radha and Krsna in their eternal identities as Radha’s maidservants.

Devotion rooted in transcendental lust is of two kinds: that of the sakhis, who desire to serve Krsna by directly enjoying with Him (sambhogheccha-mayi), and that of the manjaris, who desire to taste the sweetness of the sakhis’ love without enjoying directly with Krsna themselves (tad-tad-bhavecchatma).

The happiness Radha’s maidservants feel is greater than the happiness felt by Her friends because Her maidservants enjoy the mellow of servitude alongside the mellow of friendship. Furthermore, sakhis like Visakha have equal love for Radha and Krsna, called sancari- bhava, but manjaris like Rupa have greater love for Radha than for Krsna. The manjaris’ love is called bhavollasa-rati. Moreover, because the manjaris take the role of maidservants, Radha allows them to do menial services for Her that She would never give to Her friends. She also allows the manjaris to serve Her and Krsna in circumstances that are too intimate for sakhis to witness. Thus the fortune of the manjaris is greater.

The manjaris want only to assist in Radha's and Krsna’s loving pastimes. Although bodily contact with Krsna gives happiness to all the girls of Vraja, the manjaris are not eager for such pleasure because they find greater pleasure in serving the union of Radha and Krsna. Why should they trade a greater happiness for a lesser one?

Therefore Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has taught us to appreciate the service of the manjaris and to pray to them as follows:

*tambularpana-pada-mardana-payo-danabhisaradibhir*  
*vrndaranya-mahesvarim priyataya yas tosayanti priyah*  
*prana-prestha-sakhi-kulad api kilasankocita bhumikah*  
*keli-bhumisu rupa-manjari-mukhas ta dasikah samsraye*

**“By offering Radha and Krsna betel nuts, by massaging Their feet, bringing Them water, arranging Their secret meetings, and by performing many other services, many maidservants affectionately please Radharani, the supreme controller of the Vrndavana forest. When the divine couple are absorbed in loving pastimes, these maidservants serve Them — in Their presence — without shyness, moving more freely than even Radha's dearmost friends such as Lalita and Visakha. I take shelter of those maidservants, who have Rupa-manjari as their leader.”**

After hearing Dasa Gosvami’s appeal, Radha may test him, saying, “Perhaps you are too shy to tell Me that you want to be My friend. Perhaps it is your humility that makes you say you want to be My maidservant.”

Then Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami will reply, “With palms joined, I beg You not to tease me. The desire to be Your sakhi has never entered my heart. I tell You truthfully, it has not appeared in my mind even while dreaming. I have always had only one desire: to be Your maintained maidservant (palyadasi)

**Verse 17**

*ati-su-lalita-laksaslista-saubhagya-mudra-*  
*tatibhir adhika-tustya cihniti-krtya bahu*  
*nakha-dalita-haridra-garva-gauri priyam me*  
*carana-kamala-sevam ha kada dasyasi tvam*

**“O lady whose golden complexion defeats the pride of crushed turmeric! When will You be pleased to stamp my arm with the lacquer-coloured symbols on Your soles, certifying me as a servant of Your lotus feet?”**

Commentary: In the previous verse Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami rejected Radha’s offer to become Her sakhi, reaffirming his exclusive desire to be Her maidservant. In this verse he silences all doubts about his aspirations by requesting Radha for a hallmark. He wants Her to stamp his body with a distinctive mark that would declare him to be Her servant. But he will not be satisfied with any ordinary hallmark; he only wants one that clearly proclaims his connection to Krsna as well. After all, isn’t Krsna Radha’s beloved, as well as the beloved of the Vraja gopis?

What is this very special hallmark, and how will he acquire it?

Radha and Krsna are conversing in a grove by the banks of Radha-kunda. Suddenly Radha assumes a domineering role and demands that Her beloved repaint the alta on Her feet. Nearby, Rati-manjari overhears Radha’s order. At once Rati enters the kunja with a golden tray holding a container of lacquer and the brushes for applying it. Rati kneels beside Krsna, holding the tray as Radha leans back and places Her feet in the lap of Krsna, who then eagerly begins to paint the pink soles of Sri Radha’s lotus feet.

As Krsna goes about His work, He praises the alta’s great fortune for being able to take up residence upon Radha’s lotus feet. “Even I don’t have such a privilege!” He thinks. Then Krsna gets an idea: “I am no different from My name. So if I write My name in the alta on Radha’s feet, then I will also be able to reside there.” Taking up a jewelled stylus He writes “Krsna” on the balls of both feet then leans back to look at His work with pride.

Meanwhile, Rati is still kneeling beside Krsna, watching His every move and reading His mind. When she sees that Krsna is very pleased with Himself she giggles and covers her face with her veil. Radha suspiciously eyes the two co-conspirators, wondering what they could be up to. Rati can’t control her giggling, and so Radha sits up to find out what’s going on, inadvertently kicking Rati’s upper arm, just below the shoulder.

Rati looks at her arm and sees a moist aka mark displaying unmistakable signs like a flag, thunderbolt, barleycorn, and chariot. And there in the midst of those distinctive icons is the signature “Krsna.” This is exactly what she wanted, an official hallmark certifying her as Radha’s dasi. Rati looks up at smiling Radha and then over at Krsna, whose eyes betray His divine jealousy for not having been similarly recognised by Radha. It is a rare accolade indeed. Rati thinks, “I will never wash this arm.” Now, wherever she goes, she will show the sakhis and manjaris that she has been officially certified a maidservant of Radha.

Absorbed in relishing this pastime, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami is fully submerged in his form as Radha’s maidservant and in the sequence of morning services he renders to Sri Radha as Rati-manjari. He feels confident. He is now an accredited dasi.

**Verse 18**

*pranalim kilalair bahubhir abhi sanksalya madhurair*  
*muda sammarjya svair vivrta-kaca-vrndaih priyataya*  
*kada bahyagaram vara-parimalair dhupa-nivahair*  
*vidhasye te devi pratidinam aho vasitam aham*

**“O Goddess! When will I, with great love and happiness, daily rinse the drains of Your house with pure water, dry them with my own hair, and then scent Your commode with fragrant incense?”**

Commentary: The day begins early for Radha and Krsna at about three-thirty each morning. During the night They enjoy the rasa dance in the company of Their girlfriends, then bathe in the refreshing waters of the Yamuna and picnic beneath a starlit sky. Afterwards they all rest for a while in a grove of Vrndavana forest. But as daybreak approaches they are obliged to return to their homes, sneak back into their bedrooms, and when awakened by their parents, pretend to have been there all night. This transcendental deception is possible only by the arrangements of Yogamaya.

The manjaris are the first to rise, bathe, and dress. Sakhis like Lalita are not far behind. After making one excuse or another they all leave their homes and families and hurry to Radha’s residence to help Her prepare for the day. Most of these girls, having taken birth in or around Varsana, have been Radha’s friends from childhood. They were all married to cowherd men in Yavata, and so now they continue to live in the same village as their princess and friend. It is not surprising, therefore, that they would spend so much time with Srimati Radharani. Over time, their husbands and in-laws have grown accustomed to that daily reality.

Narottama Dasa Thakura longs for a life that begins with birth in Varsana, where the company of the divine couple is possible by the mercy of the gopis. He opens his prayer of longing with these words:

*hari hari ara ki emana dasa*  
*kabe brsabhanu-pure ahiri gopera ghare*  
*tanaya haiya janamiba*

**“When, oh when will I take birth as a gopi in Maharaja Vrsabhanu’s town, where many gopas and gopis live? O Lord Hari! Lord Hari! Will I someday attain this perfection?”**

Narottama continues,

**“Living in the city of Vrsabhanu, when will I be accepted by its residents as one of their kin, and when will I become the dear friend of the exalted gopis and be able to serve them directly? When will Lord Krsna be merciful and reveal to me His reddish lotus feet? When will I become so fortunate as to attain the divine couple’s lotus feet? Then at last, my heart’s desires fulfilled, my life will be successful.”**

The word rati means love. Rati-manjari is the embodiment of love for Sri Radha. As Srimati Radharani’s maidservant, Rati gives her love exclusively to Radharani. Rati is as inseparable from Radha as is Radha’s own shadow. Therefore Rati is the first to appear in the morning at Radha’s home in Yavata. In verses eighteen through forty-four, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami describes the different aspects of Srimati Radharani’s bathing, dressing, and ornamentation, and how he, as Rati-manjari, assists in these services while constantly reminding Radha of Krsna.

Krsna’s pastimes are called human-like (nara-lila) because — especially on earth — they are similar to the activities of human beings. But does that mean the Lord evacuates like an ordinary human being? In Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.31) the elderly gopis complain to Mother Yasoda, *evam dharstyany usati kurute mehanadini vastau*: “Sometimes, being angry, Krsna passes urine and stool in a neat, clean place in our houses.”

However, the waste from the transcendental body of the Lord or His eternal companions cannot be compared to the obnoxious substances that come from the bodies of conditioned souls. Srimad-Bhagavatam hints at the difference when describing the stool and urine of Lord Rsabhadeva. His excrement was not disturbing; to the contrary, the Lord’s stool and urine were so aromatic that eighty square miles of the countryside were filled with their pleasant aroma.

Regarding this unique characteristic of Rsabhadeva, Srila Prabhupada says,

**“From this we can certainly assume that Lord Rsabhadeva was transcendentally blissful. His stool and urine were so completely different from material stool and urine that they were aromatic. Even in the material world, cow dung is accepted as purified and antiseptic. A person can keep stacks of cow dung in one place, and it will not create a bad odour to disturb anyone. We can take it for granted that in the spiritual world, stool and urine are also pleasantly scented. Indeed, the entire atmosphere became very pleasant due to Lord Rsabhadeva’s stool and urine.”**

It is then not surprising that Rati-manjari prepares Radha’s commode and burns incense so that it is clean and fresh when Radha rises from bed. What may be surprising is that Rati cleans the drains of the house with her hair. But this merely shows the extent of Rati’s love. She loves everything about Radha. There is nothing she would not do for Her. Devotees truly eager to go back to Godhead must be willing to render any kind of service. This is the statement Dasa Gosvami makes by placing this verse before those that describe services seemingly more pleasant, like dressing Radha or combing Her hair. Similarly, devotees must be willing to accept the more arduous services of preaching and pushing forward the Krsna consciousness movement before they can take up the wonderful services described in the verses of this book. As Srila Prabhupada would often say, “First deserve, then desire.”

**Verse 19**

*pratah sudhamsu-militam mrdam atra yatnad*  
*ahrtya vasita-payas ca grhantare ca*  
*padambuje bata kada jala-dharaya te*  
*praksalya bhaviru kacair iha marjayami*

**“When, at Your house early in the morning, will I carefully wash Your two lotus feet with water mixed with clay and scented with camphor, and then dry them with my hair?”**

Commentary: Getting Radha ready for Her morning excursion to Nandagrama takes place between six and seven. Generally, Radha and Krsna bathe at home, but on occasion They bathe in the Yamuna, giving Them another opportunity to meet.

Since Rati washed the commode earlier and dried the drain with her hair, it should be understood that after performing that service she again bathed and dressed in fresh clothes. In a clean state she uses her hair once again, but this time to dry Radha’s feet.

Out of intense spiritual greed Dasa Gosvami’s mind is spontaneously attracted to these meditations, a process that may be called the “religion of the mind” (manodharma). Unless the heart has been purified and awakened to spiritual attachment, the mind will be too agitated to remain absorbed in thoughts of Krsna’s pastimes. But by chanting Hare Krsna, devotees learn to concentrate their minds on the sweet sound of Krsna’s names. As their minds become attached to the holy names, attraction to thinking of Krsna’s pastimes gradually follows.

Since Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali is all about remembering Radha’s and Krsna’s pastimes, more should be said about the process of smaranam, especially in conjunction with the chanting of the Hare Krsna maha-mantra.

Jiva Gosvami explains that if devotees’ hearts have been purified by surrender, by service to their gurus, and by hearing about the Lord, then they can practise remembrance (smaranam). However, because scriptures stress the indispensability of chanting Krsna’s names — as in the verse ending with harer namanukirtanam — the practice of remembrance should always be accompanied by harinama-sankirtana. Chanting should never be given up.

The practice of smaranam entails the mind’s disciplined investigation into the Lord’s names, forms, qualities, and eventually His pastimes. It all begins with the process of remembering Krsna’s sweet holy names: chanting them softly to oneself (japa), or chanting them loudly, by oneself or with others (kirtana or sankirtana). Such chanting should be free from the ten offences against the holy name, and should be clear, steady, and blissful.

Thereafter, when the mind no longer wavers while chanting, hearing, and remembering the Lord’s holy names, a devotee may add the practice of remembering His form, a process which, when perfected, results in loving devotion. The wife of Sudama Brahmana declares that the Lord appears directly and offers Himself to those who remember Him:

*aste 'dhuna dvaravatyam*  
*bhoja-vrsny-andhakesvarah*  
*smaratah pada-kamalam*  
*atmanam api yacchati*  
*kim nv archa-kaman bhajato*  
*naty-abhistan jagad-guruh*

**“Lord Krsna is now the ruler of the Bhojas, Vrsnis, and Andhakas and is staying at Dvaraka. Since He gives even His own self to anyone who simply remembers His lotus feet, what doubt is there that He, the spiritual master of the universe, will bestow upon His sincere worshiper prosperity and material enjoyment, which are not even very desirable?”**

When chanting spontaneously invokes the form of the Lord, devotees may begin to remember Krsna’s qualities, complementing the already perfected remembrance of the first two attributes of the Lord, His name and form.

Once devotees have mastered remembrance of the Lord’s name, form, and qualities they may endeavour to remember His pastimes as well, employing the celebrated process of lila-smaranam. As remembrance of the Lord's pastimes becomes harmonised with the other three attributes, a hint of devotional inclination appears in the mind. As remembrance of the Lord’s pastimes becomes increasingly spontaneous and fixed on the daily eightfold division in which Krsna enacts them, lila-smaranam has fully matured by the sunlight of divine mercy, suddha-sattva. At this point pure spiritual mellow (rasa) blossoms in the heart. In this way, by continued chanting of Krsna’s names, contemplative devotees eventually become aware of their eternal spiritual identities (svarupa-siddhi) along with their individual characteristics, such as name and service.

To discuss the many nuances of meditation would exceed the scope of this appendix, but devotees should at least be aware that there are five progressive stages of remembrance, known as recollection, absorption, meditation, constant remembrance, and trance. Awareness of these stages will help devotees evaluate their own progress and determine whether they are qualified to practise the process of remembrance. If they are qualified and inclined, such knowledge offers a kind of road map to help them prepare for the challenges that lie ahead.

In a very general sense, recollection (smarana) implies the basic effort to understand Krsna and the process of devotional service to Him. That effort is in itself a form of remembrance, but one lacking in direction and consistency. New devotees' uninformed and unskilled efforts at japa are one example of this type of remembrance. Recollection is followed by absorption (dharana), in which a semblance of attraction to Krsna enables devotees to briefly withdraw their minds from material affairs and fix them in a general way — and again, unsystematically — on their japa.

Then comes meditation (dhyana), which includes following an authorised procedure for contemplating the four attributes of the Lord as described in the preceding paragraphs — His name, form, qualities, and pastimes. This is the beginning of real meditation.

When such remembrance proceeds without interruption and becomes a continuous flow of nectar, it is called constant remembrance (dhruvanusmrii). In constant remembrance nothing can divert the mind from its spontaneous attraction to the Lord, for devotees so accomplished have attained liberation from material entanglement.

The fifth stage of remembrance is trance (samadhi), in which devotees are so absorbed in the object of their remembrance that they are aware of nothing else, including their very own selves. This is theplatform from which the verses of Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali are spoken. In his ecstatic trance, absorbed only in service to Srimati Radharani, the author has forgotten his identity as Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami. He identifies himself only with Rati-manjari, and nothing—other than the disappearance of his worshipable object, Sri Radha — can bring him back to external consciousness. At the stage of samadhi devotees are not only absorbed in exclusive remembrance of the Lord, but they may actually have a vision of Krsna and His pastimes.

Thus Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s samadhi begins with remembrance and transforms into direct revelation, the bliss of which, after an all too brief period, abruptly ends with him once again realising that he is an aged sannyasi on the banks of Radha-kunda.

Devotees who desire to practise remembering the pastimes Dasa Gosvami describes here in Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali should do so only when their spiritual masters have certified that they are qualified for meditation (dhyana) and have given their blessings for the same. Others may read these verses, without attempting to deeply meditate upon them, to know about the transcendental ideals that they reveal about the realm of pure devotion.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura explained to his disciples that even if they were not fully qualified to hear of Krsna’s eightfold daily pastimes in detail, they should know that such a reality exists:

**“After the realm of anartha-nivrtti is artha-pravrtti, pure conjugal service to Radha and Krsna. This is the transcendental reality. If we do not know of this transcendental realm then all our efforts may end in nirvisesa-vada, impersonalism. Do not let your days pass in trying only for anartha-nivrtti. Artha-pravrtti is also necessary.”**

**Verse 20**

*praksalya pada-kamalam krta-danta-kastam*  
*snanartham anya-sadane bhavatim nivistam*  
*abhyajya-gandhitatarair iha taila-puraih*  
*prodvartayisyati kada kim u kinkariyam*

**“When will this maidservant brush Your teeth with a twig, wash Your lotus feet, and, when You have entered the bathroom, offer You a seat and massage You with scented oil?”**

Commentary: By training the mind to hear and by keeping it absorbed in thoughts of Krsna, devotees qualify themselves to eventually enter the Lord’s pastimes. Krsna Himself says:

*yam yam vapi smaran bhavam tyajaty ante kalevaram*  
*tam tam evaiti kaunteya sada tad-bhava-bhavitah*

**“Whatever state of being one remembers when he quits his present body, in his next life he will attain to that state without fail.”**

And Narada Muni gives a brilliant example of how, by absorbing his mind in thoughts of Krsna, a devotee is awarded an eternal spiritual body after giving up his temporary material frame. He says:

**“A grassworm confined in a hole of a wall by a bee always thinks of the bee in fear and enmity and later becomes a bee simply because of such remembrance. Similarly, if the conditioned souls somehow or other think of Krsna, who is sac-cid-ananda-vigraha, they will become free from their sins. Whether thinking of Him as their worshipable Lord or an enemy, because of constantly thinking of Him they will regain their spiritual bodies.’’**

Here Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami calls himself kinkari. The etymological meaning of the word is based on the syllables kim (what) and karin (doing). Thus a kinkari is someone who asks, “What can I do?” (kim karomi). Such is the mentality of a maidservant.

In earlier verses Dasa Gosvami was adamant that as the gopi Rati he would only accept the service of being Radha’s maidservant. Now he speaks more casually, calling himself “this maidservant.”

And if Radha were to ask, “O kinkari! What service will you do?” Rati would answer, “When You rise from bed, into Your cupped hands I will pour camphor-scented water, with which You can first rinse Your mouth and then wash Your face to refresh Yourself. Then I will give You a desire-tree twig and watch Your earrings swing back and forth as You vigorously brush Your teeth. After that, I will offer

You a jewelled, bow-shaped scraper that You can pull across Your delicate tongue. Then, after You have rinsed Your mouth and face a few more times and washed Your hands, I will give You a towel with which You can pat dry Your face and hands.”

To tease Rati, Radha may say, “But what about My other friends and maidservants who usually help with these services? If you do everything, what will they do?” Joining her palms, Rati would reply, “She who can arrange for countless gopis to serve Her, can also arrange for this maidservant to serve Her alone.”

And if Srimati Radharani raised Her eyebrows in wonder and nodded Her head as if to say, “And then?” Rati would continue, “And then I will lead You into the bathroom and seat You on a golden chair covered with a soft cloth. I will remove whatever ornaments remain and anoint Your body with rose-coloured oil, so sweetly scented that it captivates the mind. I will then tenderly but firmly massage Your limbs from head to toe, trying to touch You with the same delicate care as Krsna does, quickly relieving Your fatigue. Finally, I will sprinkle Your body with powdered saffron and camphor to remove the oil.”

As Sri Radha’s eternal maidservant, Rati knows how to perfectly execute every aspect of her mistress’s morning ablutions. Rati is a kinkari, but she doesn’t need to ask or be told what to do because her temperament is that of a maidservant. She is always looking for service. Of kinkaris like Rati-manjari, Prabodhananda Sarasvati Thakura writes:

*unmada-madhura-prema-nanda-marandaika-sindhu-nihsyandi*  
*radha-padaravindam visramayan naumi kinkari-vrndam*

**“Let me glorify the gopi maidservants (kinkaris) who attend Sri Radha’s lotus feet, from which flows a nectar ocean of the bliss of unrestrained, sweet pure love.”**

Although pleased that her service as a manjari is acceptable, Rati still wants to hear directly from Radha’s own mouth that she has been accepted to the rank of maidservants.

Once Radha was returning from Surya-kunda where Krsna, disguised as a brahmana, had just conducted the worship in the presence of Jatila. As Radha was leaving, She kept turning Her head for another glance at Krsna while calling out to Her helper, “O kinkari! Come on. Hurry up!” Rati also wants to hear Radha call out to her, saying, “O kinkari!” She wants Radha to acknowledge her with the words “You are Mine!”

**Verse 21**

*ayi vimala-jalanam gandha-karpura-puspair*  
*jita-vidhu-mukha-padme vasitanam ghataughaih*  
*pranaya-lalita-sakhya diyamanaih purastat*  
*tava varam abhisekam ha kadaham karisye*

**“O You, the heavenliness of whose lotus face shames the moon! When may I carefully bathe You with water scented with flowers and camphor, brought in jugs in advance by one of Your charming and affectionate friends?”**

Commentary: Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali may be called an elegy, or an elegiac poem, the verses of which can be seen from two perspectives. One perspective is that of an advanced practitioner who describes, with the word “when,” his longing for a service or revelation he has not yet attained. The other perspective is that of a fully perfected devotee who has achieved direct, personal realisation of the events described in these verses, but absorbed in the mood of separation, he still hankers for them. Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami is one such eternally perfect devotee. Caitanya Mahaprabhu has obliged him to express his realisations in a mood suitable for practitioners to follow by placing Dasa Gosvami in a situation wherein he hankers in separation from his beloved Radharani.

Perfected souls will sometimes say, “I have seen this pastime!” But in order to set an example for practitioners, they generally say, “When will I see this pastime!” For example, Bhaktivinoda Thakura sings, “O friend! What did I see today!”But elsewhere he says, “When, oh when will that day be mine?"

The path of perfection is never achieved through cheating; that is, by artificially trying to induce realisation. Rather, realisation progresses naturally from intense hankering during separation, to direct realisation of a pastime. Therefore, hankering in separation is the key that unlocks the impenetrable vault of divine grace and gives admittance into the realm of true realisation. And even after perfection is achieved, the mood of separation still prevails. In short, feelings of separation act like salt to keep the ocean of spiritual mellows ever fresh.

After Rati removes Radha’s ornaments, she helps her mistress change from an ornate sari into simple white bathing clothes. Rati then gently unties Radha’s braid and combs it lightly, allowing Radha’s lovely hair to cover Her back. From behind, Sri Radha appears to have disappeared under Her cascading black tresses, as if She had gone beneath one of Yamuna’s waterfalls. Enchanted, Rati pours amalaki juice over Radharani’s head, rubbing Her scalp with the tips of her fingers and thoroughly cleansing Her hair with the scented liquid.

One after another, Rati empties golden pots full of Yamuna water over Radha’s transcendental form, rubbing the powdered saffron, camphor, and sandalwood from Her limbs and making them shine like newly molten gold. As she expertly does all of this, she also speaks to Radhika in a soft voice:

“Lotus-faced girl, the water flowing over Your limbs makes You appear like the golden Ganges, flowing without impediment to one place — the dark Krsna-ocean. In the water of that Ganges grows one golden lotus, Your face. When that lotus reaches its destination, its intense loveliness will cause the appearance of Krsna’s smiling face, just as the moon appeared to the demigods and demons as they churned the ocean of milk. And when the waters of the Ganga and the ocean have merged together, and the lotus and moon float side by side, the lotus will prove to be the more gorgeous of the two. To acknowledge this truth, the moon will rejoice and dance in bliss upon the nectarean waves of love.”

Srimati Radharani, eyes closed, plunges into Rati’s description of Her imminent meeting with Krsna. The very thought of flowing to Him in the way the Ganges flows to the ocean soothes Her heart. She wants Krsna to be happy, and She is willing to do anything to realise His happiness. From materialists who covet wealth, to advanced devotees who want nothing but prema, everyone is praying to Krsna for something. But Sri Radha does not want anything from Him. She just wants to give to Krsna, not to take. And that giving culminates in offering to Him the most precious gifts — Her own body and mind.
