Rati softly speaks to Radha’s feet, and at the same time indirectly addresses Radha, who listens with interest. Rati says, “Playful, dancing feet! Countless winsome gopis offer you their obeisances, and the Upanisads keep you hidden in their hearts. You are the only goal of my life.”

Rati continues speaking, but this time to the lac. “O laksa! What austerities did you perform to be awarded residence at this topmost place of pilgrimage? Please tell me and I will adopt that self-same vow. It would be my great fortune to take birth as red lac too. Not only do you adorn these sacred feet, but the curly locks of Krsna’s head as well. Truly, you are most fortunate.”

The mention of Her foot lac on Krsna’s head awakens mixed emotions in Radha, emotions that forcibly drag Her mind back to a well-known pastime. By reading the expressions on Sri Radha’s face, Rati-mafijari follows her mistress into the realm of recollection.

One evening, Srimati Radharani sets out in search of Krsna, Her longing for Him increasing with every empty grove. At long last She discovers Krsna on the bank of the Yamuna, enjoying the company of other gopis. Krsna acknowledges Radha’s arrival but treats Her in the same way as the others, neglecting Her unequalled stature. Understandably, Radharani feels slighted and runs away. Krsna at once abandons the other girls and sets out in search of His favourite gopi. Finally, after a concerted effort by Radha’s friends, Radha agrees to meet with Krsna. But the result only adds insult to injury when Krsna keeps Radha waiting for Him all night.

Srimati Radharani feels neglected, betrayed, and cheated. When Krsna finally arrives at dawn, Radha, convinced that He had spent His entire night with other girls, accuses Krsna of wilfully trying to kill Her with His thoughtlessness. And in Her unrelenting, wounded pride She drives Him away. Throughout the next day the divine couple suffer separation from each other. That night, Krsna again approaches Radharani in a very humble and submissive mood. Removing His turban, He kneels before Her, places Her feet on His head, and utters the following famous words:

*smara-garala-khandanam mama sirasi mandanam*  
*dehi pada-pallavam udaram*  
*jvalati mayi daruno madana-kadananalo*  
*haratu tad-upahita-vikaram*

**“O Radha! Please ornament My head with the fresh lotus buds of Your feet. Those flower-feet will counteract Cupid’s poison — the love I feel in separation from You — and extinguish the harsh fire of amorous desires that rages within My heart.”**

Finally, encouraged by Her friends, Radha abandons Her pique, thus removing the obstacle to the divine couple’s union.

Intruding on Radha’s reverie, Rati speaks up, “Syamajiu! This laksa is undoubtedly splendid on Your feet. But when Krsna tries to pacify You and places Your feet upon His head, Your red footprints are especially magnificent on His black locks. Don’t You agree?” Srimati Radharani is somewhat startled by Rati’s boldness, but the image of Her footprints on Krsna’s head melts Her heart and brings a broad smile to Her lips. Krsna’s greatness, by which He creates and destroys universes with His unlimited potencies, is surely wonderful. But the greatness by which He becomes subservient to and dependent on the love of His pure devotees is more wonderful still.

Jayadeva Gosvami, while composing his famous Gita-govinda, hesitated to put into writing the verse just quoted (smara-garala- khandanam), thinking it unbefitting to depict the Supreme Lord’s subservience to a village girl. But when Jayadeva went away, Krsna came and personally rewrote, in His own hand, the verse Jayadeva had crossed out.

“Vrndavana’s parrots still sing of Krsna’s return to Nandagrama with red lac on His forehead,” Rati continues. “And in those songs the birds deride solemn moralists who refuse to worship Krsna due to such improprieties. Actually, Bakulamala told me that Syama-devi became so angry with Krsna—when at sunrise she saw His head and arms smudged with lac — that she refused to speak to Him for days.”

Krsna certainly cherishes Radha’s red footprints as the foremost of His ornaments. And because He loves them so, He places them not only on His head, but also upon His chest to show that Radha’s lotus feet are always in His heart. Whatever other marks and decorations Krsna wears are overshadowed by the presence of Krsna's favourite bodily adornment.

Kavi Karnapura invokes the protection of this lac upon us all:

“May the red lac on Radha’s lotus feet, lac that sticks on Hari’s chest and is more beautiful than even the sign of Srivatsa, the Kaustubha jewel, and the mark of the goddess of fortune, lac that shines like the rising sun prayed to by the darkness, or like a red lotus blossoming in the Yamuna, protect you all.”

After both soles have been painted, Rati-manjarl dries them using the edge of her veil as a fan. And when they are dry, she bends over and gently kisses Sri Radha’s lotus feet before placing them on the floor.

**Verse 44**

*kalavati natamsayoh pracura-kama-punjojjvalat-*  
*kalanidhi-muradvisah prakata-rasa-sambhavayoh*  
*bhrama-bhramara-jhankrtair matlhura-malli-malam muda*  
*kada tava tayoh samarpayati devi dasi-janah*

**“O artistic girl! When will this maidservant happily hang a sweet jasmine garland surrounded with humming bees on Your gracefully sloping shoulders, shoulders touched in the rasa dance by Krsna, who is a moon shining with amorous passion?”**

Commentary: Srimati Radharani’s bathing, dressing, and ornamentation are now complete; all that remains is to decorate Her shoulders with a jasmine garland. This is not a thick, knee-length, Vaijayanti garland like the one Krsna wears. It is made of tiny white aromatic flowers and hangs no lower than Radharani’s waist.

An open window has allowed bees to follow the garland’s sweet fragrance into the room. But it does not take them long to realise that the fragrance they are really after is not coming from the jasmine flowers, but from Radha’s lotus mouth. Drawn towards that sweet aroma, they swarm around Radha’s face and Rati has to constantly shoo them away. Rati hangs the garland over Radharani’s slender shoulders and says, “Tonight, when You are at the centre of the rasa dance with Krsna, He will drape His arm over Your shoulders and most likely break this delicate garland. But by then it will have served its purpose. And anyway, the snake-like arm of that passionate black moon is the most fitting garland for Your neck.”

Rati addresses Sri Radha as Kalavati (“artistic girl”) implying that Krsna depends on Radha for the fulfilment of His desires. Rati says, “The music of the rasa dance is made by many kinds of instruments, but instruments make music only if musicians play them. Otherwise they remain silent! Krsna is also like those instruments. To bring out the unlimited potential He has for amorous enjoyment, He requires a girl who is unlimitedly talented in the art of love. That Kalavati is You. And Krsna knows it. Every girl in Vraja knows it. And it will be proven at the rasa dance tonight.”

Sri Krsna is resplendent with divine passion, hut if He has no one with whom to share that passion, what will He do with it? Of course, from the perspective of spiritual truth (tattva), Krsna is self-satisfied and thus fulfils His own desires. But from the perspective of spiritual tastes (rasa), Krsna needs a lover to reciprocate His desire to he loved and a beloved whom He can love fully in return. Although He may reciprocate with many gopis in many ways, because none of them are equal to Him in transcendental qualities, He is always dependent on His energetic counterpart — Radha, and Radha alone — to satisfy Him completely.

Nonetheless, Radharani’s girlfriends each share a portion of Her artistic talents. Therefore, they too may be addressed as Kalavati, especially for their skills in decorating the charming forest groves filled with hanging vines by Yamuna’s shore, and for the incomparable services they render the divine couple in those kunjas.

**Verse 45**

*suryaya suryamani-nirmita-vedi-madhye*  
*mugdhangi bhavata ihali-kulair vrtayah*  
*argham samarpayitum utka-dhiyas tavarat*  
*sajjani kim sumukhi dasyati dasikeyam*

**“O girl with charming limbs! O girl with a beguiling face! Will this maidservant sit nearby and lovingly hand You the articles of worship as You, surrounded by Your friends, devotedly worship the sun god, who sits on an altar of suryamani jewels?”**

Commentary: T his verse ends the sequence of verses that describe Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s meditations on preparing Sri Radha for Her morning sojourn to Nandagrama. From verses forty-six through fifty-seven, the Gosvami jumps ahead to describe pastimes in the afternoon and evening. After verse fifty-seven, however, he again narrates pastimes that follow chronologically from this one.

Why present the pastimes out of sequence? Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami is living in the realm of transcendence, where time does not flow in a linear fashion from past to future but exists in the eternal present. Moreover, he is describing his personal ecstasies as they inspire him, and those ecstasies need not follow the expectations material time has imposed upon us.

Another example of an elevated soul narrating events out of chronological order is found in Srimad-Bhagavatam, wherein Sukadeva Gosvami, after describing the bewilderment of Brahma at the end of Krsna’s boyhood, begins the description of Krsna’s childhood with the killing of Dhenukasura. However, before going on to describe the killing of Pralamba, the sage’s ecstasy brings him back to narrate the chastisement of Kaliya, which again takes place during Krsna’s boyhood before the age of six. Since spiritual time, as mentioned above, exists in an eternal present, all of Krsna’s pastimes are concurrent. Therefore Sukadeva Gosvami’s lack of chronological consistency should not be taken as a fault, but rather as an indication of his perfected state of consciousness. The same may be said in the case of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami.

Before She leaves for Nandagrama, Radha worships Her family deity, the sun god. Both at Varsana and at Yavata the villagers perform their daily worship at various temples. The temples in these places should not be confused with the famous temple at Surya-kunda, which is acknowledged by all Vraja-vasis to be the sacred place of pilgrimage where Radharani goes, at least on Sundays, to offer extensive worship.

Why do the Vraja-vasis worship demigods? And does such worship exist also in Goloka? The first question can be answered by recalling that the lives of the Vraja-vasis resemble the lives of humans, who do in fact worship different forms of Bhagavan and the demigods. And to answer the second question, yes, this kind of worship exists in Goloka Vrndavana in its original form, where some residents, like Nanda Maharaja, worship incarnations of Krsna, and others, like Govardhana Malla, worship Durga-devi. In the Brhad-bhagavatamrta, Sanatana Gosvami explains that the demigods in Goloka are perfected souls who, like all of Krsna’s associates, eternally serve the Lord’s pastimes, but in the capacity of the Vraja-vasis’ worshipable deities.

If this verse is taken to be in sequence with the previous one, then Radha’s worship can be considered to be taking place at Her home, either in Varsana or Yavata. If it is seen in sequence with thenext verse, however, it can be considered that She is worshipping at Surya-kunda. But wherever the worship is taking place, Radha is sitting before an altar made of suryamani upon which stands the deity of the sun. Rati-manjari sits to Radha’s left, and to the left of Rati is a tray holding the items for worship: incense, flowers, lamp, and so on. Rati hands the items to Radha one by one, and after Radha offers them, Rati takes them back from Her. Meanwhile, friends like Lalita, Citra, and Tungavidya sing fitting songs.

Here Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami calls Radha by two names: Sumukhi (“fair-faced girl”) and Mugdhangi (“girl of enchanting limbs”). As Radha worships the sun god, She prays for Krsna’s welfare. Thus absorbed in thoughts of Krsna, Radha’s face looks exceedingly beautiful and serene, and therefore Dasa Gosvami calls her Sumukhi. Radha’s limbs reflect the beauty of Her face, and therefore the effect of Her bodily beauty is to enchant and bewilder anyone who sees Her. Thus he also calls Her Mugdhangi.

Srimati Radharani’s friends have known Her from Her very birth, but the sight of Her now startles them. All they can do is stare at Her and think, “I have never seen my friend look so beautiful!” The sun god is also baffled; in fact, it seems to Rati that he is looking at Radharani.

The Brahma-gayatri mantra declares that the sun god is a devotee of Radha, “(om) The personality within the sun (savitur) who illuminates the three worlds (bhur bhuvah svah), the Parambrahman (tat), worships the foremost (varenyam) potency (bhargo) of the Supreme Lord (devasya) \[by the name of Radha). Let us also worship Her in the way that he does (dhimahi dhiyo yo nah pracodayat)

Rati cannot tell whether the sun god is mesmerised by his wor- shipable Deity, Sri Radha, or whether from far away Sri Krsna is getting a better look at Radha through the sun, which is one of His eyes. Whatever the case may be, she is proud of her mistress’s beauty.

Sometimes, on their way to the temple of the sun god, Radha’s friends walk ahead of Her on the path. Mischievous Krsna, seeing His opportunity, suddenly appears and blocks Radha’s way, unbeknownstto Her friends. He grabs the edge of Radha’s sari and pulls, like a fisherman would pull on a net to retrieve his catch.

Momentarily surprised, Radha protests, “Please do not trouble Me here on the path. Can’t You see that I am a pious girl without protection?” But Krsna persistently tugs at Her garment, moving His eyebrows suggestively. Radha pleads with joined palms, “O hero of Gokula! Please do not cause Me further delay! O moon-faced one, I bow down before You again and again, but please let Me go.” And when Krsna still does not relent, hut instead advances silently towards Radha, who is now backed up against a kadamba tree, She implores Him pitiably, “O eternal one! Seeing You look at Me with such passion in this solitary place — I become afraid!”

Meanwhile, Radha’s friends have reached the temple and are making everything ready for worshipping the sun god, hut Radha has not arrived. Rupa-manjari stands at the doorway and looks back down the path. Radha is nowhere to be seen. Then Rupa hears the echo of Radha’s voice amongst the trees:

*cancala munca patancala-bhagam*  
*karavany adhuna bhaskara-yagam*

**“Libertine! Let go of the border of My garment. I must go now to perform a sacrifice for the sun god.”**

After a few moments Rupa goes back into the temple. “We should begin our worship without Radha," Rupa says. “She has already begun Her puja in a temple-grove along the way.” At first the gopis look at one another, perplexed, but then, once they also hear the distant echoes of their mistress's voice, they giggle and happily sit down to worship the sun.

**Verse 46**

*raja-pura-pati-rajnya ajnaya mistam annam*  
*bahu-vidham ati-yatnat svena pakvam varoru*  
*sapadi nija-sakhinam mad-vidhanam ca hastair*  
*madhumathana-nimittam kim tvaya sannidhapyam*

**“O girl with beautiful thighs! When will You employ the hands of friends like me to place before the killer of Madhu the many delicious foods You very carefully cooked on the order of Vraja’s queen?”**

Commentary: In Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s meditation it is afternoon and, as Rati-manjari, he is alone in the kitchen with Srimati Radharani. Mother Yasoda has just sent a message requesting Radha to cook Krsna’s supper. This opportunity to serve has brought Radha out of a coma of separation from Krsna and reawakened Her enthusiasm to live.

Rati and Radha, without ornaments or veils, stand side by side before the preparations cooking on the stove. Radhika is making Krsna’s favourite sweets: amrtakeli, piyusagranthi, and karpurakeli. Rati hands ingredients to her mistress as needed and from time to time keeps the fires in the ovens stoked with aloe wood. And as usual, she chats with Radha. It is her service.

In the heat of the kitchen Rati says, “Just a while ago it seemed like the fire of separation was going to consume Your body. Neither sandal paste nor moist lotus petals could cool You down. But now, when You have service to do for Krsna, You are tending to a dozen pots in this hot kitchen without even a drop of perspiration on Your brow. How amazing! Service to Krsna has extinguished the raging Madhu-fever burning up Your limbs.”

As Radha steps briskly towards a simmering pot, She brushes past Rati on the way. “O Varoru!” Rati continues. “Your body feels as cool as a sandalwood tree. Surely a certain black snake will want to wrap His coils around You in order to counteract the venom of kama that is scorching His limbs.”

Radha says nothing, moving expertly from one preparation to another, sometimes adding an ingredient, sometimes adjusting the flame. Yet Her ears are eager to hear Rati’s words of encouragement. And so it goes until the cooking is complete.

Radha divides what She has cooked into two parts: one for Yasoda in Nandagrama, and the other for Her late night meeting with Krsna at Govinda-sthali. She places the first portion into a large wooden basket and covers it with a cloth. She will entrust its delivery to Rati and Kasturi.

Now it is Radha’s turn to speak. Casually dressed in a thin sari, Her hair slightly dishevelled from the labour of cooking, Radha hands the basket to Kasturi. She then takes Rati’s hands in Her own and, standing face to face with her, says, “Unable to go to Nandagrama Myself, I entrust Krsna’s supper to you. Offer My repeated respects to the queen of Vraja and to the elder ladies of the court. You know My heart, Rati, so when You place these sweets before Krsna, it will be the same as if I were serving Him directly. I will be waiting here, but I will feel the same pleasure I would if I were there in Nandagrama."

Radharani embraces Rati, holding her tightly to Her bosom, and looks into her eyes. She utters not a word, yet She says so much. Rati is speechless; she has been accepted as Sri Radha’s envoy. Finally,Radha says, “Come back quickly and tell Me everything you saw and heard.” And with that She shoos the two girls out the door and stands watching until they have disappeared on the horizon.

In this verse Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has used the phrase “Your friends, such as myself.” The followers of Rupa and Raghunatha aspire to be accepted by Srimati Radharani as one of Her friends in waiting, a maidservant. Rupa Gosvami prays for this radha-dasya as follows:

*ha devi kaku-bhara-gadgadayadya vaca*  
*yace nipatya bhuvi dandavad udbhatartih*  
*asya prasadam abudhasya janasya krtva*  
*gandharvike nija-gane gananam vidhehi*

**“O Devi! In great distress I fall to the ground and offer You obeisances and prayers with a voice choked with emotion. O Gandharvika! Please bestow Your mercy on this pauper and count me amongst Your own companions.”**

**Verse 47**

*nitanna-mad-vidha-lalata-tate lalatam*  
*pritya pradaya mudita vraja-raja-rajni*  
*premna prasur iva bhavat-kusalasya prccham*  
*bhavye vidhasyati kada mayi tavakatvat*

**“O auspicious girl! When will I take the sweets You cooked to the queen of Vraja, who will place her forehead to mine as if she were my mother and enquire about Your well-being, knowing me to be Yours!”**

Commentary: Whether starting from Yavata or Varsana, the distance to Nandagrama is significant. Yet Rati-manjari routinely walks there in the morning and in the evening, in addition to an even longer walk to Govardhana and back during the day, and a walk — longer still — to the Yamuna and back at night. To walk such distances is simply not possible for humans. But Krsna and the gopis not only make walks like these daily, they also remain fresh enough to spend their nights dancing on the banks of the Yamuna. How is it possible? Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami supplies an answer:

*nyasya sviye hrdaya kamale sohyamana nigudham*  
*yantrakare vrajavana bhuva prapa krsna samipam*

**“Vraja-dhama made Radhika swiftly cross the huge distance. Thus, carried on the lotus of Vraja’s heart, She quickly reached the bank of the Yamuna."**

This verse describes Radha’s nocturnal journey from Yavata to Vamsivata for a rendezvous with Krsna. It is a long distance. Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami explains, however, that Vraja is a fully conscious entity, shaped like an open lotus, upon which Radha’s starting point and destination lie on different petals. Knowing Radharani’s intentions, and aware that time is of the essence, while Radha hurries along the paths of Vraja with Her friends, the petals of the lotus close together making a distance of five yojanas shrink to a thousand paces. The Gosvami makes a similar statement regarding Krsna’s trek to the meeting place on the same night as aforementioned.

It is late afternoon. On their walk to Nandagrama, Rati and Kasturi chat excitedly about their current mission and speculate as to where that evening’s meeting of the divine couple will take place. Will it be at Sanketa, Candra-sarovara, Govinda-sthali, or perhaps in Yavata itself?

Suddenly, by the grace of holy Vraja-dhama, they are at the gates of Nandagrama where a maidservant of Yasoda ushers them into the kitchen. There Rohini-devi oversees a bevy of cooks while moving between a dozen pots filled with steaming or bubbling preparations. She greets the two girls and directs them to place their basket of sweets on a table. At that very moment, Mother Yasoda enters the kitchen.

“O Rati!” she cries. “And Kasturi too!” As the entire kitchen staff turns to look, Yasoda unabashedly runs to the girls and embraces first Rati and then Kasturi, holding her forehead to theirs, gazing at their faces with tear-filled eyes, and repeatedly stroking their heads, braids, and backs.

Yasoda holds the girls’ hands and enquires, “Tell me, is Radhika well? When I see you two I see Her beautiful face, and when I hold your hands I feel like I am touching Her.” As Yasoda looks around, she asks, “Where did you put the sweets Radha cooked?”

Rati points to the table and says, “Over there, mother. Those are nectarean treats cooked by the hands of nectar personified, Sri Radha. They are guaranteed to be as therapeutic as they are delicious. By eating them, your son will never know disease, old age, or misfortune. That is why we call our princess Bhavya, auspicious girl.”

Yasoda bursts into tears of love at Rati’s words. She then embraces both girls at once, moistening their clothes with milk from her breasts. In Yasoda’s embrace, the two maidservants feel themselves submerged in the oceanic love of the universal mother. They feel as much Yasoda’s daughters as Radha is, and that Radha is as much Yasoda’s daughter as Krsna is her son. As Yasoda kisses Rati’s head she says, “Had fate given me Radha as a daughter-in-law, you girls would now be living in my house.”

**Verse 48**

*krsria-vaktrambujocchistam prasadam param adarat*  
*dattam dhanisthaya devi kim anesyami te ‘gratah*

**“O Queen! When will I affectionately place before You the remnants tasted by the lotus mouth of Lord Krsna, prasada given to me by Dhanistha?”**

Commentary: This and the following verse mention two kinds of remnants left by Krsna: that which Krsna chewed and then spat out, and that which Krsna left behind on His plate. Rati-manjari now speaks of the former. In the next verse she will speak of the latter.

After being embraced by Mother Yasoda, the two girls help serve supper, discreetly moving around the large table at which the male members of Nanda’s family are seated.When the time comes to serve the sweets, Yasoda-devi says, “Son! These laddus and pies were cooked by Kirtida’s daughter and brought here by Rati. Since they took great pains to serve You, please eat them all.”

But in the wake of such a public announcement, Rati feels too shy to serve. Yasoda therefore pulls Rad’s veil over her face, places her hands on Rad’s shoulders, leads her over to where Krsna is sitting, and says, “Put those sweets on His plate, dear.”

Krsna compliments each sweet as He tastes it. But when He comes to the manohara-laddu, He makes a wry face, spits it back onto His plate, and complains, “This was not properly cooked!" At the end of the meal, when the plates are collected, Yasoda’s maidservant, Dhanistha-gopi, saves this special remnant. Dhanistha knows that Krsna purposefully left it for Radharani, so she wraps it in a silken cloth. Later, as Rati is leaving for Yavata, Dhanistha gives her the prasada with the wink of an eye, and Rati ties it in the corner of her veil.

Meanwhile, Mother Yasoda has gathered a small portion of every preparation and packed it into the basket in which the girls had brought the sweets. Dhanistha mixes the food left on Krsna’s plate into the prasada in the basket, and the girls triumphantly return to their village.

But all is not well in Yavata. While the girls were away, Radha fainted, unable to tolerate being separated from Krsna.Many gopis had tried to revive Her with applications of camphor, sandalwood paste, and moist lotus petals, but none succeeded. Upon entering Radha’s quarters, Rati is shocked to see her beloved mistress lying motionless upon a couch, surrounded by gopis frantic from their unsuccessful efforts to revive Her. Before Rati can fall grief-stricken at Radha’s feet, Lalita catches her hand and says lovingly, “Steady! Control yourself,” and leads Rati to a seat by Srimati Radharani’s head.

Lalita-devi says, “Recount what you have seen at Nandagrama in Radhika’s ear.” Rati immediately leans over Radha’s left ear and describes everything that happened that evening, beginning with meeting Yasoda-devi. When she comes to the part where Krsna honours the sweets, Radha stirs, regally sits up, and looks at the gopis surrounding Her. Radha says to Lalita, “I dreamt that I was alone in a terrible desert, being scorched by a merciless sun. Then, all of a sudden, a shower of nectar entered My ears, cooled My being, and made Me feel happy."

Lalita rubs Radha’s back as she replies, “The nectar You heard was Rati-manjari recounting the events of Krsna's evening meal.” Radha places Her lotus feet on the floor, pats the couch beside Her, and says, “Rati! Sit here and tell Me more.”

Rati timidly sits beside Radha, and the other sakhis crowd around eager to hear. In a voice as sweet as a cuckoo’s at dusk, Rati relates how Nanda Maharaja lovingly greeted the gopas when they returned from the forest with the cows, how Yasoda sat Krsna in her lap, and how the hoy servants bathed Krsna before He sat down for supper with His elders and friends. “When Krsna and Balarama went to milk the cows,” she concluded, “I came back to bring You some of His remnants.”

As she speaks, Rati undoes the knot in her veil and then carefully distributes the manohara-laddu that Krsna had apparently rejected. The girls at once honour the remnants. Rati says to Sri Radha, “Krsna liked this preparation the best. He added the nectar of His lips to it and then spat it out on some false pretext so that I could bring it back to You.” While the other gopis chatter about the taste, Radha savours, with eyes tightly closed, the nectar left by Krsna’s lips.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu, while living in Puri, would relish Lord Jagannatha’s remnants with His devotees. On one occasion, stunned by the special taste of the maha-prasada, the Lord glorified those divine remnants to the servants of Lord Jagannatha. The Lord repeatedly said, *sukrti-labhya phela-lava*: “Only by great fortune may one come by a particle of the remnants of food offered to the Lord.” And when prompted Caitanya Mahaprabhu disclosed His mind further:

**“These are remnants of food that Krsna has turned to nectar by the touch of His lips. In fact, this prasada surpasses heavenly nectar. Even demigods such as Lord Brahma have difficulty obtaining it.**  
**Remnants left by Krsna are called phela. Anyone who receives even a small portion of those remnants must be considered most fortunate. Therefore, persons with ordinary good fortune cannot obtain such mercy. Only persons who have the full mercy of Krsna can receive His remnants.”**

Radharani opens Her eyes, looks at Rati and thinks, “This girl was just with Krsna; therefore Her fortune must be greater than Mine.” Radha's desires to connect with Krsna are boundless. She takes hold of Rati’s chin. “Let Me see your eyes,” She says. “Yes! They can only be so extraordinarily beautiful because they were recently gazing upon Krsna.” Radha's hands tremble and the hair on Her arms stands on end. As She looks deeper and deeper into Rati’s eyes, She sees the lavish dining hall of Nandagrama and Krsna seated to His father’s left. She sees Krsna being served manohara-laddu. She watches Him chew, smile, grimace, and then spit it out. Finally She sees Krsna look back at Her. Their eyes lock and, for a moment that stretches into eternity, They gaze at each other through the pure medium of Radha's maidservant.

**Verse 49**

*nana-vidhair amrta-sara-rasayanais taih*  
*krsna-prasada-militair iha bhojya-peyaih*  
*ha kunkumangi lalitadi-sakhi-vrta tvam*  
*yatnan maya kim u taram upabhojantya*

**“O girl whose limbs shine like vermilion! When will I carefully serve You, Lalita, and Your other friends varieties of ambrosial foods and nectar drinks mixed with the remnants of those which were directly tasted by Krsna?”**

Commentary: The gopis are sitting down for dinner. Since Radha’s husband, Abhimanyu, is absent, no one is present who could disturb a festival centred on Krsna. Only old Jatila is in the house, but she is so hard of hearing that she might as well be absent too. The girls have mixed the remnants from Krsna’s plate that Rati brought hack from Nandagrama with the food they cooked in the kitchen downstairs. Just as Ganges water imparts its transcendental qualities to any ordinary water it touches, the remnants of Krsna’s food transfer their potency to other foods with which they are mixed. Thus the girls are in bliss; they are not enjoying the flavours of a tasty meal, they are relishing the transcendental flavour of Krsna’s lips.

When Caitanya Mahaprabhu distributed Krsna’s remnants to His associates, their minds were struck with wonder at the uncommon sweetness and fragrance of the prasada. Caitanya Mahaprabhu then explained the cause for the prasada’s extraordinary potency. He said, “These ingredients — such as sugar, camphor, black pepper, cardamom, cloves, butter, spices, and liquorice — are all material. Everyone has tasted these material substances before.

“However,” the Lord continued, “having been relished by Sri Krsna, they now possess extraordinary flavours and uncommon fragrances. Just taste them and see the difference for yourselves. Apart from the taste, even the fragrance pleases the mind and makes one forget any other sweetness besides its own. Therefore, it is to be understood that the spiritual nectar of Krsna’s lips has mingled with these ordinary ingredients. That nectar is what has given them these transcendental qualities.” The Lord concluded, “Krsna’s lips possess a taste and aroma that are as uncommon as they are enchanting; indeed, the nectar of those lips makes one forget all else.”

While eating, the gopis also speak about Krsna and the nectar of His lips. Visakha-devi says, “By bringing us the nectar of Krsna’s lips, Rati-manjari has driven away Radha’s lamentation and increased the happiness of everyone. This same nectar is thoroughly relished by Krsna’s flute, and it makes the Vraja-vasis forget all other things.”

Radharani replies, “My dear friends! We have obtained this unsurpassed ambrosia — sweet nectar from Krsna’s lips — only after having performed heaps and heaps of pious activities.” After tasting another morsel, She adds, “Krsna is certainly increasing the desires of My tongue.”

At this, Radha becomes inspired by ecstatic emotions, Her gestures and facial expressions more animated than before. Still holding a lump of prasada in Her hand, She enthusiastically addresses the assembled gopis, “Friends! As Visakha has so rightly said, the characteristics of Krsna’s lips are quite mysterious. Indeed, those lips bring the whole world under their control. But allow Me to describe the special influence they have on women. We know personally how Krsna’s lips vanquish women’s dignity, piety, and patience. And, dare I say it — ” She pauses and leans forward, “ — they inspire madness in the mind. In short, Krsna’s lips increase greed in our tongues and thus attract them.”

The gopis giggle happily at Radha’s speech. As the sound of their amusement subsides, She lifts up Her handful of prasada and continues speaking, just above a whisper, “But I must disclose to you a paradoxical situation.” The gopis lean forward to hear. “Since Krsna is a man, it is not very extraordinary that the attraction of His lips disturbs the minds of women like us. But — ” She pauses once more for dramatic effect, causing Her friends to lean further forward, over their plates, before She goes on, “I am embarrassed to say that Krsna’s impudent lips are sometimes attractive even to His flute, who is male.” The gopis erupt into laugher, but Radha tries to speak over the din, “Even the male flute likes to drink the nectar of Krsna’s lips, thereby forgetting all other tastes.”

Rati laughs along with the rest of the gopis, whose noisy good cheer brings Jatila into the room. The aged and cantankerous gopi eyes the girls suspiciously from the doorway and then leaves, closing the door behind her.

In this verse Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami uses the name Kunkumangi (“a girl whose limbs shine like vermilion”) to address Sri Radha. Part of Radha’s regular beautification is to slightly tint and perfume Her limbs with kunkuma. But the gopis wiped all the kunkuma off Her limbs as they were trying to revive Her, so how can those limbs still shine red like vermilion! The answer is that the talk of Krsna’s lips has caused a surge of transcendental lust in Radha’s heart, lust that in turn has spread throughout Her body and manifest itself as a reddish hue emanating from Her limbs.

The girls all laugh at Radha’s joke, but that doesn’t stop them from teasing Her over the ardent desire for Krsna clearly visible on Her skin. Rati whispers to Radharani, “Kunkumangi! You had better control Yourself. Your passion for Krsna is advertising itself all over Your body and making You the target of Your girlfriends’ jokes.” Selfconscious and embarrassed, Sri Radha finally eats the food that has been waiting in Her hand, finishes the rest of Her meal, and leaves the table.

*saundaryananta-puraih kanaka-mani-sila-ghrsta-kasmira-gaurair*  
*angair angaih kiranti madhuratara-maha-kanti-sindhun anantan*  
*syama-premati-madhvi-mada-vikrti-vicitrakrtih sarva-cesta-*  
*madhuryair adbhutair vismita-manasi sadodetu radhesvari me*

**“May my queen, Radha, Her unlimitedly beautiful fair limbs anointed with kunkuma and decorated with jewels and gold, limbs which shower unlimited oceans of very sweet transcendental splendour, Her transcendental form bearing the wonderful symptoms of the sweet nectar of Her passionate transcendental love for dark-complexioned Krsna, appear in my heart, which is now astonished by the wonderful sweetness of Her every act.”**

**Verse 50**

*panaya vari madhuram nava-pataladi-*  
*karpura-vasitataram taralaksi dattva*  
*kale kada tava mayacamaniya-danta-*  
*kastadikam pranayatah param arpaniyam*

**“O restless-eyed one! When will I then lovingly offer You water, sweetly scented with fresh patala flowers and camphor, for rinsing Your mouth and a twig for brushing Your teeth?”**

Commentary: Srimati Radharani has finished Her meal, so Rati brings Her a jug with sweetly scented water. Meanwhile, the sakhis' maidservants do the same for them. Radha holds Her cupped hand over a golden bowl, cleanses Her mouth, and spits the rinse water into a separate spittoon. She then washes Her hands and dries them on a towel. All the while, Her eyes dart restlessly here and there. This restlessness is due in part to Her feeling embarrassed at being made fun of and in part due to the influence of love in separation from Krsna.

In his meditative trance, Dasa Gosvami says, “Your tranquil, love-filled eyes are the most beautiful things in creation. But when they move to and fro because of passionate love, their glory becomes indescribable. The creator simply did not make anything fit to be compared to Your eyes.”

“But then why do My friends laugh at Me?" Radha wonders.

Rati consoles Her, “Taralaksi! How else but by laughing can Your friends express their joy at the sweet splendour of Your roving eyes, a splendour otherwise inexpressible? Don’t be angry with them. They love You so much.”

Radha smiles at Her friends, leaves the room, and walks to Her bathroom, where Rati offers Her a soft twig for brushing Her teeth and more water to thoroughly wash Her hands. Alone in the bathroom the two girls exchange glances without saying anything. Rati shyly gazes down at Radharani’s feet, and Radha reaches out Her right hand to lovingly caress Rati’s cheek as if to say, “Thank you!" As they are returning to join the others, Rati remembers a song she learned from Rupa-manjari:

*disi disi racayantim sancaran-netra-laksmi-*  
*vilasita-khuralibhih khanjaritasya khelam*  
*hrdaya-madhupa-mallim ballavadhisa-sunor*  
*akhila-guna-gabhiram radhikam arcayami*

**“I worship Sri Radhika, who, with the splendid beauty of Her restless eyes, plays as khanjana birds do, moving in every direction, who is the malli flower that attracts the bumblebee of the prince of Vraja’s heart, and who is deeply filled with all transcendental virtues.”**

**Verse 51**

*bhojanasya samaye tava yatnad*  
*devi dhupa-nivahan vara-gandhan*  
*vijanadyam api tat-ksana-yogyam*  
*ha kada pranayatah pranayami*

**“O Goddess! When, with great love and attention, will I light an abundance of aromatic incense, fan You, and perform other suitable services as You take Your meal?”**

Commentary: In verse forty-five, due to ecstatic absorption, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami jumped ahead in the chronological sequence of Radha’s daily activities; in this verse, for the same reason, he steps back. By describing Radha brushing Her teeth in the bathroom, Dasa Gosvami had already moved on from the scene of Radha’s evening meal. Now he returns to thoughts of the dinner and again relishes serving Radha while She eats.

Two essential ingredients of devotional service are mentioned in this verse: attention (yama) and affection (pranaya). Only when devotional service is performed attentively can it be free of offence. And only after that attentiveness becomes spontaneous can the attitude of loving service mature. Therefore devotees must overcome the obstacle of inattention (pramada). This is done by fixing one’s vows, seeking the company of advanced devotees, and following the etiquette of Vaisnava culture.

Thakura Bhaktivinoda names three causes of inattention: apathy, laziness, and distraction. All three are born from material attachment. To develop spontaneous, transcendental attachment in devotional service, devotees must make a special effort to be attentive to the details of their services, especially in chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra. By this serious effort, devotees are gradually able to serve with the consciousness requested of them by Krsna Himself, *ya me bhaktya prayacchati*: “Offer things to Me with love and devotion.” On the other hand, if devotees do not seriously endeavour to develop attentiveness, their service and chanting remain offensive and simply breed more bad habits. In such a sorry state, one cannot be fit for remembering the pastimes of the Lord.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, however, lives in the world of love, and for him attention to detail is spontaneous. As Rati-manjari, he knows which flavour incense Radha prefers, how She likes to be fanned, and Her other preferences during meals. Rati is the personification of love, and that is why Srimati Radharani keeps this maidservant so close at hand and entrusts her with so many confidential services.

Moreover, Rati takes the initiative to perfect and increase her services to Radha. For example, knowing that there is always a need for good singers during the nocturnal rasa dances, Rati decides that she wants to learn how to please the divine couple by that particular service. Since no one has a sweeter voice than Visakha-devi, Rati humbly approaches her and begs, “Please teach me the art of singing!”

Visakha is always helpful and friendly to the maidservants, but still, she wants to know more and so she asks, “Why do you want to improve your already lovely singing style?”

Rati explains, “I hope that Radha, Krsna, and Their friends — such as you — will thus be pleased to give me many necklaces of gold and jewels as a reward.”

Why would Rati want to be rewarded with jewellery? She does not. Speaking in the indirect language of the gopis, she means to say, “I hope that Radha, Krsna, and Their friends — such as you — will be pleased to reward me with many ornaments of ecstatic love for Sri Radha. That is all.”

By following Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s teachings and example, devotees can gradually imbibe his mood of attentive, loving service, which is the legacy bequeathed to every follower of Rupa Gosvami. The author of the Sri Caitanya-caritamrta reminds us of this eternal truth at the conclusion of every chapter:

*sri-rupa-raghunatha-pade yara asa*  
*caitanya-caritamrta kahe krsnadasa*

**“Praying at the lotus feet of Sri Rupa and Sri Raghunatha, always desiring their mercy, I, Krsnadasa, narrate Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, following in their footsteps.”**

**Verse 52**

*karpura-pura-paripurita-naga-valli-*  
*parnadi-puga-parikalpita-vitikam te*  
*vaktrambuje madhura-gatri muda kadaham*  
*protphulla-roma-nikaraih param arpayami*

**“O sweet-limbed girl! When will the hairs of my body stand on end in ecstasy as I place a betel leaf filled with betel nuts and camphor into Your lotus mouth?”**

Commentary: After supper the gopis gather around Radha and, in the way of young girls, speak about the enchanter of their hearts. Since every gopi’s beloved is the self-same prince of Vraja, they always and only speak of Krsna. How is it possible that many women can share the same man and yet not have a trace of envy or animosity towards one another? The answer to this question lies in understanding spiritual love and how it differs from the so-called love in the material world, which is more accurately known as lust. Consider the following definition of both kinds of love given by Kaviraja Gosvami:

*atmendriya-priu-vancha— tare bali ‘kama’*  
*krsnendriya-priti-iccha dhare ‘prema’ nama*

**“The desire to gratify one’s own senses is kama \[lust\], hut the desire to please the senses of Lord Krsna is prema\[love\].”**

Because the gopis have completely given up all desire to satisfy their own senses in order that they might satisfy the senses of Krsna, there are neither conflicting desires nor points of contention amongst them. Indeed, because they all want the same thing — Krsna’s happiness — they are in perfect harmony and thus are free from any competitive feelings. And of course this selfless, loving sentiment reaches its summit in Srimati Radharani.

The girls in Radha’s quarters are all Her dear friends who know that Her love for Krsna is greater than anyone else’s, and they worship Her accordingly. While sitting together they take the opportunity to excavate a few jewels of Radha’s consummate love. One gopi asks, “O Radha! How can You continue to love Krsna? You know that at any moment He may be unfaithful to You.”

As She sits upon a jewel-studded throne, Radha taps the ringed fingers of Her right hand on the armrest and says with a smile, “I am but a maidservant of Krsna, who is the embodiment of transcendental happiness and mellows. He may embrace Me or neglect Me, but He will always be the Lord of My life.”

Another gopi objects, "But Devi! How long can a person tolerate being a victim of such a two-faced lover?”

Unperturbed, Radha replies, "My dear friend! Long ago I made a decision within My mind. Just listen! Whether He gives Me happiness by showing Me affection, or kills Me with unhappiness by withholding the same, Krsna is the Lord of My life, forever.”

Just as another gopi is about to speak, Radharani continues, “Sometimes Krsna becomes controlled by Me, mind and body, and manifests My good fortune. Sometimes He indulges in loving affairs with other women just in front of Me to give distress to My mind. Nevertheless, He is still the Lord of My life.”

Raising her hand to get Radha’s attention, a fourth gopi says, “But how can Your soft heart tolerate such distress?”

With an angelic smile, Radharani replies, “Krsna’s happiness is the goal of My life. If He feels great happiness in giving Me distress, that distress is My greatest happiness.” Radha stops speaking and the room gets very quiet. The silence is thick, caused not by the absence of voices speaking, but rather by the profundity of what Radha has said.

Tears gather in Sri Radha’s eyes as She continues in a soft voice that trembles with emotion, “If Krsna, at tracted by the beauty of some other woman, wants to enjoy with her and is unhappy because He cannot have her, I fall down at her feet, catch her hand, and bring her to Krsna in order to engage her for His happiness. If a gopi envious of Me satisfies Krsna and Krsna desires her, I shall not hesitate to go to her house and become her maidservant, for then My happiness will be awakened.

“My dear friends!” Radha says with emphasis. “Try to understand that Krsna is My life and soul, indeed the very life of My life. I therefore keep Him always in My heart and try to please Him by rendering service — devotional service, the home of happiness and the only thing sweeter than direct union with Him. That is My constant meditation!”

“O sweet one!” a soft voice interrupts. It is Rati-manjari, standing to the left of Radha’s seat with betel mouth-freshener on a gold plate. She moves the plate closer to Radha and says, “Please smell this betel. It is especially good.”

Radharani is about to ignore Rati's request and continue Her conversation when She notices the aroma wafting from the plate beside Her. This is no ordinary betel. This betel is mixed with the remnants of Krsna’s chewed betel sent by Dhanistha and is thus sweeter than nectar. Radha’s tongue refuses to speak any further — it wants to relish the taste of what Rati is offering. With a wink, Radha opens Her lotus mouth slightly. Once Rati has fed Her the betel, Radha closes Her mouth — and Her eyes.

*krsna ye khaya tambula, kahe tara nahi mula,*  
*tahe ara dambha-paripati*  
*tara yeba udgara, tare kaya ‘amrta-sara,'*  
*gopira mukha kare ‘alabati’*

**“The betel chewed by Krsna is priceless, and the remnants of such chewed betel from His mouth are said to be the essence of nectar. When the gopis accept these remnants, their mouths become His spittoons.”**

**Verse 53**

*aratrikena bhavatim kim u devi devim*  
*nirmanchayisyatitaram lalita pramodat*  
*anydlayas ca nava-mangala-gana-puspaih*  
*pranarbudair api kacair api dasikeyam*

**“O Goddess! Beloved of Krsna! While Lalita joyfully performs the aratrika ceremony, offering You items like a ghee lamp, and while the others worship You with new, auspicious songs and flowers, may this maidservant, to whom You are dearer than billions of lives, worship You with the hair at the end of her opened braid?”**

Commentary: Radha has completed the evening’s lessons. Who can know more than She does about love? As love of Godhead personified, She is more knowledgeable on the subject than anyone else. She instructs not only Her friends, not only the world, She instructs Krsna Himself, who has therefore awarded Her the distinguished title “guru of love."

*radhikara prema—guru, ami — sisya nata*  
*sada ama nana nrtye nacaya udbhata*

**“The love of Radhika is My teacher, and I am Her dancing pupil. Her prema makes Me dance various novel dances.”**

Once Krsna saw the beauty of His own reflection in a mirror-like pillar and His mind became bewildered. He then desired to enjoy His own form in the way Srimati Radharani does.

*aparikalita-purvah kas camatkara-kari*  
*sphurati mama gariyan esa madhurya-purah*  
*ayam aham api hanta preksya yam lubdha-cetah*  
*sarabhasam upabhoktum kamaye radhikeva*

**“Who manifests an abundance of sweetness greater than Mine, which has never been experienced before and which causes wonder to all? Alas, I Myself, My mind bewildered upon seeing this beauty, impetuously desire to enjoy it like Srimati Radharani.”**

To better understand Radha’s mentality, Krsna once disguised Himself as a demigoddess and appeared before Radharani as She was conversing with Her friends in a courtyard of Her husband’s home in Yavata. In perfect disguise, Krsna severely challenged Radha’s love for Him, even going so far as to defame Himself in the process. At the conclusion of Their talks, He was fully decorated with the touchstone ornaments of Radha’s wisdom. This wonderful conversation is described by Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura in his Prema-samputa.

But as hard as Krsna tried to put Radha’s wisdom into practice, He met with limited success. He was unable to completely emulate Her loving mood. For example, Vrnda-devi once reported that Krsna was trying to dance to the tune of Radha’s love under the tutelage of Radha's own image as it revealed itself in every tree and creeper of Radha-kunda. After a considerable attempt to understand and emulate Radha’s love, Krsna became as adept as He could from the position of love’s object. He then concluded that it would only be possible to proceed further if He were to switch roles with Radha and become love’s subject instead. Thus He appeared as Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, who is Krsna in the mood of Srimati Radharani.

In the form of His own devotee, richly endowed with Radha’s emotions, Krsna was thus able to “understand the glory of Radharani’s love, the wonderful qualities in Him that She alone relishes through Her love, and the happiness She feels when She realises the sweetness of His love.” In this way Krsna was able to realise the teachings of His prema-guru, Sri Radha, and become the supreme student of love (prema-sisya).

After Radha’s open confession to Her friends that Krsna sometimes pursues other girls, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami calls Radha “Devi Devi.” Why?

Rati tells Srimati Radharani, “O Radha! Say what You like, but we all know that Krsna is not attracted to anyone but You.”

“Why do you say that, Rati?” Radha replies to Her maidservant with a smile.

Rati is ready with her answer, “Because You are the most beautiful girl there is (devi), and because You alone are the perfect abode of His love sports (devi).”

Radha baits Rati a little further, “Then why does Krsna sometimes leave Me for another?”

Again Rati doesn’t lose a moment, “Only because He feels obligated to reciprocate with Your rivals, not because He is spontaneously attracted to them. You’ve said so Yourself:

*sanketagam api vidhaya mad-eka-tano*  
*mam najagama yad ihabhavad antarayah*  
*ruddhah kayacid anurodha-vasat sa reme*  
*mad-duhkha-cintana-davardita eva ratrim*

**‘“If Krsna does not arrive at the meeting place, He must have met with some obstacle. Though His mind is fixed on Me, still He may feel obliged to enjoy with another gopi who stopped Him on the way. But He will not feel happy with Her; just the opposite, He will burn in the forest fire of misery the whole night.’**

“But Devi, look!” continues Rati. “Lalita is about to offer arati, which will no doubt remove even the slightest chance of an obstacle to Your meeting with Krsna tonight.”

Indeed, the conch shell sounds and the hell rings. And because Lalita is the senior gopi, she stands to Radha’s right while offering Her the articles of worship: incense, lamp, scented water, cloth, flowers, and yak-tail whisk. These are the items of worship generally offered to deities or respectable persons, and by doing so, the material elements offered are purified, as are the sense objects and the sense organs. More significantly, arati symbolises offering oneself to the Lord. Most significantly, however, the gopis’ offering of arati is meant to petition the elements and senses — gross and subtle — to remove any obstacles that may stand in the way of Radha’s scheduled meeting with Krsna. Because this worship is done before (a) the night (ratri) of the meeting, it is called arati.

While Lalita offers the articles one by one, the gopis offer Radha flowers, sing songs, call out “Jaya! Jaya!” and do the ulu-dhvani. Meanwhile, Jatila wonders what the commotion is all about. She concludes that the girls must be worshipping some demigod to ensure that ghosts or evil spirits do not disturb their sleep.

The gopis offer flowers to Radha as a symbol of self-surrender. They are offering their lives, their very existence, in service to Radharani, and through Her to Krsna. Radharani looks around the room for Rati and asks, “Aren’t you going to offer a flower?”

Rati is standing nearby waving the hair at the end of her opened braid as if it were a flower. “Devi!” she replies. “This is my offering to You.”

Radha turns Her head slightly and enquires, “But what does it mean?"

Rati answers, “The blackness of my hair is Krsna, and I am offering Him to You.”

Radha smiles and asks, “Does it mean anything else?”

Rati becomes emotional as she says, “You know everything, but still You ask. Listen, Devi! I will tell You what is in my heart. Just as Your loving thoughts of Krsna appear from Your head in the form of fine hair, my love for You has sprouted from me as the hair in my braid. I love You a billion times more than my very own life, and I am offering that love to You.”

**Verse 54**

*ali-kulena lalita-pramukhena sardham*  
*atanvati tvam iha nirbhara-narma-gosthim*  
*mat-pani-kalpita-manohara-keli-talpam*  
*abhusayisyasi kada svapanena devi*

**“O beautiful girl! When, after eloquently joking with Lalita and Your other friends, will You decorate with dreams the charming pastime-bed I made with my own hands?”**

Commentary: Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami refers to one of the eight activities by which the gopis please Krsna: their joking words (narma-gosthim). Humour plays an important role in Krsna’s pastimes. The cowherd boys, for instance, are also famous for the humorous and sometimes nonsensical talks with which they entertain Krsna. Amongst the boys, Madhumangala is especially well known for this. For example, Radha’s presence in the kitchen at Nandagrama sometimes distracts Krsna from eating breakfast. Mother Yasoda then complains that He is not eating. At such times, Madhu places an arm around his friend and says, “Mother, don’t worry that Krsna does not eat much. Just give what He doesn’t eat to me, and I will nourish Him simply by my embrace. In that way He will become strong!”

But the humorous talks described in this verse are of a different nature. Radharani sits at ease in Yavata, speaking casually but confidentially with Her very dear girlfriends like Lalita, Citra, and Tungavidya. Naturally they talk only of Krsna. But to increase the joy of these intimate topics they speak in riddles with subtle innuendos and clever humour. The gopis are expert at making golden earrings out of joking words— fashioning verbal ornaments that are very pleasing to the ears. And according to their natures, the gopis' humour is mild, sharp, or somewhere in-between. Of all the gopis, Radha is the most accomplished in decorating Her friends with the ornaments of witty words and — most importantly — in crowning Krsna with them. But despite their mistress’s expertise, the damsels of Vraja take the greatest pleasure in recalling Krsna’s joking words, words spoken with His deep voice rumbling like thunder and illuminated by double meanings designed to increase the desires of the gopis hearts through the medium of their ears.

One day, Krsna and Radha displayed Their verbal savvy in a quick-witted duel of words.

Krsna began, “Your incomparable qualities, My dear Radha, eclipse even those of the goddess of fortune, who gave up her pride and became Your follower.”

Radha replied, “But Laksmi is Your wife!”

Krsna said, “Certainly! And that is why You are that Sri!”

“But how can a cowherd girl be the goddess of fortune?” Radha objected.

Krsna explained, “If I am the husband of both the gopis and of Laksmi, then You must all be goddesses of fortune!”

Radha laughed, “Why would fickle Laksmi give up her divine prowess to become a human girl?”

Krsna replied, “In order to attain Your unparalleled beauty — and then offer it to Me.”

Radha points to some female deer nearby, “They are also Your dear ones. Are they goddesses of fortune too?” Krsna makes a wry face and Radha continues, “And since You love the Yamuna, is she also Laksmi? Or because she is black, perhaps she is Your expansion, and Your affection for her is yet another example of Your narcissism?”

Rati goes to the bedroom to make Sri Radha’s bed while the girls continue their conversation. Lalita quips, “O Radha! Take time to ornament Yourself properly before You leave tonight. In haste, You recently went to meet Krsna with Your necklace in Your braid, Your crown on Your breasts, mascara on Your arms, and musk perfume around Your eyes. What a sight You were!” Recalling how bewildered Radha was that day, the girls exchange amused glances, and a few giggle under their breath.

From the curved bow of Her raised eyebrows, Radha shoots a look at Lalita that says, “What makes you think I want to meet Krsna at all tonight? If you want to see Him, then go ahead. Don’t wait for Me — ”

Visakha interjects, “Don’t be cross, Hari-priya. We just thought Krsna might be on Your mind. As I arrived tonight, jatila told me how strangely You had been behaving. She said You were continually sighing, You were barely breathing, and You were staring into space with crooked eyes. And when she asked You for some black sesame (krsnatila), You went into a trembling fit.”

The gopis continue their light-hearted conversation, all the while expertly stoking the embers of Radha’s love for Krsna. Within a short span of time, Sri Radha displays a wide range of ecstatic emotions from anger to indifference, finally arriving at great longing.

Just then Rati returns. As soon as a break in the conversation comes, she announces, “Devi! This evening You have a long journey ahead of You, and an even longer night of enjoyment at Your destination. Please, rest now so that You’ll have the strength You need.”

Radha acquiesces, rising gracefully and leaving for Her bedroom followed by Rati and Rupa. At the doorway She turns and, in a voice filled with humility, pleads, “Dear friends! Please bless Me so that tonight I may become a bumblebee on Krsna’s forest garland.’’

Taking Radharani by the hand, Rati leads Her to the bedroom, where she says, “I have prepared this pastime-bed. Please decorate it with Your dreams."

The room is lit by a single lamp and scented with aguru incense. The sheets are fresh, cool, and soothing to the touch. Radha lies down, places Her head on the pillow, and whispers, “How is this a pastime-bed when I am here alone?”

Rati answers, “Wherever You are, Syama is also there.”

Radha opens Her sleepy eyes and says, “Do you think so?”

Rati speaks softly, “Close Your eyes and You will see Him.”

Srimati Radharani closes Her eyes. It is just as Rati said it would be. Radha is at once transported to a grove by the Yamuna’s shore where Krsna is waiting for Her. His bodily lustre resembles fresh lotus flowers, His smile is sweeter than honey, and His eagerness for Radha is as sure as the movements of the sun. Krsna’s voice is like a feast for Sri Radha’s ears; His nectarean words are like pillows of soft, cloud-white curds, cooked golden in the ghee of love, sweetened with the honey of His smile, topped with the icing of jokes, and spiced with the camphor of metaphor, alliteration, and other literary ornaments. And although this oral banquet delights the world, curbs the nectar-ocean’s pride, and cools the gopis’ amorous torment, in Radha it produces arrogance. She relishes Krsna’s joking words, but conceals all signs of Her ecstasy and looks at Him askance. With an air of disdain She turns to leave, but Krsna catches the end of Her sari and says: “Wicked girl! Where are You going? Who do You think You are to ignore Me like this?”

Rati can understand the events of Radha’s dream by reading Her facial expressions and bodily movements. Upon rising, Radha will think that what She saw while asleep was just dream, but it was real. In an unmanifest phase, Radha’s and Krsna’s meeting decorates Her bed, transforming it into a place of pastimes, keli-talpam.

**Verse 55**

*samvahayisyati padau tava kinkariyam*  
*ha rupa-manjarir asau ca karambuje dve*  
*yasmin manojna-hrdaye sadaye 'nayoh kim*  
*sriman bhavisyatitaram subha-vasarah sah*

**“O girl with a beautiful heart! O merciful one! Will that auspicious day come when this maidservant massages Your two lotus feet as Rupa-manjari massages Your two lotus hands?”**

Commentary: Again Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami calls Radharani by two names: Manojna-hrdaya (“girl with a beautiful heart”) and Sadaya (“merciful one”). Radha is Manojna because she knows (jna) what is on Rati’s mind (manah). Thus, by lying down upon the bed She indicates that Rati may massage Her lotus feet. This confidential service is reserved for Radha’s closest maidservants, with whom there is not even a speck of formality and from whom Radha never hesitates to request anything.

Usually Rupa-manjari massages Radha’s lotus feet and limbs when Radha is fatigued from walking, when She plays dice with Krsna, when Her limbs are burning with passion, or when She is resting with Krsna in a grove.

*kunje prasuna-kula-kalpita-keli-talpe*  
*samvistayor madhura-narma-vilasa-bhajoh*  
*loka-trayabharanayos caranambujani*  
*samvahayisyati kada yuvayor jano ‘yam*

**“When, as You, the two ornaments of the three worlds, recline on a pastime bed of flowers and exchange sweet joking words, will this person \[Rupa-manjari\] massage Your lotus feet?”**

Now Rati is being granted Rupa-manjari’s service, but before accepting it she gazes at Sri Rupa for permission. Rupa and Rati are close friends in Krsna’s pastimes, as they are in the pastimes of Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Rupa’s smile and the look in her eyes tell Rati, “Yes, of course. Radharani knew what was on your mind. Please, carefully serve Her lotus feet.”

Because they are Radha’s friends as well as Her maidservants, Rati and Rupa don’t hesitate to climb onto the bed with Her. Just as Govinda stepped over Lord Caitanya’s body for the purpose of serving Him, they too will transgress the rules of etiquette in the greater interest of Sri Radha. Softly, Rati massages Radha’s feet as Rupa gently rubs Radha’s hands. As Radha drifts off to sleep, Rati prays to Her, “Merciful girl! By giving me this service You have accepted me as Your maidservant. This kindness is but a feature of Your beautiful heart, for which I have nothing to give in return other than myself. O Sadaya! I am Yours.”

Looking up at Rupa-manjari with grateful eyes that say, “Thank you,” Rati puts her very being into the service she has just received by the grace of her dearmost, well-wishing friend. Rati thinks, “I am eternally indebted to Sri Rupa.” Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has elsewhere voiced his own feelings about Srila Rupa Gosvami, and through those feelings true rupanuga Vaisnavas may know how obliged they also are to Sri Rupa.

*adadanas trnam dantair idam yace punah punah*  
*srimad-rupa-padambhoja-rajo 'ham syam bhave bhave*

**“Taking a blade of grass between my teeth, I repeatedly beg that birth after birth I may be the dust of Srila Rupa Gosvami’s lotus feet.”**

**Verse 56**

*tavodgirnam bhojyam sumukhi kila kallola-salilam*  
*tatha padambhojamrtam iha maya bhakti-lataya*  
*ayi premna sardham pranayi-jana-vargair bahu-vidhai*  
*raho labdhavyam kim pracuratara-bhagyodaya-balaih*

**“O fair-faced girl! On the strength of some good fortune will I, this vine of fidelity, attain the remnants of food You have chewed, the mouthwash You have spit out, and the waves of ambrosial water that have washed Your lotus feet — and then share those priceless treasures with Your affectionate friends?”**

Commentary: Those with impure hearts will be unable to understand Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s eagerness to perform menial service for Sri Radha and his hunger for any morsel of Her remnants. Indeed, materialists consider such a mentality to be the sure sign of someone suffering from a severe loss of dignity and self-esteem. But Krsna's internal energy (svarupa-sakti) can transform such materially conditioned thinking into pure Krsna consciousness, in which one can fully appreciate Dasa Gosvami’s humble desires. Every living being is eternally Krsna’s servant, jivera ‘svarupa’ haya — krsnera ‘nitya-dasa. And when that service attitude has been fully reawakened, it becomes a devotee’s very source of sustenance. Such fortunate devotees hanker for Radha’s remnants in the same way Rati-manjari does.

The manjaris are living embodiments of pure devotional service; as such, there is nothing the divine couple could request that the manjaris would consider too lowly or trivial. Rati-manjari is a vine of devotion, whose flowers and fruits of ecstasy depend completely upon constant nourishment from the water of service rendered. If she cannot serve, she feels miserable and neglected, like a vine that shrivels up without water. Prabodhananda Sarasvati describes the manjaris’ service attitude, *radha-padabja-sevanya-sprha-kala-trayojjhitam*: “In all three phases of time (past, present, and future) the manjaris have no desire other than to serve Sri Radha’s lotus feet.”

Rati-manjari now requests Sri Radha, “By good fortune I managed to collect some of Your remnants during dinner. May I honour them in the company of Your other maidservants?"

Radha asks, “What remnants did you collect?”

Rati lists them, “There were remnants of Your food, Your mouthwash, and Your foot bath.”

Srimati Radharani doesn’t say anything. Her smile is Her consent. Thus at some convenient time, perhaps when Radha and Her close friends are resting, the maidservants will retreat to a private place and serve each other Radha’s remnants, at times lovingly quarrelling over who gets what.

The name Sumukhi, “fair-faced girl,” is significant. Radha is eating Krsna’s remnants, which means that the nectar of Krsna’s lips (adhara-amrta) becomes mixed with the nectar of Radha’s lips. The prefix su is an adjunct that enhances any word it precedes. As Sumukhi, whatever Radha eats — even Krsna’s remnants — is enhanced. Persons fortunate enough to honour Sri Radha’s remnants get a taste of the complete Absolute Truth. The first verse of Srimad-Bhagavatam implies meditation on this taste with the words satyam param dhimahi.

It is said that Krsna’s remnants, maha-prasada, when honoured by a devotee, are elevated to the stature of maha-maha-prasada. One can just imagine, then, the potency of the remnants of the foremost devotee, Srimati Radharani. Therefore Rati-manjari says, “By the strength of some good fortune I have obtained Your maha-maha-prasada.”

A friend of Sri Radha’s named Malli-devi, a leader of the girls descended from the uncivilised mountain tribe known as the Pulindas, appeared during the time of Lord Caitanya as the uncle of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami known as Kalidasa. Throughout life, even in old age, Kalidasa would always try to eat the remnants of food left by Vaisnavas, as a result of which Caitanya Mahaprabhu favoured him with supreme mercy. In narrating that pastime, Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami advises those devotees serious about achieving perfection to follow in the footsteps of Kalidasa.

*tate ‘vaisnavera jhuta’ khao chadi' ghrna-laja*  
*yaha haite paiba nija vanchita saba kaja*

**“Therefore, giving up hatred and hesitation, try to eat the remnants of the food of Vaisnavas, for you will thus be able to achieve your desired goal of life.”**

Radha asks, “Is there something you want to achieve by taking these remnants?”

With a sweet smile, Rati answers, “Yes!”

Curious, Radha enquires further, “Well, what is it you desire?”

Rati answers, “To always be Your dasi."

**Verse 57**

*bhojartavasare devi snehena sva-mukhambujat*  
*mahyam tvad-gata-cittayai kim sudhas tvam pradasyasi*

**“O Queen! While You eat Your meal, when will You take a nee-tarean morsel from Your own lotus mouth and affectionately give it to me, whose heart has gone to You?”**

Commentary: Religiously honouring the remnants of the Vaisnavas eventually enabled Kalidasa to receive the remnants of Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Similarly, Rati-manjari hopes that by the potency of Radha’s remnants she may he blessed with remnants still more intimate. Because Radha is a desire tree of love, She satisfies Her servants in ways they cannot even imagine; indeed, the fulfilment of Rati’s supreme desire will he seen in verse ninety-three.

After revealing her purpose for honouring Radha’s prasada in the previous verse, Rati has more to say.

Rati says, “But I have another desire.”

Nodding Her head in consent, Radha says, “Tell Me what it is.” Rati replies, “At Your next meal, please take some of the food You are chewing and give it to me directly.”Radha opens Her eyes wide in surprise, but before She can object, Rati explains, “Devi! You need not be shy before Your friends. They all know that I have given my heart to You and have no separate interest other than to serve You. In that sense we are one and the same. So if You eat by using Your mouth or by using mine, what is the difference?”

With the slightest nod of Her head, Radha acknowledges Her maidservant’s request. With satisfaction, Rati thinks, “It is only a question of time.”

Greed (lobha), one of the gates leading to hell, when used in the service of the Lord becomes the key to the gates of Vraja. Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami is unlimitedly greedy to be accepted as Radharani’s servant. By reading Dasa Gosvami’s aspirations, practising devotees— under the guidance of a qualified spiritual master—can cultivate the shadow of transcendental greed, and when liberated, awaken transcendental greed itself.

Some days later at the conclusion of supper, Rati comes to take Radha’s plate away. So that others cannot see, Radharani discreetly removes a portion of Krsna’s remnants from Her mouth and puts them back onto the plate. She doesn’t even look at Rati, but Rati knows for whom that maha-maha-prasada is meant. As Rati takes the plate into the kitchen, she scoops the remnants into her right hand and steps out onto a balcony into the fresh night air. Leaning happily against the wall, she places the mixture into her mouth. It came from the lotus mouth of Sumukhi, so it is indescribably delicious.

**Verse 58**

*api bata rasavatyah siddhaye madhavasya*  
*vraja-pati-puram udyad-roma-roma vrajanti*  
*skhalita-gatir udancat-svanta-saukhyena kim me*  
*kvacid api nayanabhyam lapsyase svamini tvam*

**“O mistress! Will my eyes someday attain a vision of You as You walk to the town of Vraja’s king to cook for Madhava — the hairs on Your body standing on end and Your gait faltering, all because of the happiness rising in Your heart?”**

Commentary: Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami here returns to the sequence of events he departed from with verse forty-five. Just as Radharani’s morning ablutions are finished, a gopi named Hiranyangi arrives to tell Her about Krsna’s morning activities in Nandagrama. They learn from her account that after Krsna was fully dressed, Nanda Maharaja asked Him to give a thousand cows in charity to the brahmanas. Krsna obediently performed acamana, sat down in meditation, and distributed the ornamented cows.

Nanda Maharaja’s celestial wealth is proof that the goddess of fortune resides in his city. Since she is never separated from her husband, Narayana Himself must also be residing there. For that reason Dasa Gosvami refers to Krsna as Madhava; He is the original Narayana and the husband (dhava) of the goddess of fortune (ma).

As Radha is drinking the nectar of Krsna’s pastimes, Kundalata arrives from Nandagrama on the order of Mother Yasoda. Rati stands behind Radharani as Kundalata says, “Dear friend! Please call Your friends and come to Nanda’s home at once. Since the day Yasoda got word of Durvasa Muni’s blessing that Your cooking will be not only tasty but will grant long life, strength, and victory to whoever tastes it, she will not let her son eat unless the food has been prepared by You.”

Radha’s heart flies to Nandagrama at once, but for Her body to be able to follow, She requests Kundalata to secure Jatila’s permission. At first the old woman is reluctant, but then she recalls Paurnamasi’s order never to disobey Yasoda-devi and says, “Kundalata! I am of two minds. I want to serve Yasoda’s order, but I am afraid that Nandanandana will harass my chaste daughter-in-law.”

Kundalata replies, “Mother! Do not worry! The stories envious people tell about the well-behaved son of Maharaja Nanda are simply fabricated — village gossip and nothing more. But to ease your mind, I promise that He will not so much as see Radha's shadow. And once She completes Her work, I also promise that I will personally bring Her back here at once.”

Convinced by this vow, Jatila places Radha’s hand in Kundalata’s and says, “Daughter! You need not fear Krsna; Bhagavan, who protects everyone, will also protect You.” Radharani struggles to suppress a smile of happiness, touches Jatila’s feet, and immediately prepares to leave the palace compound.

When all is ready, Srimati Radharani steps out of the gate, surrounded by Her friends and maidservants who carry laddus and other foods. As soon as She steps onto the streets of Yavata the town is instantly made golden by Her bodily effulgence and aromatic by Her sweet bodily fragrance.

First the girls turn right and walk quickly down the street to the edge of town. Then they turn right again onto the path that leads through the pastures to Nandagrama. Radha covers Her face, lowers Her eyes, and remains silent to avoid being recognised as She walks down the village streets. But once beyond the edge of town, Radha allows Her veil to slip from Her head and with wide-open eyes She gazes at the distant skyline of Nandagrama. She thinks, “Somewhere in that town My beloved is playing just now."

The eyes of Rati-manjari and her peers are all fixed on Srimati Radharani, whose ecstasy visibly increases with each step She takes towards Nandagrama and the imminent meeting with Her lover. To further heighten Radha’s eagerness, and thus the pleasure She will feel when She finally meets Krsna, Kundalata jokes, “Radha! Your husband left three days ago to buy new cows, and yet bite marks are clearly visible on Your lips. In fact, there are even scratch marks on Your breasts. How is that possible?”

Radha self-consciously licks Her lips and then squints Her eyes to conceal Her joy. The girls around Her start to giggle, but Lalita comes to Her defence, “Actually, we were collecting flowers in the forest yesterday. A parrot mistook Radha’s lips for bimba fruit. Trying to taste their sweet nectar, it aggressively bit Her lips and scratched Her breasts in the process.”

This conversation sparks Radha’s memory of Her pastimes with Krsna, causing Her body to shake with tremors of ecstatic bliss. From behind Radha, Rati sees the hairs on her mistress’s neck, back, and arms stand up. She thinks, “Just see! I have just finished dressing Radhika, and now prema is adding even more ornaments to Her body."

At appropriate times, a veritable treasure house of transcendental decorations cover Srimati Radharani’s body, including eight transcendental symptoms, thirty-three aggressive ecstasies, and twenty emotional ecstasies. What happens when Krsna beholds these opulences on Radha’s body?

*eta bhava-bhusaya bhusita sri-radhara anga*  
*dekhite uthale krsna-sukhabdhi-taranga*

**“When Srimati Radharani’s body manifests the ornaments of assorted ecstatic symptoms, the ocean of Krsna’s happiness immediately generates transcendental waves.”**

In fact, it is said that Sri Krsna feels thousands of times more satisfied when, from afar, He sees Srimati Radharani’s face light up due to symptoms of ecstatic love than when He directly touches Her. The way Krsna reciprocates Radha’s ecstatic displays proves that His happiness is not at all mundane. For instance, on one occasion, as Krsna tried to block Her way, a combination of ecstasies known as kila-kincita overwhelmed Sri Radha. Her eyes turned red from tears, Her lips quivered with desire, Her eyebrows arched high, and Her mouth curved into a mild smile. As Krsna watched Her display these emotions, He felt a million times happier than He would have by embracing Her.

A gopi sees Radha’s condition and says, “Dear friend! Is the cool morning breeze the cause for Your hair standing on end? Or is it perhaps something else?”

Pointing to a lotus in a nearby pond, Visakha responds, “O friend! That tender lotus we know as Sri Radha appears to be moved by the wind, but in truth it is trembling in fear of an approaching bumblebee (madhusudana).”

Radha hears the word madhusudana and Her ecstasy increases, causing Her to stumble. Rati notices this and addresses Radha within her mind, “Svamini is the name of one who controls Krsna’s senses! But at the moment, assailed by love for Him, You cannot even control Your own senses. In fact, You can barely even walk. Please, therefore, allow me to stay by Your side to give You support when You need it.”

If devotees want to taste transcendental symptoms upon hearing the words of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, they must be svamis or svaminis — masters of their senses. That is the verdict of Srimad-Bhagavatam:

*nisamya karmani gunan atulyan*  
*viryani lila-tanubhih krtani*  
*yadatiharsotpulakasru-gadgadam*  
*pratkantha udgayati rauti nrtyati*

**“One who is situated in devotional service is certainly the controller of his senses, and thus he is a liberated person. When such a liberated person, the pure devotee, hears of the transcendental qualities and activities of the Lord’s incarnations for the performance of various pastimes, his hair stands on end on his body, tears fall from his eyes, and in his spiritual realisation his voice falters. Sometimes he very openly dances, sometimes he sings loudly, and sometimes he cries. Thus he expresses his transcendental jubilation.”**

**Verse 59**

*parsva-dvaye lalitayatha visakhaya ca*  
*tvam sarvatah parijanais ca paraih paritam*  
*pascan maya vibhrta-bhangura-madhya-bhagam*  
*kim rupa-manjarir iyam pathi nesyatiha*

**“Will Rupa-manjari lead You on the path, with Lalita and Visakha at Your two sides, Your friends all around, and me holding Your delicate waist from behind?”**

Commentary: What support will a little girl like Rati offer Radharani as She struggles to control Her ecstasies? Rati will help to steady her mistress by holding on to Radha’s waist from behind.
