**Verse 88**

*bhratra go-’yutam atra manju-vadane snehena dattvalayam*  
*sridamna krpanam-pratosya jatilam-raksakhya-raka-ksane*  
*nitayah sukha-soka-rodana-bharais te sandravantyah param*  
*vatsalyah janakau vidhasyata itah kim-lalanam-me 'gratah*

**“O sweet-faced girl! When, on the full moon day named Raksa-purnima, upon which Your brother Sridama comes to Yavata with ten thousand cows to satisfy the greedy Jatila before affectionately returning with You to Varsana, will Your parents lovingly fondle You in front of me, as You melt with weeping from happiness and sorrow?”**

Commentary: It is the Vedic custom that a married girl regularly visits her parental home so that she and her parents do not feel too much separation from one another. In this verse Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami describes one such visit of Radha’s to Varsana.

The oral traditions of Vraja give different accounts of Radha’s year-round itinerary.According to one, in the month of Magha (January-February) Sridama escorts his sister Radha back to Varsana, where She stays for three months until Her brother-in-law Durmada returns in Visakha (April-May) to take Her back to Yavata, where She spends a period of three months with Her in-laws. Then — as described in this verse—Sridama again returns in the month of Sravana (July-August) and takes Radha back to Varsana for another three-month visit, and finally at the end of the month of Asvina (September-October), Durmada again returns to take Her back to Yavata. A rough account, then, of Srimati Radharani’s year is that She alternates every three months between Her parental home and Her marital home.

Just before the celebration of Raksa-bandhana, the full-moon day of Sravana on which girls tie sacred threads around their brothers’ wrists, Radha’s elder brother, Sridama, arrives on horseback in Yavata, bringing with him ten thousand cows. Radha is meant to visit Her parents, but Jatila, true to her quarrelsome disposition, might object. King Vrsabhanu therefore, in order to appease Jatila’s wrath and satiate her greed for wealth, sends a herd of cows as a gift.

When Radha leaves Yavata, Her friends and maidservants, whose parental homes are also in or around Varsana, go with Her. Curiously, Yavata is at those times emptied of young brides and village life there is peaceful in comparison to the months when the young girls are not away. In contrast, at those times Varsana becomes a beehive of activity, where, liberated from the strict scrutiny of Her in-laws, Radha can more easily meet with Krsna.

Radha travels to Varsana on an elegant royal palanquin, surrounded by Her friends and maidservants, who sing songs about Krsna along the way. Rati-manjari walks right next to the palanquin, separated from Radha only by a thin, see-through curtain, in case the princess should need anything. Radharani is beaming with happiness to be liberated from the prison-like house of Her husband.

“Manju-vadana!” Rati calls out to Radha and then turns to Her with a smile. “Your face is radiating so much sweetness that bees are following us in swarms. But I know why You are so happy."

Raising Her eyebrows, Radharani responds, “If you know, then why not tell Me?"

Placing a hand on the door handle of the palanquin, Rati says, “You are happy because in Varsana the black bee of Vraja will find it very easy to drink the nectar of Your face.”

“Is that what you think?" Radha nods.

“Yes!” replies Rati. “And no doubt You will cry in happiness to see Your loving parents — and probably in sorrow too, remembering the suffering You have had to endure with Your in-laws. But Your greatest bliss will be in casting off the shackles with which Jatila chains You down and, consequently, in meeting with Krsna more freely.” Upon returning to Varsana, Srimati Radharani again lives as a carefree princess rather than as a young bride with household chores. Moreover, no one in Her father’s palace is suspicious of Her movements. She can easily go to Radha-kunda during the day and Govinda-sthali at night. Yet because She is married Her movements are not wholly unrestricted — and rightly so. Radha’s liaisons with Krsna must always be forbidden in order for Them to nourish the mood of parakiya-rasa.

Krsna also takes full advantage of having easier access to Radha in Varsana. For example, in the guise of a female poet He enters the ladies’ inner chambers and sings songs about Radha’s qualities and pastimes. Astonished, Radha turns to Her friends and exclaims, “How this dark-complexioned poetess came to know of My personal secrets is astonishing!”

On another occasion, Krsna disguises Himself as a female artist selling paintings. Upon seeing the finest painting, Radha whispers to Lalita, “Look! This portrait is of a girl who looks just like Me, alongside a handsome boy resembling this artist. How is that?”

Rati and Radha continue talking until they arrive at the foot of Varsana Hill, where they are received by the villagers, the king’s musicians, brahmanas chanting mantras, and of course the king and queen themselves. Radha melts into Her mother’s arms and, all at once, the tension of having to spend three months with Her husband’s family bursts forth in the form of tears. But those tears are mixed with tears of joy at being with those who love Her. As Rati watches Radha crying in Kirtida's arms, she sings a song of her own composition:

*kirtida-kanyaka matr-sneha-piyusa-putrika*

**“Queen Kirtida's daughter always overflows with the nectar of love for Her beautiful mother.”**

Radha is smothered by Her mother’s kisses and Her father’s words of love, and then She is greeted by the elderly ladies and all the other villagers, including the cows. It seems to Rati-manjari that nightfall will come before the greetings come to an end. Such intense loving exchanges are natural for Radha, who is also known as *Vraja-go- gopa-gopali-jiva-matraika-jivana*, “the life of the cows, gopas, and gopis of Vraja.”

And why not! Who could not love Her?

**Verse 89**

*lajjayah-puratah parato mam*  
*gahvaram giri-pater bata nitva*  
*divya-ganam api tat-svara-bhedam*  
*siksayisyasi kada sa-daye tvam*

**“O merciful girl! Because You are shy before Your friends, will You take me to a cave of Govardhana Hill to lovingly tutor me in singing divine songs in various melodies?”**

Commentary: Each verse of Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali is a sutra-like vignette of Radha’s and Krsna’s eternal pastimes. The author puts into words what he sees of the spiritual realm through the window of his pure heart. Meditating upon these verses through the medium of the holy name, Vaisnavas can glimpse the world of Dasa Gosvami in proportion to their spiritual attainment.

Why is Srimati Radharani shy before Her friends? Because they lovingly make fun of Her intimate relationship with Krsna! Her maidservants, however, rarely joke about their mistress, and therefore She reveals to them everything about Her feelings and activities. Radha is uninhibited before Her maidservants.

To enrich Krsna’s pastimes, there is always need for new melodious songs describing His glories. The gopis compose these songs, teach them to one another, and then perform them during the rasa dance. The songs Radharani composes about Her loving pastimes with Krsna cannot he disclosed to just anyone or sung just anywhere, however. These songs are meant to enhance Krsna’s pleasure when Radha is alone with Him and Her close friends are not around. And although Radha composes these songs, because She and Krsna are their subject, She cannot be the one to sing them. Thus the maidservants must be taught these songs in a secluded place, away from Radha’s close friends, the sakhis.

As the gopis sit stringing garlands by Radha-kunda, Radharani signals to Rati and the two girls stealthily retreat to a cave in nearby Govardhana Hill.

When they reach the heart of the cave Radha tells Rati, “Come sit in front of Me." Rati sits down, and Radha begins the lesson. “When Syamasundara and I are resting within a grove, from just outside the grove you should sing this song at the appropriate time.”

Sri Radha picks up Her vina, plucks the strings, and in Her sweet, melodious voice sings a beautiful composition that makes the stones of Govardhana cry in ecstasy. Rati watches and listens. Her heart pounds with excitement and she thinks, “Am I dreaming, or am I really this fortunate?”Songs about Krsna, however, can never be kept completely confidential. Even if no one else hears them Krsna will. And where those songs are sung with love, Krsna will even appear in person. This is Narada’s conclusion as well:

*pragayatah sva-viryani tirtha-padah priya-sravah*  
*ahuta iva me sighram darsanam yati cetasi*

**“The Supreme Lord Sri Krsna, whose glories and activities are pleasing to hear, at once appears on the seat of my heart, as if called for, as soon as I begin to chant His holy activities.”**

And so as Radha sings Her own composition, Krsna comes to the entrance of the cave just as a hypnotised snake follows the sound of its charmer’s flute to its source. Syama suddenly appears before the two girls and says, “What song are You teaching Rati?” startling both Radha and Her maidservant.

Bashful before Krsna, Radha says, “Nothing! We were just rehearsing.”

But Krsna is not to be denied. He sits down beside Radha and with a sweet smile says, “Please let Me hear it.”

Radha gives Him an uncertain look but, unable to refuse Him, She hands the vina to Rati, telling her to sing.

With closed eyes, Rati sings the song she has just heard from Radha with exactly the same words, melody, mood, and instrumental accompaniment. Because she has fully harmonised her heart with Radharani’s, Rati perfectly reproduces what she has heard. It was Radha’s mercy, and for this, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami calls Radha, Sadaya (“merciful girl”). As Krsna listens to Rati’s beautiful, love- saturated voice, He floats on the waves of rasa and enjoys the same bliss as if He were actually enacting the pastime being chronicled in song.

At the end of the song Rati looks down at Radha’s feet and asks, “Was that all right?”

Radha and Krsna both clap and call out, “Beautiful! Just beautiful." As a reward, Radha embraces Rati, and Krsna gives her a gunja necklace. Rati thinks, “O Sadaya! This has been a very wonderful day, a day made possible only by Your mercy.”

*drstvaiva campaka-lateva camatkrtangi*  
*venu-dhvanim kva ca nisamya ca vihvalangi*  
*sa syamasundara-gunair anugiyamanaih*  
*prita parisvajatu mam vrsabhanu-putri*

**“May King Vrsabhanu’s daughter, who is startled when She sees Krsna, and whose limbs blossom like a vine of campaka flowers at the sound of His flute, embrace me with love after I sing Krsna’s glories.”**

**Verse 90**

*yacita lalitaya kila devya*  
*lajjaya nata-mukhim ganato mam*  
*devi divya-rasa-kavya-kadambam*  
*pathayisyasi kada pranayena*

**“O Goddess! When will I shyly bow my head in the assembly of gopis as Lalita-devi requests You to lovingly read some romantic poems and to teach them to me?”**

Commentary: Verses eighty-nine through ninety-one recount Radha’s teaching Rati-manjari the musical arts (sangitaka-nija-kalah). The role that songs, poetry, and music play in attaining and expressing stages of spiritual perfection cannot be overstated. In fact, Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s nama-sankirtana is no different from Krsna’s rasa-lila. One of the first paintings Srila Prabhupada commissioned for his Caitanya-caritamrta was a split canvas, with one half showing Lord Caitanya performing nama-sankirtana with His associates, and the other half depicting Krsna and the gopis enjoying the rasa dance. The former is for practising devotees, the latter for perfected associates, but the essence of both is the divine treasure of Goloka. Narottama Dasa Thakura says, *golokera prema-dhana, hari-nama-sankirtana*: “Thetreasure of divine love in Goloka Vrndavana has descended as the congregational chanting of Lord Hari’s holy names.”

To progress from devotional service in practice to ecstasy, and finally to pure love, devotees must always receive guidance from their gurus, especially in the matter of singing Krsna’s names and glorifying Him. This guidance continues even after devotees have attained their eternal spiritual forms. Bhaktivinoda Thakura explains:

*sri visakha pade sangita sikhibo*  
*krsna-lila rasa-moya*  
*sri rati manjari sri rasa manjari*  
*hoibe sabe sa-doya*

**“At the lotus feet of Sri Visakha I will learn to play music and sing songs which are full of the transcendental mellow of Krsna’s pastimes. All of the other sakhis in our group, including Sri Rati-manjari and Sri Rasa-manjari will also welcome me into their fold with \[the\] most kind and affectionate dealings.”**

The songs taught by Visakha-devi or Sri Radha cannot be learned in this world because they require expressions of love for which only spiritual bodies are equipped. These songs are not just words and music. They are the highest expressions of spiritual mellows transmitted through mature spiritual moods, and they enable both the performer and the audience to taste true bliss.

At times, when the gopis are all together, Lalita-devi asks Radharani, “Why don’t You read some poems that Rati can include in Her repertoire of verses? She will be able to serve You and Syama by reciting them at different times, such as when she’s delivering messages.”

At this, Rati is embarrassed and thinks, “Amongst so many girls more qualified than I, why is Lalita selecting me?” The answer is obvious: amongst all the manjaris, Rati has the most confidential relationship with Sri Radha.

This time Radha teaches Rati in the presence of others. She recites poems that Rati can utter to Krsna in order to make Him drop whatever He is doing and come to His beloved’s side. This service is extremely sensitive and requires a very trustworthy and reliable messenger—sometimes the poems have hidden meanings, and sometimes they are quite direct.

Radha seats Rati before Her and, as the others huddle around to hear, She says, “Listen carefully! Sometimes Krsna’s flute-playing enters My ears and acts like a poison that only Krsna’s physical presence can counteract. When you see Me disoriented in that way, you must go to Krsna and say:

*sakrt pitva vamsi-dhvani-nava-sudham karna-culukair*  
*madali vibhranta laghima-nikarottanita-matih*  
*sadaham kamsare kam api gadam asadya visamam*  
*vivarna tvam dhanvacarim iha param niscitavati*

**“My friend once drank the fresh nectar of Your flute music with the cupped hands of Her ears. At once Her mind became very light and She fainted. Since then, She has become very pale and constantly afflicted with a grave and mysterious disease. She thinks that You are the expert Dhanvantari to cure Her.’”**

In ways like this, Radha instructs Her student. Rati memorises the poems by hearing them just once. But more important than the memorisation, she understands which poems are fit for which circumstances and knows the proper moods in which to recite them. When Radha says, “Now repeat,” Rati closes her eyes, pictures herself delivering a message to Krsna, and repeats with all her heart precisely what she has heard. Then the gopis all reward her with signs of pleasure.

Svarupa Damodara Gosvami and Ramananda Raya had assimilated many such poems, and they were very expert at reciting them in a way that complemented Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s nocturnal moods of separation in the Gambhira. And during Rupa Gosvami’s visits to Jagannatha Puri, Caitanya Mahaprabhu would have him recite poems from his books in the presence of His companions. All the devotees acclaimed Rupa Gosvami’s compositions, which contained many verses originally spoken by Srimati Radharani. Rati’s lesson now complete, the gopis go about their services while Rati remains at Radha’s side. She looks at Radha with the adoring eyes of a worshipper gazing at her Deity. Rati says, “Devi! You are the guru of the goddess of learning. Indeed You are the original Sarasvati.” Radha decides to test Her student and tries to catch her off guard. Radha says with guile, “What would you say to Krsna if you had to unite Him with Me by a single verse?”

Without hesitating for a moment, Rati repeats the fitting poem she just learned:

*aghadamana jagaty anargha-rupa*  
*vilasati sa guna-ratna-rasir eka*  
*dhig apatumatir asmi yat purastat*  
*kathina-manes tava vaktum udyatam*

**“O crusher of Agha! The transcendental virtues of Radharani are like a host of priceless jewels that have no equal anywhere. But foolish me! Why should I describe jewels to one whose heart is as hard as diamond?”**

Radha claps Her hands in pleasant surprise. “Oh, you are such a fast learner!”

Rati replies gravely, “I have to be! You may need my services at any moment.”

**Verse 91**

*nija-kunda-tati-kunje ganjad-bhramara-sankule*  
*devi tvam kacchapi-siksam kada mam karayisyasi*

**“My queen! When will You teach me to play the kacchapi-vina in a grove filled with humming bees situated by the shore of Your lake?”**

Commentary: Both for singing songs and reciting poems, music is needed, and for women, the most fitting instrument is the vina or lute. The kacchapi-vina is named after its resonator, which is shaped like the shell of a turtle (kacchapa). It is said that Narada Muni’s tumburu, the stringed instrument he is famous for carrying, is also a kacchapi-vina. And when he plays it, the names of Radhika-ramana resound throughout the universe, making everyone dance in bliss.Imagine, then, the effect of Radha’s vina playing!

Radha’s skill in playing the vina can only be compared to Her mastery of singing and dancing. In other words, it is unsurpassable. And when She plays, the sound of Her vina not only proclaims Her fame throughout Vraja, but also dries up the faces of Her competitors, like Candravali. And beyond that, Her vina charms infallible Krsna.

Dasa Gosvami says:

*vina-dhvani-dhutopendra-hastac-cyotita-vamsika*  
*cuda-svana-hrta-syama-deha-geha-patha-smrtih*

**“The sound of Radha’s vina causes Krsna to tremble so that the flute slips from His hand. He then forgets both His own body and the path to His home, just as He does when He hears the tinkling of Her bracelets and ornaments.”**

To complement Rati’s previous lessons, Srimati Radharani now teaches her how to play the kacchapi-vina. Rati already knows how to play, but Radha now helps her to perfect her skill. They sit alone together in a beautiful grove of blossoming flowers, the fragrance of which has attracted many humming bees. The sound of lapping waves further sweetens the atmosphere. But, for Rati, all these things pale in comparison to Sri Radha’s presence, which exudes untold loveliness, sweetness, and sublimity.

Radha shows Rati how to tune the vina, how to hold it, and how to vibrate its strings. She then sings a song and shows Rati how to play its accompaniment on the vina. After some time, Radharani hands the instrument to Rati and says, “Now you try.” Rati tries her best. When she makes a mistake Radha patiently corrects her. And so it goes for quite some time.

Sri Radha is in the role of guru, teaching Her disciple how to serve Krsna. A maidservant proficient on the vina will be a greater asset to Krsna and His pastimes. Radha’s constant meditation is how to increase Krsna’s pleasure more and more, and one way to do that is to bring more and more gopis into His intimate company.

Of course it is only a matter of time before Krsna comes to know that Radha is giving music lessons at Radha-kunda, to where He hurries all alone. His sudden presence in the entrance to the kunja interrupts Rati’s singing, but He sits down, eager to hear more. With prompting from Radha, Rati softly plucks the vina's strings and sings a love ballad meant to inspire amorous enjoyment. Her recital is effective.

Without stopping her performance, Rati discreetly leaves the kunja to sit nearby and continue her newly assigned service of serenading the divine couple. Now and then Rati looks through the latticework around the grove to watch Radha and Krsna display Their unlimited skill at amorous sports. The two lovers appear to be a dark monsoon cloud surrounded on all sides by flashing lightning, creating a downpour of transcendental mellows with which They drench Their senses and the senses of Their faithful maidservant.

**Verse 92**

*viharais trutitam haram gumphitam dayitam kada*  
*saklunam lajjaya devi samjhaya mam nideksyasi*

**“O Devi! Being shy before Your girlfriends, will You give me a hint to restring the necklace which broke during Your loving pastimes with Krsna?”**

Commentary: In a storm some trees are inevitably blown over by the wind, others are struck by lightning, and yet others are uprooted by floodwater. So it is in Radha’s and Krsna’s loving pastimes that Their clothes become loosened, Their ornaments broken, and Their hair dishevelled. Meanwhile, Rati sits outside the grove, singing for Radha and Syama. When she discerns that Their pastimes of love have ended for the time being, she enters and sees that Krsna is busy dressing Radharani.

“Do it quickly!” Radha tells Him. “Lalita and the others will come any moment. If they see Me like this, they will tease Me.”

Krsna does His best to straighten Her clothes, tie Her braids, and refresh Her mascara, but His own ecstasies are interfering with His usual expertise. Just as Deities become more radiant after devotees worship Them, Radha becomes more beautiful after Krsna enjoys with Her, and seeing Her radiant beauty, He becomes bewildered.

*lila-ante sukhe inhara angera madhuri*  
*taha dekhi’ sukhe ami apana pasari*

**“Seeing the lustre of Her complexion after Our pastimes together, I forget My own identity in happiness.”**

Radharani’s overflowing splendour distracts Krsna from the task at hand. He is reluctant to obscure with garments and ornaments that cause of His overflowing pleasure. Worried that Krsna will not finish in time, Radha glances at Her broken pearl necklace, as if to say, “Rati! You must restring it quickly.”

Sitting down on the ground, Rati at once begins threading the large pearls as she continues to hum the tune she had been singing earlier. More familiar with this service than with playing the vina, she quickly completes her task. The maidservants learn to dexterously carry out many of these kinds of personal services.

For example, in the early morning, when the divine couple wake up in a grove by the Yamuna’s shore, maidservants replace Radha’s used garments with new ones. They retie Her braid, restring Her broken pearl necklace, and apply mascara to Her eyes. And finally, with coloured ointment they conceal the evidence of aggressive amorous enjoyment that marks Her limbs.

The selfless, amorous mellow embraced by Radha’s maidservants is the key to achieving the most intimate service possible to Radha and Krsna, the personal, dual feature of the Absolute Truth. Thus the manjaris are at the top end of the spectrum of loving service — higher even than Radha’s dear friends, the sakhis. And the great yogis, however practised they may be in the mellow of neutrality, remain mere observers at the opposite end of the spectrum of devotional engagements.

Lord Caitanya’s associate Prabodhananda Sarasvati Thakura, who is the gopi Tungavidya in the pastimes of Sri Krsna, is an example of a girlfriend of Radharani who aspires for the manjaris’ intimate services. He writes:

*kada raty-unmuktam kaca-bharam aham samyamayita*  
*kada va sandhasye trutita-nava-muktavalim api*  
*kada va kasturyas tilakam api bhuyo racayita*  
*nikunjantar-vrtte nava-rati-rane yauvana-maneh*

**“When will I retie the braids undone in amorous pastimes? When will I restring the broken pearl necklace? When will I redraw the musk tilaka broken in the forest during an amorous battle between the jewels of teenage youths?”**

Why does Prabodhananda Sarasvati hanker for the position of Radha’s maidservant?

Radha and Krsna are not embarrassed to engage in amorous sports in the presence of Their maidservants, but They are too shy to do so in front of Their girlfriends. Thus the manjaris are privy to certain confidential services rendered at such times, services inaccessible to the sakhis. Prabodhananda Sarasvati aspires for such intimate service.

And why are Radha and Krsna shy before the sakhis but not before the manjaris?

The sakhis are also heroines like Srimati Radharani, gopis who enjoy direct loving pastimes with Krsna. Thus they cannot maintain the same dispassionate impartiality during Radha’s and Krsna’s intimate exchanges as do the manjaris, who offer their hearts to Krsna but never their bodies.

Only the most advanced devotees will fully realise such esoteric truths, but the followers of Lord Caitanya who have firm faith in the gopis should at least know the theory underlying those truths.

Rati holds up the necklace, now restrung, and Radha exclaims in a soft voice, “That was quick. Rati, My dear, you are so expert!” Radha’s affectionate praise makes Rati’s heart bob like a buoy in the ocean of bliss. She wants nothing else but to please Sri Radha. That is the substance of her being— her sthayi-bhava.

**Verse 93**

*sva-mukhan man-mukhe devi kada tambula-carvitam*  
*snehat sarva-diso viksya samaye tvam pradasyasi*

**“O Goddess! When will You, after looking in all directions, affectionately transfer the chewed betel nuts from Your mouth into mine?”**

Commentary: Srimati Radharani is greatly pleased with Rati-manjari for having learned to sing, recite poems, and play the kacchapi-vina, and for quickly rethreading Her necklace. Radha thinks, “Somehow I should reward her.”

Rad does not want to he materially rewarded for her service. But she does want something: She wants to be explicitly accepted by Radha as Her maidservant and to receive Sri Radha’s remnants. Sri Radha knows Rati’s mind and thus decides to please her.

After Krsna finishes dressing Radharani, He is so enamoured by Her sweetness that He kisses Her on the lips. As They kiss, Krsna transfers His chewed tambula into Radha’s mouth.

*krsna ye khaya tambula, kahe tara nahi mula,*  
*tahe ara dambha-paripati*  
*tara yeba udgara, tare kaya ‘amrta-sara’,*  
*gopira mukha kare ‘alabati’*

**“The betel chewed by Krsna is priceless, and the remnants of such chewed betel from His mouth are said to be the essence of nectar. When the gopis accept these remnants, their mouths become His spittoons.”**

While chewing Krsna’s remnants, Radha lowers Her head so that Rati can tie the string of pearls around Her neck. Rati finishes quickly, and as she is about to sit down, Radha wraps Her arm around Rati and holds her. Looking to the entrance of the kunja to make sure no gopi can see, Radha transfers Krsna’s tambula from Her mouth directly into Rati’s.

This single act of mercy completely fulfils Rati’s spiritual longings. Like an unexpectedly erupting geyser, Rati’s eyes shower Radha’s lotus feet with tears. Unable to think or speak, Rati can only feel the bliss surging through her heart and the symptoms of ecstasy in her limbs.

Materialists may think such loving exchanges trivial; in fact, they may even find them repulsive. And neophyte devotees may he confused by or even critical of them. But transcendentalists always recognise such exchanges to be the summit of good fortune and spiritual achievement. Rupa Gosvami prayed to have Krsna’s tambula from Sri Radha’s mouth, but he requested Radha to leave it for him on a leaf.

*asye devyah katham api muda nyastam asyat tvayesa*  
*ksiptam parne pranaya-janitad devi vamyat tvayagre*  
*akutajnas tad ati-nibhrtam carvitam kharvitangas*  
*tambuliyam rasayati janah phulla-roma kadayam*

**“O Radha! When the Lord pushes the remnants of His chewed betel into Your mouth as a gift, and You, feigning loving unwillingness, spit it onto a leaf, may I relish these remnants as the hairs on my small body stand upright inecstasy?”**

By the grace of Rupa-manjari, Rati’s fortune is even greater. For Rati, Radha docs not place the tambula on a leaf but transfers it directly from Her mouth to Rati’s. When Rati finally comes to her senses, she thinks, “Just as the gopis’ mouths are Krsna’s spittoons, my mouth has become Radhika’s spittoon. I have now achieved everything.” Throughout this episode, Krsna sits silently by appreciating the exchange of love between His two servants.

**Verse 94**

*nivida-madana-yuddhe prana-nathena sardham*  
*dayita-madhura-kanci ya madad vismrtasit*  
*sasi-mukhi samaye tam hanta sambhalya bhangya*  
*tvaritam iha tad-artham kim tvaydham praheya*

**“O moon-faced girl! With clever hints, will You direct me to Your favourite chain of waist bells, lying forgotten due to Your bewilderment during an amorous battle with the Lord of Your life?”**

Commentary: Krsna is not the only one distracted by ecstasy due to the festival of amorous enjoyment mentioned in the previous verses. Even after the divine couple’s pastime comes to an end, Radharani is so enchanted by Krsna’s divine features that She becomes forgetful in Her bewilderment. Forgetfulness and bewilderment are two of thirty-three bodily symptoms (vyabhicari-bhavas) visible in ecstatic love. As a result of such forgetfulness, when the trio leave the grove to meet their friends, Radha leaves behind the chain of tinkling bells (kancana-citrangi) that She always wears around Her waist.

What is the cause of Radha’s forgetfulness? The cause is the nectar of Krsna’s lips, which acts as an intoxicant with effects that linger hours after being consumed. Thus, due to the effects of kissing Krsna, Radha does not remember Her most treasured ornament until long after the end of Their loving pastime.

The gopis attest to the enchanting effect of Krsna’s lips, which they feel directly by kissing Him and indirectly by hearing the music of His flute. In either case, the effects are the same.

*surata-vardhanam soka-nasanam*  
*svarita-venuna susthu-cumbitam*  
*itara-raga-vismaranam nrnam*  
*vitara vira nas te ’dharamrtam*

**“O hero of charity! Please deliver unto us the nectar of Your lips. That nectar increases lusty desires for enjoyment and diminishes lamentation in the material world. Kindly give us the nectar of Your lips, which are touched by Your transcendentally vibrating flute, for that nectar makes all human beings forget all other attachments.”**

The gopis’ intense love for Krsna enables them to treasure His transcendental qualities - like the nectar of His lips — with the intensity expressed in this verse. As Krsna mentions in the Bhagavad-gita and the Caitanya-caritamrta, the extent to which devotees surrender to Him in love and devotion determines the degree to which they taste His sweetness. Although Krsna’s sweetness is inherent in Him, non-devotees can neither taste it nor be attracted to it.

The gopis, however, through their superlative devotion, taste some inexplicable ambrosia from Krsna’s lips by kissing and by hearing the flute. And Radha, by Her unique, incomprehensible love, tastes something a thousand times more nectarean. Caitanya Mahaprabhu describes the lingering influence of the taste of Krsna’s lips:

*kanera bhitara vasa kare, apane tanha sada sphure,*  
*anya sabda na deya pravesite*  
*ana katha na sune kana, ana balite bolaya ana,*  
*ei krsnera vamsira carite*

**“The vibration of His flute is just like a bird that creates a nest within the ears of the gopis and always remains prominent there, not allowing any other sound to enter their ears. Indeed, the gopis cannot hear anything else, nor are they able to concentrate on anything else, not even to give a suitable reply. Such are the effects of the vibration of Lord Krsna’s flute.”**

Since Sri Radha is still reeling from the effects of tasting Krsna’s sweetness through all of Her senses, is it any wonder that She forgets the prized ornament that slipped off during Their pastimes?

Lalita and the other gopis arrive outside the grove, and the sakhis are surprised to see that Radha looks just as She did before. Her body shows no trace of having received Krsna’s affections. Lalita looks suspiciously at Rati-manjari, who covers her face with her veil and follows the others to a clearing where they will entertain Krsna by dancing.

As Krsna sits upon a golden dais and plays His flute, the girls rise one by one, dancing sometimes alone, sometimes together, but always singing songs and clapping hands. The sounds of tinkling bangles, anklets, and waist bells add to the sweetness of the festivities. But when Radharani gets up to dance She notices that Her waist bells are silent. It is then that She realises they must still be lying somewhere in the kunja.

What can She do? If She acknowledges the missing ornament, then Her friends will realise that there was more to Her time with Krsna than sweet talks and they will all have their fun with Her. Radha looks to Rati-manjari who, ever attentive, catches her mistress’s glance. Then, by slapping Her hips during Her dance and raising Her eyebrows, Radha informs Rati of the missing ornament. Radha’s resourceful maidservant knows what is to be done.

Luckily, in the ecstasy of clapping and singing, the other girls don’t notice the missing belt. Meanwhile, Rati returns to the grove, recovers the waist bells, hides them in the folds of her dress, and returns to the dance arena. Just then, breathing heavily from Her exertion, Radha sits down beside Krsna. And Rati, while drying the perspiration from Sri Radha’s limbs, takes the opportunity to replace the belt, unseen by the others. Such are the manjaris’ services in Vraja.

Indebted to Rati yet again, Radha sends a grateful glance her way. Rati responds with a glance of her own that says, “Moon-faced girl! For that gift of tambula, You can ask me to do anything.” Rati addresses Radha as “moon-faced girl” (Sasi-mukhi) because the anxious look on Radha’s otherwise perfect face made it look as if the full moon had begun to wane.

**Verse 95**

*kenapi dosa-lava-matra-lavena devi*  
*santadyamana iha dhira-mate tvayoccaih*  
*rosena tal laluaya kila niyamanah*  
*sandraksyate kim u manak sa-dayam jano ’yam*

**“O Goddess! You are generally very calm, but when You severely rebuke me for a slight mistake, will You again mercifully glance upon me when Lalita brings me before You?”**

Commentary: In this verse Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami refers to an incident in which Radha chastises Rati-manjari. Although the Lord is an ocean of mercy, He bestows His mercy in various ways. He might award His mercy through praise or by a strong reprimand, but because He is absolute, His praise and censure are both His kindness. Wise devotees, therefore, accept both equally. They do not avoid chastisement. Indeed, the learned recognise chastisement by the Lord, or by a Vaisnava representative of the Lord, as evidence of their having been accepted as confidential servants.

An example of how the Lord reprimands His devotee, and how the devotee accepts that reprimand as mercy, is found in the pastime of Lord Nityananda’s cursing and kicking Sivananda Sena.

Once, as the devotees from Bengal were on their way to see Lord Caitanya in Jagannatha Puri, Sivananda Sena was late in arranging their food and lodging for the night. Lord Nityananda became very upset at the delay and cursed the sons of Sivananda Sena to die. When Sivananda heard from his distressed wife about the extent of the Lord’s displeasure, Sivananda replied, “Why are you needlessly crying? Let my three sons die for the inconvenience we have caused Nityananda Prabhu.”

Sivananda Sena then went to apologise to the Lord. But the Lord got up and kicked him. Sivananda Sena was very pleased at being kicked by Lord Nityananda, as is self-evident in his reaction:

*“aji more bhrtya kari’ angikara kaila*  
*yemana aparadha bhrtyera, yogya phala dila*  
*‘sasti’-chale krpa kara — e tomara 'karuna’*  
*trijagate tomara caritra bujhe kon jana?*

**“Today You have accepted me as Your servant and have properly punished me for my offence. My dear Lord! Your chastising me is Your causeless mercy. Who within the three worlds can understand Your real character?”**

At this, Lord Nityananda was very pleased and embraced His servant.

This is the attitude of sincere devotees. They remain Krsna’s servants whether the Lord embraces them with His arms or tramples them beneath His feet. Such a disposition endears devotees to the Lord and certifies them as faithful and dependable.

When Rati leaves to find Sri Radha’s belt, Lalita-devi, who is also ever vigilant, notices Rati’s absence. Upon Rati’s return Lalita enquires where she had been but, predictably, she receives no reply. Nonetheless, Lalita didn’t need a reply to know what had happened: it was obvious to her that Radha and Krsna had done more than chat while the gopis were elsewhere picking flowers. Therefore, at the conclusion of the dancing, Radha notices that Her friends are huddled together giggling and glancing in Her direction. Embarrassed, She retires to Her grove with Rati at Her heels.

Although generally calm and grave, Srimati Radharani is now visibly angry. She paces from one side of the grove to the other and then turns to Rati and says in a fiery voice, “My friends are joking and snickering about Me. What did you tell Lalita?”

Taken aback by Radha’s fury, Rati answers, “I didn’t tell her anything.”

Radharani’s features glow with a red hue, “Then why are they gossiping about Me?”

Rati ventures an explanation, “Perhaps Lalita noticed that I had left..."

“That’s the problem!” snaps Radha. “You weren’t discreet enough. First Lalita knows, and now every gopi in Vrndavana knows.” Taking two steps towards Rati, Radharani waves Her forefinger, “And it’s your fault!”

At Radha’s sudden anger the bees leave the grove, the flowers close, and the birds stop singing. Rati feels like the earth is slipping out from under her feet and fire is consuming her body. Radha doesn’t relent. “It’s your fault,” She repeats.

In barely a whisper, Rati-manjari asks, “What should I do.?” Raising Her right arm and pointing to the entrance of the grove, Radha replies, “Go!”

“Go?” Rati asks.

“Leave My grove. Now!” replies Radha with finality.

Her eyes blinded by tears, Rati staggers from the grove with Radha’s order ringing in her ears. Unable to walk any further, Rati sits down against a tree just outside the grove. Covering her face with her veil, she cries uncontrollably.

Go? Where is there to go? Other than at Radha’s side, there is no other place for her to be. Mascara stains streak Rati’s face, and her dress is soaked in tears. Just a little while ago she sat not far from here blissfully singing for Radha and Krsna, and now she is sitting and crying pitifully over the anger of her mistress.

Curious to know where Sri Radha has gone, Lalita-devi leaves the other girls and arrives at the grove to find Rati sobbing woefully. “Rati,” she asks lovingly, “what’s wrong?”

Rati raises her tear-streaked face but, unable to say anything, she just shakes her head and cries. Once again, Lalita doesn’t need an explanation. With Rati affectionately in tow, Lalita enters the grove where Radha, seated sulking upon a bed, aimlessly draws patterns on the ground with Her toe. Radha frowns as the two girls enter, but before She can say anything, Lalita addresses Her in a brassy voice, “Why are you angry with Rati for something that I did?”

Without allowing Radha to say a word, Lalita continues, “I was the one who saw Rati bring the belt, and I was the one who shared Your conquest over Syama with the other gopis. If You want to blame someone, blame me. If You want to chastise someone, chastise me.” Hands planted on her hips in a challenging mood, Lalita stares into Radha’s eyes. For a long moment the two friends simply stare at each other in silence. Then, placing her right arm over Rati-mahjari’s slender shoulders and pulling her close, Lalita says in a more conciliatory voice, “Rati didn’t do anything. Don’t make her suffer.”

Radha shifts her gaze to Rati-manjari, who looks up at her mistress with reddened, uncertain eyes. Lalita concludes, “Be merciful to this girl. Whether You beat her or caress her, she knows only You. She doesn’t deserve to be punished.”

Seeing Rati’s sweet face lined with sorrow, Radha throws her the lifeline of a compassionate smile and their reconciliation begins. With Radha’s outlook changed, Lalita leaves the two girls and goes to her own kunja.

Radha motions to Rati, and Rati, letting out a small cry of relief, scurries to Radha’s feet and looks up into Her eyes adoringly. Without speaking, they exchange loving glances. Rati thinks, “O grave one! My Dhiramati! You can do with me whatever You want. But I am always Yours.” Radha responds with a merciful glance.

In this way, Lalita-devi, true to her magnanimous nature, expertly reunites Radha with Rati. Lalita is equally eager to help anyone else who sincerely longs for Radha’s service. Rupa Gosvami says:

*yam kam api vraja-kule vrsabhanujayah*  
*preksya sva-paksa-padavim anurudhyamanam*  
*sadyas tad ista-ghatanena krtarthayantim*  
*devim gunaih su-lalitam lalitam namami*

**“I offer my obeisances to supremely charming Lalita-devi, who is the treasure house of all wonderful qualities. When she sees that a young maiden is inclined towards Srimati Radharani, Lalita brings that girl into the presence of King Vrsabhanu’s daughter and requests Her to accept that girl as a member of Her own party.”**

**Verse 96**

*tavaivasmi tavaivasmi na jivami tvaya vina iti vijnaya devi tvam naya mam caranantikam*

**“I am Yours! I am Yours! I cannot live without You! O Goddess! Knowing this, please take me to Your lotus feet.”**

Commentary: Rati offers herself at Srimati Radharani’s lotus feet. Just as one offers flowers to the lotus feet of one’s worshipable deity with the words esa puspanjali, Rati offers her entire being with the words "I am Yours.” Rati’s surrender is not partial; therefore she says, “I cannot live without You.” And one who has given oneself so completely to Srimati Radharani can expect to he quickly taken to the shelter of Her lotus feet. Krsna also says that He offers His personal shelter to those who exclusively surrender unto Him:

*sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam saranam vraja*  
*aham tvam sarva-papebhyo moksayisyami ma sucah*

**“Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.”**

After passing through a trial-by-fire in the form of Radha’s chastisement, Rati’s faith and love are not only intact, but also intensified, and she expresses her increased commitment as she kneels before Sri Radha. And then, just as Radharani is about to embrace Her surrendered maidservant, the entire scene in the grove disappears, and once again Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami finds himself by the bank of Radha-kunda. In that light, the words of this verse take on another meaning.

As an elderly renunciate who is unable to walk and whose sight is all but gone, Dasa Gosvami cries out to Srimati Radharani in a pitiful voice capable of melting stone. He grieves thus, “O Devi! I have spent many years living by this lake, chanting Your names and remembering Your pastimes. Sometimes You appear briefly to me and then disappear. In this way I continued to live. But for one like me, who has no one else but You, I can no longer maintain my existence by these fleeting visions. Try to understand: I cannot live without You. Having now heard this directly from my lips, I beg You to take me to Your lotus feet.”

After some time the pain of separation becomes unbearable. Raghunatha Dasa simply cries for Srimati Radharani, repeatedly uttering the words, na jivami tvaya vina: “I cannot live without You.”

Dasa Gosvami’s present predicament is the very image of Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s last days on earth, which were full of the ecstasies of divine madness caused by separation from Krsna. Dasa Gosvami endures similar separation from Sri Radha. His example shows practising devotees what to expect from the culmination of a life spent in dedication to the ideals and mission of Caitanya Mahaprabhu.

Devotees who actually feel that they can no longer live without the divine couple have qualified themselves for the shelter of Radha’s and Krsna’s lotus feet. It is just a matter of time.

**Verse 97**

*sva-kundam tava lolaksi sa-priyayah sad aspadam*  
*atraiva mama samvasa ihaiva mama samsthitih*

**“O girl with restless eyes! Because You and Your beloved eternally reside at Your lake, I have made it my home, from where I never leave.”**

Commentary: Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s meditation on his service to Srimati Radharani as Rari-manjari comes to an end with verse ninety-six. The concluding verses of this work (from ninety-seven through one hundred and four) are Raghunatha Dasa’s prayers for eternal, direct service to Sri Radha. The verse at hand speaks not only of his vow to live at Radha-kunda, but also of his vows to serve Radha and Krsna in this life as a practitioner and in the life beyond as Their eternal maidservant.

Devotees purify their hearts by practising the ninefold process of devotional service. Then, by regularly hearing, over time, about the dealings of the Vraja-vasis, they become attracted to one of the five mellows of divine love.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s life is a perfect example of how a devotee always thinks of Krsna within himself and chooses a very dear servitor of Krsna in Vrndavana as his guide. For Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, to think of Krsna means to think of Radharani’s service to

Krsna. And the devotee servitor of Krsna whom Raghunatha chooses to follow is Rupa-manjari. While residing on the banks of Radha- kunda, Dasa Gosvami is constantly absorbed in topics connected to Rupa-manjarl, Sri Radha, and Sri Syamasundara, topics spelled out in the verses of Sri Vilapa-kusumanjali.

This verse shows Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s fixed determination to stay in Radha-kunda, where he spent the last fifty years of his life. However, if devotees cannot physically live at Radha-kunda — or anywhere else in Bhauma Vrndavana — they should mentally reside there. Indeed, the very essence of living in Vraja is to live there within one’s mind. Living there physically, although tremendously beneficial due to the transcendental influence of the holy dhama and the eternal presence of the unmanifest pastimes of the Lord, does not in and of itself make one Krsna conscious. Devotees physically living there must still follow in the footsteps of a resident of Vrndavana like Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami and make an effort to live in Vraja within their minds as well. It is this internal absorption in Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes that allows one to reach the perfectional stage of Krsna consciousness. If devotees do not do so, then just living there physically does not make them Krsna conscious.

Devotees surrendered to the degree that Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami shows here will never leave their place of worship. Why? Since Radha and Krsna reside in such places eternally, once having given themselves to Their Lordships, devotees cannot bear to be without Them. This principle is so important that Lord Caitanya would not allow Gadadhara Pandita to leave Jagannatha Puri and his avowed service to the Tota-gopinatha Deity, even to travel to Vrndavana in the company of the Lord, who is Himself non-different from Tota-gopinatha.”

Although devotees are encouraged to reside in Vraja by thoughts of Krsna and His associates, they are also warned not to make an external show of their internal meditations. Indeed, Rupa Gosvami has ordered practising devotees to always conduct themselves as regulated Vaisnavas and to dedicate themselves to the mission of Caitanya Mahaprabhu:

*seva sadhaka-rupena siddha-rupena catra hi*  
*tad-bhava-lipsuna karya vraja-lokanusaratah*

**“The advanced devotee who is inclined to spontaneous loving service should follow the activities of a particular associate of Krsna’s in Vrndavana. He should execute service externally as a regulative devotee as well as internally from his self-realised position. Thus he should perform devotional service both externally and internally.’’**

A doubt may here arise: Can devotees’ inner meditations and attempts to follow a resident of Vrndavana properly mature as long as they are externally engaged in so many apparently material affairs? The answer is that by serving the mission of Lord Caitanya — who is Radha and Krsna combined — not only do devotees’ inner meditations become enhanced but also their spiritual identities as Krsna’s eternal servants become progressively realised. Prabodhananda Sarasvati explains this principle in the following way:

*yatha yatha gaura-padaravinde*  
*vindeta bhaktim krta-purtya-rasih*  
*tatha tathot-sarpati hrdya-kasmad*  
*radha-padambhoja-sudhambu-rasih*

**“As much as one devotes his full attention to the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya, to that extent he will he able to taste the nectarean service of the lotus feet of Srimati Radharani in Vrndavana. The more one engages in the service of Sri Caitanya, the more one finds oneself in Vrndavana, tasting the nectar of the service of Sri Radha.”**

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami now prays,

**“O Lolaksi, girl with wandering eyes! You have so many girls to serve You, and therefore Your eyes are wandering here and there. But just rest Your eyes on me for a moment.**

**“I have vowed to live in Your eternal home, Radha-kunda, and so I never move from this place. My body is wasting away, however, and my vow will remain intact only if You give me entrance into the eternal, unmanifested Radha-kunda. As Your maidservant, Rati, let me serve You and Your beloved there. Forever. That is my prayer.”**

**Verse 98**

*he sri-sarovara sada tvayi sa mad-isa*  
*presthena sardham iha khelati kama-rangaih*  
*tvam cet priyat priyam ativa tayor itimam*  
*ha darsayadya krpaya mama jivitam tam*

**“O beautiful lake! My queen eternally enjoys amorous pastimes with Her beloved on your shore. If you are dearer than the dearest to Them, then please mercifully now show me the girl who is my life and soul.”**

Commentary: Since he has vowed to live by Radha-kunda, Dasa Gosvami first appeals to his place of residence to help him realise his other vows, of which eternal service to Srimati Radharani and Sri Krsna is most urgent.

The Puranas say that Radha’s lake is as dear to Krsna as is Radha Herself, *yatha radha priya visnos tasyah kundam priyam tatha*. Moreover, that beautiful reservoir of spiritual flavours is known for being able to unite even Lord Sri Krsna with Radharani.

*agha-ripur api yatnad atra devyah prasada-*  
*prasara-krta-kataksa-prapti-kamah prakamam*  
*anusarati yad ucaaih snana-sevanubandhais*  
*tad ati-surabhi radha-kundam evasrayo me*

**“May very dear and fragrant Radha-kunda, where Lord Krsna Himself, yearning to attain the merciful sidelong glance of His queen, diligently bathes, carefully observing the appropriate rituals as directed by Radha’s attendants, be my shelter.”**

Long ago, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami took shelter of Radha-kunda with full knowledge that such a vow guaranteed pure love for Krsna and eternal service to Srimati Radharani. But now, after fifty years of strictly following his guru’s instructions, he calls out as a practitioner would — even though he has already attained perfection— appealing to his place of residence to give him the fruit of love and service: direct vision of the divine couple.

“O beautiful lake!” he prays. “You have the power to unite even Radha and Krsna when They quarrel. Since I have been separated from my mistress for so long, and since you are so dear to Her, can you not unite me with Her also?”

At this appeal, Radha-kunda may well reply, “Dasa Gosvami! Your desire will be realised in time. Just be patient.”

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami joins his palms and counters, “Sri Sarovara! You are not only a beautiful lake but you are also the lake that belongs to Sri. You are not filled with water, but with the liquid form of amorous love. And you are not merely a sacred place, rather you are more than the sum total of all holy places. These glories make you omnipotent. I have already waited here most of my life. Can you not exercise a fraction of your power and make me happy? Why make me wait even a moment longer?”

Radha-kunda replies, “Dear one! In the way that the fruit of a tree ripens in time, the fruit that grows on the creeper of your love will also appear in due time.”

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami answers in a voice that cracks with emotion, “Can’t you see that I am no longer able to live without Her?”

While instructing Rupa Gosvami on the principles of devotional mellows, Caitanya Mahaprabhu describes the creeper of puredevotion. At the conclusion of His description the Lord explains that the final growth of this creeper is the ripening fruit of devotional service, the tasting of which transports one to the desire tree of Lord Krsna’s lotus feet in Goloka Vrndavana. Once there, devotees directly serve the lotus feet of the Lord, taste the juice of the fruit of pure love, and become eternally happy. Lord Kapila says:

*sa eva bhakti-yogakhya alyantika udahrtah*  
*yenativrajya tri-gunam mad-bhavayopapadyate*

**“By attaining the highest platform of devotional service, as I have explained, one can overcome the influence of the three modes of material nature and be situated in the transcendental stage, as is the Lord.”**

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, in whose heart the creeper of pure devotion bears many juicy fruits of love for Radha and Syama, is now begging Radha-kunda for the happiness of direct service to the divine couple. He no longer wants to meditate on his beloved Lords in fleeting darsanas. He yearns to return to Them in the eternal Radha-kunda and serve Them there directly, for evermore.

But the acarya is not making demands. He is simply disclosing the natural condition of his devotion. Just as a tender creeper overloaded with unpicked fruit will break, Dasa Gosvami now says, “If I do not see my worshipable Goddess, I will die."

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s example is a proclamation to practising devotees: “If you remain determined and patiently cultivate devotional service according to the established procedure, in time you will achieve every perfection.” This is Krsna’s promise when He says mam evaisyasi, and it is the promise of Caitanya Mahaprabhu when He says:

*bhavite bhavite krsna sphuraye antare*  
*krsna-krpaya ajna paya rasa-sindhu-pare*

**“When one thinks of Krsna constantly, love for Him manifests within the heart. Even though one may be ignorant, one can reach the far shore of the ocean of transcendental love by Lord Krsna’s mercy.”**

**Verse 99**

*ksanam api tava sangam na tyajed eva devi*  
*tvam asi samavayastvan narma-bhumir yad asyah*  
*iti sumukhi visakhe darsayitva mad-isam*  
*mama viraha-hatayah prana-raksam kurusva*

**“O beautiful-faced Visakha! Because my queen will not leave your company for even a moment, and because you have become the realm of Her joking pastimes due to your being the same age as She, can you please free my life from this torment of separation by showing my mistress to me?”**

Commentary: Devotees who aspire to become Radha’s maidservants must first become the servants of one of Her maidservants. Having been accepted by a manjari like Sri Rupa, devotees should then serve the feet of a sakhi like Lalita-devi who will then place them under the care of Sri Radha. As Rati-manjari, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami is intimately connected to Visakha-devI, and so it is natural that he appeals to her.

Throughout his life, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has been linked with Visakha-devi. In Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s pastimes, Visakha appeared as Ramananda Raya, with whom Dasa Gosvami associated intimately in Jagannatha Puri. After coming to Vraja, Dasa Gosvami described Visakha-devI in his books and dedicated one composition for her pleasure called Sri Visakhanandabhidha-stotra, or “Prayers including names that delight Visakha.”

With joined palms, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami submits to his senior sakhi the same aspiration he just presented to Radha-kunda, and the same one he will present to Krsna and then Radharani Herself. Dasa Gosvami epitomises Krsna’s description of one “resolute in purpose” (*vyavasayatmika buddhih*):

*vyavasayatmika buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana*  
*bahu-sakha hy anantas ca buddhayo ’vyavasayinam*

**“Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. O beloved child of the Kurus, the intelligence of those who are irresolute is many-branched.”**

Wherever he goes, whomever he meets, or whatever he sees, Dasa Gosvami enquires how he can find his worshipable Radha. He is ekeha: a person with only one aim in life. Gaurakisora Dasa Babaji, his heart full of the same moods of separation, would also wander around Vrndavana singing a song by Dasa Gosvami:

*kothay go prema-mayi radhe radhe!*  
*radhe radhe go jaya radhe radhe!*

**“Radhe! Radhe! Goddess of ecstatic love, where are You? Radhe! Radhe! All glories to You! Radhe! Radhe!”**

*dekha diya prana rakho radhe radhe!*  
*tomar kangal tomay dake radhe radhe!*

**“Radhe! Radhe! Please show Yourself and save my life! Your wretched servant calls out to You! Radhe! Radhe!”**

*radhe vrndavana-vilasini radhe radhe!*  
*radhe kanu-mano-mohini radhe radhe!*

**“Radha is the enjoyer of Vrndavana, Radhe! Radhe! Radha is the enchantress of Kanu’s mind! Radhe! Radhe!”**

*radhe astha-sakhir siromani radhe radhe!*  
*radhe Vrsabhanu-nandini radhe radhe!*

**“Radha is the crest jewel of Her eight girlfriends, Radhe! Radhe! Radha is the delightful daughter of King Vrsabhanu! Radhe! Radhe!”**

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami now turns to Visakha-devi to save the sinking boat of his aspiration. Just to remember her extraordinary qualities gives him hope. He has already spoken of her unique position in one of his books:

*bhava-nama-gunadinam aikyat sri-radhikaiva ya*  
*krsnendoh preyasi sa me sri-visakha prasidatu*

**“May Sri Visakha, the beloved of the Krsna-moon, who is just like Radha, being identical in nature, name, features, and in many other ways, be pleased with me.”**

Born near Varsana at the same moment of the same day as Radharani (Bhadra-sukla-astami), Visakha’s astrological constitution is bound to resemble Radha’s in many ways. These similarities naturally make the two girls very close friends. Indeed, Radha is completely dedicated to Visakha, considering her an intimate friend (narma-sakhi). And Visakha adores Sri Radha, worshipping Her toenails with the lamp of every breath she takes. Amongst Visakha’s many skills, she especially excels at witty talks and joking words, which prove to he more eloquent than Sarasvati’s, and with which she easily defeats even Krsna in verbal duels.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami thinks, “Since Radha-kunda would not reveal Sri Radha to me, I shall pray to Visakha. She is always by Sri Radha’s side, and so my mistress will also hear my appeal. Moreover, because they are so much alike, speaking to her is like speaking to Sri Radha Herself.”

All-cognisant, Visakha surely hears Dasa Gosvami’s plea and, like Radha-kunda, must have also encouraged him to he patient, saying, “Rati! You have waited so long. Just wait a little longer.”

To tell a starving man to wait for his meal will hardly reduce his hunger. Indeed, Visakha’s advising Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami to be patient actually increases his feelings of separation from Radha. But, with those increased feelings of separation flooding his heart, Dasa Gosvami feels transcendental bliss, the taste of which has no equal.

Nevertheless, his yearning for direct service is greater than his desire to enjoy bliss, and so he turns to his last hope for shelter, Sri Krsna.

**Verse 100**

*ha natha gokula-sudhakara su-prasanna-*  
*vaktraravinda madhura-smita he krpardra*  
*yatra tvaya viharate pranayaih priyarat*  
*tatraiva mam api naya priya-sevanaya*

**“O Lord! O nectar moon of Gokula who melts with compassion, whose cheerful lotus face smiles sweetly with self-satisfaction, wherever You go to enjoy loving pastimes with Your beloved, please take me there so that I can affectionately serve You.”**

Commentary: Does Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami see and hear Visakha-devi, Sri Krsna, and Srimati Radharani? Certainly! An advanced devotee like Dasa Gosvami sees the objects of his worship in one of two ways: as a manifestation (sphurti), or as a direct revelation (saksat-darsana). Lord Caitanya describes the former aspect of spiritual vision to Ramananda Raya as follows:

*sthavara-jangama dekhe, na dekhe tara murti*  
*sarvatra haya nija ista-deva-sphurti*

**“The maha-bhagavata, the advanced devotee, certainly sees everything mobile and immobile, but he does not exactly see their forms. Rather, everywhere he immediately sees manifest the form of the Supreme Lord.”**

In this way, the advanced devotee, by his own Krsna conscious perception, sees Krsna within everything and also sees everything in Krsna.

In contrast to the effort of the purified mind to see Krsna and His associates, revelation comes when divine beings disclose themselves or their potencies by their own merciful initiative. Depending on individual circumstances, this revelation is called saksat-darsana or avirbhava, hut in both cases it constitutes direct meeting as a consequence of the Lord’s own volition. These terms are described in relation to Caitanya Mahaprabhu:

*saksat-darsana, ara yogya-bhakta-jive*  
*'avesa' karaye kahan, kahan ‘avirbhave’*

**“The Lord delivered the fallen souls in some places by meeting them directly \[saksat-darsana\], in other places by empowering a pure devotee, and in still other places by appearing before someone Himself \[avirbhava\].”**

As he offers this heartfelt prayer, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami sees Syamasundara standing before him. Krsna is all-powerful. Nothing is impossible for Him. Yet Dasa Gosvami appeals to the Lord on the basis of the services he can render as Rati-manjari, indicating that Krsna will also be benefited by uniting Rati with Radha.

If Krsna were to ask, “Rati, why did you call Me?” Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami might answer, “I called to offer You my services for any pastime You might enjoy with Your beloved."

Although Krsna is fully aware of Rati’s skills, He enquires, “What services would you do?”

Dasa Gosvami replies, “O Lord! O my Natha! As the lover of my mistress, You are naturally my master, and I am Your servant. Thus, whatever You ask of me, that I will do."

“But all living entities are My servants," Krsna points out, “and most of them are also prepared to serve Me. What will you do that is unique?”

Emphasising his special services as a manjari, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami says, “Like a moon softened by its own rays of mercy, You shower the nectar of Your sweerly smiling lotus face all over Gokula. However, Your disposition and Your smile last only as long as Sri Radha showers the nectar of Her smile upon You. As Her attendant and Your maidservant, I will ensure that She remains favourably disposed towards You. That will be my unique contribution to Your pastimes."

“Pray, tell!” Krsna enquires with curiosity. “How will you keep Radhika pleased with Me?”

“I will chant Your glories to Her,” Dasa Gosvami replies, “ensure that She is always attracted to You, maintain a jovial atmosphere between You and Her, encourage both of You to reveal Your hearts to each other, and — ” the elderly sadhu falls silent.

Curious why Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has suddenly stopped speaking, Krsna prompts him, “And what else?”

Dasa Gosvami says softly, “I will conceal Your faults.” They both laugh, and then the acarya continues, “In addition to keeping Radharani submissive to You, I can offer my special services, like massaging Your feet and singing love songs.”

Now Krsna tests Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s fidelity to Radha by saying, “It seems that your request to Me is solely based on fulfilling your desire to serve your mistress. Do you have any desire to serve Me directly?"

Not one to be easily fooled, Dasa Gosvami replies, “O Govinda! My firm conviction is that the best way to serve You is to serve Your beloved. That faith of mine will never waver. Please know that I worship only Radha who has lotus-like eyes, I remember only Radha who has a sweetly smiling face, I speak only of Radha who melts with compassion. She is the only goal of my life, and I have no other.”

When Krsna sees Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s sincere and unwavering devotion to Sri Radha’s lotus feet, a devotion filled with boundless love, greater even than the love Krsna feels for His own devotees, Krsna embraces Dasa Gosvami, places His own garland around Raghunatha’s neck, and then disappears.

The names Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami uses to address Krsna — Natha (“Lord”), Gokula-sudhakara (“nectar moon of Gokula”), Suprasanna-vaktraravinda-madhura-smita (“one whose cheerful lotus face smiles sweetly with self-satisfaction”), and Krpardra (“one who melts with compassion") — are very wonderful. Amongst other things, they invoke the Gopala-gayatri mantra and suggest this alternative reading to the verse:

**“O Lord (Krsna), who showers nectar on the cows and senses (Govinda), and whose satisfied, smiling lotus face reveals amorous attraction to the gopis (Gopijanavallabha), since You have accepted a body that constantly melts under the influence of Radha’s mercy (Caitanya Mahaprabhu) in order to personally taste the nectar of service to Her, is it difficult to understand why I also want to serve Srimati Radharani as the two of You enjoy loving pastimes throughout the forests of Vraja?”**

**Verse 101**

*laksmir yad-anghri-kamalasya nakhancalasya*  
*saundarya-bindum api narhati labdhum ise*  
*sa tvam vidhasyasi na cen mama netra-danam*  
*kim jivitena mama duhkha-davagnidena*

**“O Goddess — a drop of the beauty from the tip of whose lotus feet shames the splendour of the goddess of fortune—if You do not give charity to my eyes, then what is the use of my life, ablaze with a great forest fire of sufferings?”**

Commentary: Has Krsna gone to bring Srimati Radharani, or has He disappeared, only to increase Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s longing? The acarya cannot say. If he is already burning in the midst of a great conflagration, what is to be gained by pouring more fuel on it? Instead, those who are merciful will extinguish such a blaze. Because the person who is the cause of Dasa Gosvami’s suffering can just as easily end it, the author now turns to his beloved, Radha.

Radharani’s unique loveliness is a reflection of two things: Her unrivalled love for Krsna and Krsna’s own peerless beauty, krsna-sobha dekhi’ gopira sobha badhe tata: “The more the gopis see Lord Krsna’s beauty, the more their beauty increases.” And since Krsna’s beauty and sweetness by far outshine that of Lord Narayana, the husband of the goddess of fortune, it is only natural that Radha’s beauty puts to shame the beauty of Laksmi-devi.

And Dasa Gosvami’s incomparably beautiful mistress, as mentioned in the previous verse, melts with compassion. Here Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami is asking beautiful Radha to take pity on his miserable condition. He says:

“Isa! O mistress! As You are an ocean of beauty, You are also an ocean of mercy. Since it is You who empower Your representatives to extinguish the blazing fire of material existence, won’t You kindly extinguish the blazing fire of separation that is consuming me? You alone have the power to do so.”

Hearing Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s appeal, Srimati Radharani might say, “Rati! Tell Me what you want.”

His voice weak with sorrow, Dasa Gosvami replies: “O Goddess! Why do You hide Yourself from me? I am already a blind old man. Why make me blinder by not letting me see Your form of beauty. Please be kind and give that charity to my eyes.”

Radha replies, “You are a renunciate who lives by begging alms, and I am a princess bound by duty to give charity. Surely I must also give charity to you.”

Dissatisfied by the promise of future compensation, Dasa Gosvami responds, “I have waited until I can wait no more. If You want me to wait longer, then better let me die. Don’t keep me in a state of perpetual misery in which I can neither see nor serve You. Najivami tvaya vina: I cannot live without You.”

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s inability to live in separation from Srimati Radharani is a characteristic of pure love spoken of by Caitanya Mahaprabhu:

*kaitava-rahitam prema na hi bhavati manuse loke*  
*yadi bhavati kasya viraha virahe saty api ko jivati*

**“Love of Godhead, devoid of cheating propensities, is not possible within this material world. If there is such a love, there cannot be separation, for if there is separation, how can one live?”**

Here Caitanya Mahaprabhu is speaking in the mood of Srimati Radharani. He frankly confesses that continuing to live in the absence of Krsna indicates an absence of pure love for the Lord.

Furthermore, to Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya, Caitanya Mahaprabhu says:

*na prema-gandho 'sti darapi me harau*  
*krandami saubhagya-bharam prakasitum*  
*vamsi-vilasy-anana-lokanam vina*  
*bibharmi yat prana-patangakan vrtha*

**“My dear friends, I have not the slightest tinge of love of Godhead within My heart. When you see Me crying in separation, I am just falsely exhibiting a demonstration of My great fortune. Indeed, not seeing the beautiful face of Krsna playing His flute, I continue to live My life like an insect, without purpose."**

Having already heard these words of the Lord through Svarupa Damodara while in Puri, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami says, “Devi! Do You think that I have no love for You?”Naturally, Sri Radha replies, “I never doubted your love for a moment.”

“Then?” Dasa Gosvami concludes, “How do You expect me to live by promises while You remain absent from me? It is better that I die.”

**Verse 102**

*asa-bharair amrta-sindhu-mayaih kathancit*  
*kalo mayati-gamitah kila sampratam hi*  
*tvam cet krpam mayi vidhasyasi naiva kim me*  
*pranair vrajena ca varoru bakairinapi*

**“O Varoru! Thus I somehow spent my time here aspiring after oceans of nectar. But if You are not merciful to me, then of what use are Krsna, living in Vraja, and even life itself?”**

Commentary: Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami now makes a startling disclosure. If he cannot see Srimati Radharani then he is as disinterested in Vrndavana — and even as disinterested in Krsna — as he is in living. Certainly this is a state of consciousness that cannot be imitated; nevertheless, devotees should be aware of it, and they should try to understand it. In tandem with verse 96, this verse defines the unwavering devotion of Gaudiya Vaisnavas who follow the amorous serving mood of Rupa-manjari.

When in the company of confidential disciples, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura would recite this verse. He would be overwhelmed with spiritual emotions and his complexion would turn pale. The acarya confided that the inner meaning of his name, Sri Varsabhanavi-devi-dayita Dasa, was disclosed in the last two lines of this verse: “O Radha! If you are not merciful to me, then of what use are Krsna, Vraja, and even lifeitself?”

Dasa Gosvami openly speaks his heart to Sri Radha: “O girl with beautiful thighs! O Varoru! Because the nature of Your ecstatic devotion is to generate hope (asa-bandhah), I have lived my life in the hope that You would accept me as Your maidservant and that someday I could enter into Your pastimes. That hope, and only that hope, has kept me alive.

“At first I struggled to no end with the hope of securing Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s mercy. Finally, by the grace of Lord Nityananda, I was successful. But my years as the Lord’s servant passed by like fleeting moments, and He and all His confidential companions departed from this world, leaving me behind.

“I decided to give up my life, and with that end in mind I came to Vraja. But Rupa and Sanatana gave me hope again. They said, ‘Be patient, Radhika is very merciful.’ But then they too departed from this world, leaving me alone. During those years You would sometimes appear and flood my heart with bliss but then disappear and break my heart to pieces. By remembering those moments of divine grace, I held on to the hope that one day You would embrace me and never let me go. But that day has not come.”

Seeing Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s torment, and hearing his plaintive appeal, Radha says, “Rati! You have been brave to keep faith despite so many reverses.”

Recalling how merciful Radha had been after the lost waist bells were again placed on Her hips, Dasa Gosvami replies, “O girl with beautiful thighs! Don’t think that it has been easy to live like this. At times I have thought, ‘If I were to give up hope of meeting my mistress, then I might be happy.’”

“You thought in that way?” Radha enquires.

Shaking his head, Dasa Gosvami replies, “Like the gopis who tried to follow the advice of Pingala by giving up all desires but could not, I also could not give up the hope of seeing You.”

Curious to know more, Radha asks, “Tell Me why?”

Dasa Gosvami answers, “All my life I have subsisted by chanting Your names and those of Your beloved. I have satiated my tortured tongue by constantly drinking the charming elixir made by mixing the delicious nectar of Your names with the wonderfully sweet condensed milk of Krsna’s names and then adding the fragrant ice of my love for You both.

“The constant chanting of the maha-mantra was like a stream of nectar that I thought would ultimately take me to the nectar ocean of Your company. Sadly, that has not happened. But at least the chanting of Your names has kept You in my heart, in my ears, and upon my tongue. At least the constant remembrance of You kept me from abandoning hope altogether.”

In an attempt to console Her devotee, Radha answers, “But Rati! Living in Vraja, My home, is a sign of My mercy. Is that not reward enough for your hope?”

With a small laugh of disbelief, Dasa Gosvami answers, “Devi! If without Your Rupa-manjari I see Vraja like an endless desert, Govardhana Hill a great python, and Radha-kunda the gaping mouth of a tiger, then without You, how do You think these places appear to me?”

Again Radha tries to console Her servant, “But Krsna, the shelter of all great souls, is constantly wandering about in Vraja.”

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami shrugs off Radharani’s proposal, “I worship Your Syama with my every breath, and I live only to serve Him. But for me, His worship and service can only be done through You. Please, try to understand: You are the soul of the body of my existence. No matter how many wonderful attributes that body may have, without You — its soul — my existence is meaningless. Therefore, Vraja and Krsna are equally meaningless without You.” Srimati Radharani is silent, and in that silence, which has become the greater part of Dasa Gosvami’s life and bhajana, he asks, “Will You be merciful to me now?” As tears flow down his wrinkled cheeks and his hands shake with age, the great saint whispers a prayer of his own composition:

*na muncec charana-yatam api dustam dayamayah*  
*ato gandharvike ha ha muncainam naiva tadrsam*

**“O Gandharvika! Those who are merciful never reject a surrendered soul even though he may have been very wicked; therefore, please don’t reject me.”**

Dasa Gosvami then adds, “I believe with all my heart that You are merciful. I will never give up hope that I will someday attain Your mercy.”

**Verse 103**

*tvam cet krpamayi krpam mayi duhkhitayam*  
*naivatanor atitaram kim iha pralapaih*  
*tvat-kunda-madhyam api tad-bahu-kalam eva*  
*samsevyamanam api kim nu karisyatiha*

**“O merciful girl! If You do not give Your great mercy to suffering me, then what will all these lamentations and this long-time service to Your lake have accomplished?”**

Commentary: Implied in this verse is the question, “Can someone made of mercy not be merciful?” The phrase krsna-mayi means “one whose within and without are Lord Krsna,” and krpa-mayi means “one whose within and without are mercy.” Not only is Srimati Radharani made of mercy but also She takes the first of Her three daily baths in the nectar of compassion. Therefore, it is assured that She must be kind to Dasa Gosvami.

A thread of hope — the hope that because Srimati Radharani is grace personified, She will be merciful — keeps Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami alive. And since he has staked his life on Radha’s mercy, he may as well request a lot of it (atitaram).

Rupa Gosvami writes about Krsna’s dispensation of mercy:

*pracinanam bhajanam atulam duskaram srnvato me*  
*nairyasena jvalati hrdayam bhakti-lesalasasya*  
*visva-dricim aghahara tavakarnya karunya-vicim*  
*asa-binduksitam idam upety antare hanta saityam*

**“I am very weak and lazy to do even the smallest devotional service, and so when I hear of the peerless and difficult-to-perform services carried out by the great devotees in ancient times, my heart burns with despair. O Lord, O killer of Aghasura, when I hear that the waves of Your mercy splash everyone from the demigod Brahma down to the most insignificant creature, then my heart becomes sprinkled with a cooling drop of hope.”**

Should Dasa Gosvami expect any less from Krsna’s most beloved?

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami’s lamentations seem to bring him repeatedly to the same doorstep and a door that Radha has yet to open. But with every tear, with every appeal, with every slowly passing day, he comes closer to the moment at which She will invite him everlastingly into Her life.

Now the acarya places a new lamentation before his mistress: if service to Radha-kunda leads to Radha, then why shouldn’t he be evidence of that truth?

Supporting himself with the stick of hope, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami asks, “Krpa-mayi! Will You he kind to me now?”

Radha may reply, "By My grace you already live by My lake, where I also reside, eternally. I am close by.”

Dasa Gosvami replies, “You are close, yet You keep Your distance. Nonetheless, I have served Your lake knowing it is dear to You, that it is, in fact, not different from You.”

Knowing what is on Her servant’s mind, Radha says, “Others also serve My lake.”

Now Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami makes his final appeal, “Devi! That is just my point! I was living at Laghmohana kunda when Your Sanatana told me to come live by Arista-kunda. He said that I wouldreceive Radhika’s grace. Thereafter, I excavated Your lake, planted gardens around it, built cottages for sadhus on its shores, and daily served those saintly persons. Moreover, I bathed thrice daily in Your lake, bowed down in scheduled measurements around it, offered worship to it, celebrated the day of its appearance, Bahulastami, and above all, I wrote about it for the benefit of all Vaisnavas. And day and night I cried for You—”

After stopping for a moment to emphasise his point, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami continues, “I am not boasting about my achievements. Rather, I mention these things on behalf of all the devotees who reside on the shores of Your lake — I am concerned for them. If service to Your lake does not lead to You, then how will they be inspired to stay here? They will think, ‘Dasa Gosvami has rendered so much service to Radha-kunda, but still he is unhappily crying for Radha, still he has not received Her mercy.’”

Srimati Radharani gazes at Her humble, devoted servant as he pleads with all the humility at his command.

“Tell me, Devi!” he asks, tears trickling from his eyes. “Is what Your Rupa wrote not true? When he says that ‘those who execute devotional service on the hanks of Radha-kunda are the most fortunate people in the universe,’ can it somehow be otherwise?
